#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH user_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    user_pseudo_id,
    -- Count pageviews per user
    COUNTIF(event_name = 'page_view') AS pageviews,
    -- Flag as purchaser if any purchase event exists
    LOGICAL_OR(event_name = 'purchase') AS is_purchaser
  FROM 
    `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_202012*`
  WHERE 
    -- Ensure we only include December 2020 data
    event_date BETWEEN '20201201' AND '20201231'
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
  GROUP BY 
    user_pseudo_id
)
SELECT 
  -- Average pageviews for purchasers
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser THEN pageviews ELSE NULL END) AS avg_pageviews_purchasers,
  -- Average pageviews for non-purchasers
  AVG(CASE WHEN NOT is_purchaser THEN pageviews ELSE NULL END) AS avg_pageviews_non_purchasers,
  -- Difference: purchasers minus non-purchasers
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser THEN pageviews ELSE NULL END) - 
  AVG(CASE WHEN NOT is_purchaser THEN pageviews ELSE NULL END) AS avg_difference
FROM 
  user_stats;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Define the end timestamp for January 7, 2021 23:59:59 UTC
WITH end_timestamp AS (
  SELECT UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-07 23:59:59 UTC')) AS end_ts
),
-- Compute start timestamps for 7-day and 2-day periods
periods AS (
  SELECT 
    end_ts,
    -- 7 days before end (including start of Jan 1)
    UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-01 00:00:00 UTC')) AS start_7day_ts,
    -- 2 days before end (including start of Jan 6)
    UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-06 00:00:00 UTC')) AS start_2day_ts
  FROM end_timestamp
),
-- Distinct users with positive engagement in the 7-day period
users_7day AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`, periods
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210101' AND '20210107'
    AND event_timestamp >= periods.start_7day_ts
    AND event_timestamp <= periods.end_ts
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS param
      WHERE param.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
        AND param.value.int_value > 0
    )
),
-- Distinct users with positive engagement in the 2-day period
users_2day AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`, periods
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210106' AND '20210107'
    AND event_timestamp >= periods.start_2day_ts
    AND event_timestamp <= periods.end_ts
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS param
      WHERE param.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
        AND param.value.int_value > 0
    )
)
-- Count users in 7-day period but not in 2-day period
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS distinct_users_count
FROM users_7day
WHERE user_pseudo_id NOT IN (SELECT user_pseudo_id FROM users_2day);
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Define exact timestamp boundaries in microseconds (UTC)
boundaries AS (
  SELECT
    UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-01 00:00:00+00')) AS period_7d_start_usec,
    UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-06 00:00:00+00')) AS period_2d_start_usec,
    UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP('2021-01-07 23:59:59+00')) AS period_end_usec
),

-- Users with positive engagement time in the 7-day period (Jan 1 - Jan 7)
users_in_7d AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(event_params) AS ep
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210101' AND '20210107'
    AND event_name = 'user_engagement'
    AND ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
    AND ep.value.int_value > 0
    AND event_timestamp >= (SELECT period_7d_start_usec FROM boundaries)
    AND event_timestamp <= (SELECT period_end_usec FROM boundaries)
),

-- Users with positive engagement time in the 2-day period (Jan 6 - Jan 7)
users_in_2d AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(event_params) AS ep
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210106' AND '20210107'
    AND event_name = 'user_engagement'
    AND ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
    AND ep.value.int_value > 0
    AND event_timestamp >= (SELECT period_2d_start_usec FROM boundaries)
    AND event_timestamp <= (SELECT period_end_usec FROM boundaries)
)

-- Count users who engaged in the 7-day window but NOT in the 2-day window
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_title') AS page_title,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_location
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210102`
  WHERE user_pseudo_id = '1402138.5184246691'
    AND event_name = 'page_view'
    AND event_date = '20210102'
),
categories AS (
  SELECT * FROM UNNEST([
    'accessories', 'apparel', 'brands', 'campus collection', 'drinkware',
    'electronics', 'google redesign', 'lifestyle', 'nest', 'new 2015 logo',
    'notebooks journals', 'office', 'shop by brand', 'small goods',
    'stationery', 'wearables'
  ]) AS category
)
SELECT
  event_timestamp,
  page_title,
  page_location,
  CASE
    -- Check for PDP: at least 5 segments, last segment has '+', and 4th/5th segment matches a category
    WHEN 
      ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) >= 5 
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) AS segment WITH OFFSET idx 
        WHERE idx IN (3, 4) 
          AND LOWER(REPLACE(segment, '+', ' ')) IN (SELECT category FROM categories)
      )
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) AS segment WITH OFFSET idx 
        WHERE idx = ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) - 1 
          AND segment LIKE '%+%'
      )
    THEN 'PDP'
    -- Check for PLP: at least 5 segments, no '+' in 4th/5th segments, and 4th/5th segment matches a category
    WHEN 
      ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) >= 5 
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) AS segment WITH OFFSET idx 
        WHERE idx IN (3, 4) 
          AND LOWER(REPLACE(segment, '+', ' ')) IN (SELECT category FROM categories)
      )
      AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(TRIM(page_location, '/'), '/')) AS segment WITH OFFSET idx 
        WHERE idx IN (3, 4) AND segment LIKE '%+%'
      )
    THEN 'PLP'
    -- Otherwise, keep the original page title
    ELSE page_title
  END AS adjusted_page_name
FROM events
ORDER BY event_timestamp;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH page_data AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_title') AS page_title,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_location
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210102`
  WHERE user_pseudo_id = '1402138.5184246691'
    AND event_name = 'page_view'
),
all_pages AS (
  SELECT
    page_title,
    page_location,
    SPLIT(page_location, '/') AS segments
  FROM page_data
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  CASE
    -- PDP criteria: >= 5 segments, last non-empty segment contains '+', 4th or 5th is a recognized category
    WHEN
      ARRAY_LENGTH(segments) >= 5
      AND (
        LOWER(segments[SAFE_OFFSET(3)]) IN ('accessories', 'apparel', 'brands', 'campus+collection', 'drinkware', 'electronics', 'google+redesign', 'lifestyle', 'nest', 'new+2015+logo', 'notebooks+journals', 'office', 'shop+by+brand', 'small+goods', 'stationery', 'wearables')
        OR
        LOWER(segments[SAFE_OFFSET(4)]) IN ('accessories', 'apparel', 'brands', 'campus+collection', 'drinkware', 'electronics', 'google+redesign', 'lifestyle', 'nest', 'new+2015+logo', 'notebooks+journals', 'office', 'shop+by+brand', 'small+goods', 'stationery', 'wearables')
      )
      AND (SELECT elem FROM UNNEST(segments) AS elem WITH OFFSET WHERE elem != '' ORDER BY OFFSET DESC LIMIT 1) LIKE '%+%'
    THEN 'PDP'
    -- PLP criteria: >= 5 segments, neither 4th nor 5th contains '+', 4th or 5th is a recognized category
    WHEN
      ARRAY_LENGTH(segments) >= 5
      AND (
        LOWER(segments[SAFE_OFFSET(3)]) IN ('accessories', 'apparel', 'brands', 'campus+collection', 'drinkware', 'electronics', 'google+redesign', 'lifestyle', 'nest', 'new+2015+logo', 'notebooks+journals', 'office', 'shop+by+brand', 'small+goods', 'stationery', 'wearables')
        OR
        LOWER(segments[SAFE_OFFSET(4)]) IN ('accessories', 'apparel', 'brands', 'campus+collection', 'drinkware', 'electronics', 'google+redesign', 'lifestyle', 'nest', 'new+2015+logo', 'notebooks+journals', 'office', 'shop+by+brand', 'small+goods', 'stationery', 'wearables')
      )
      AND (segments[SAFE_OFFSET(3)] NOT LIKE '%+%' OR segments[SAFE_OFFSET(3)] IS NULL)
      AND (segments[SAFE_OFFSET(4)] NOT LIKE '%+%' OR segments[SAFE_OFFSET(4)] IS NULL)
    THEN 'PLP'
    -- Keep the original page name for pages that don't match either classification
    ELSE COALESCE(page_title, page_location, '(no page info)')
  END AS page_name
FROM all_pages
ORDER BY page_name;
```
</details>

**Question**: In January 2017, among visitors whose campaign name contains 'Data Share' and who accessed any page starting with '/home', which page did they most commonly visit next, and what is the maximum time (in seconds) they spent on the '/home' page before moving on?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|:-------------------------------------------------|-------------------:|

</details>

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| most_common_next_page                            |   visit_count |   max_time_on_home_seconds |
|:-------------------------------------------------|--------------:|---------------------------:|
| /google+redesign/apparel/men++s/men++s+outerwear |            75 |                    1785.27 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH home_page_hits AS (
  -- Step 1: Filter sessions from January 2017 with 'Data Share' campaign
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    date,
    hit.hitNumber,
    hit.time AS hit_time_ms,
    hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
    -- Get next page and its time using LEAD window function
    LEAD(hit.page.pagePath) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId 
      ORDER BY hit.hitNumber
    ) AS next_page_path,
    LEAD(hit.time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId 
      ORDER BY hit.hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time_ms
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
    UNNEST(hits) AS hit
  WHERE
    -- Filter for January 2017 using table suffix
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    -- Campaign name contains 'Data Share' (case-insensitive)
    AND LOWER(trafficSource.campaign) LIKE '%data share%'
    -- Only include PAGE type hits
    AND hit.type = 'PAGE'
),

-- Step 2: Filter for '/home' page hits that have a next page
home_to_next AS (
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    date,
    page_path,
    next_page_path,
    -- Calculate time on '/home' page in seconds
    -- Convert milliseconds to seconds and round to 4 decimal places
    ROUND((next_hit_time_ms - hit_time_ms) / 1000.0, 4) AS time_on_home_seconds
  FROM home_page_hits
  WHERE
    -- Current page starts with '/home'
    page_path LIKE '/home%'
    -- Ensure there is a next page (not the last hit in session)
    AND next_page_path IS NOT NULL
    -- Ensure next page is different from current page
    AND next_page_path != page_path
    -- Valid time difference (positive)
    AND next_hit_time_ms > hit_time_ms
),

-- Step 3: Calculate statistics
next_page_stats AS (
  SELECT
    next_page_path,
    COUNT(*) AS visit_count,
    MAX(time_on_home_seconds) AS max_time_on_home_seconds
  FROM home_to_next
  GROUP BY next_page_path
)

-- Step 4: Get the most common next page and overall maximum time
SELECT
  next_page_path AS most_common_next_page,
  visit_count,
  max_time_on_home_seconds
FROM next_page_stats
WHERE visit_count = (SELECT MAX(visit_count) FROM next_page_stats)
ORDER BY next_page_path
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH january_sessions AS (
  -- Step 1: Get all January 2017 sessions with campaign containing 'Data Share'
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    visitStartTime,
    trafficSource.campaign AS campaign,
    hits
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_2017*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    AND LOWER(trafficSource.campaign) LIKE LOWER('%Data Share%')
),
-- Step 2: Unnest hits and use LEAD to find the next page in each session
hit_sequences AS (
  SELECT
    s.fullVisitorId,
    s.visitId,
    h.hitNumber,
    h.time AS hit_time_ms,
    h.page.pagePath AS current_page,
    LEAD(h.page.pagePath) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId
      ORDER BY h.hitNumber
    ) AS next_page,
    LEAD(h.time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId
      ORDER BY h.hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time_ms
  FROM january_sessions s
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
  WHERE h.type = 'PAGE'  -- Only consider page hits
)
-- Step 3: Filter for '/home' pages, find most common next page and max time
SELECT
  next_page AS most_common_next_page,
  ROUND(MAX((next_hit_time_ms - hit_time_ms) / 1000.0), 4) AS max_time_on_home_seconds
FROM hit_sequences
WHERE current_page LIKE '/home%'
  AND next_page IS NOT NULL  -- Ensure there was a subsequent page
GROUP BY next_page
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH youtube_buyers AS (
  -- Step 1: Identify all visitors who bought YouTube products in July 2017
  SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(hits) AS hit,
           UNNEST(hit.product) AS product
      WHERE hit.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'  -- Completed purchase
        AND LOWER(product.v2ProductName) LIKE '%youtube%'
        AND product.productQuantity IS NOT NULL
        AND product.productQuantity > 0
    )
),

product_purchases AS (
  -- Step 2: Aggregate all non-YouTube products purchased by YouTube buyers
  SELECT 
    product.v2ProductName AS product_name,
    SUM(product.productQuantity) AS total_quantity
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`,
    UNNEST(hits) AS hit,
    UNNEST(hit.product) AS product
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
    AND hit.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'  -- Completed purchase
    AND fullVisitorId IN (SELECT fullVisitorId FROM youtube_buyers)
    AND LOWER(product.v2ProductName) NOT LIKE '%youtube%'
    AND product.productQuantity IS NOT NULL
    AND product.productQuantity > 0
  GROUP BY product.v2ProductName
)

-- Step 3: Find the product with highest total quantity
SELECT 
  product_name,
  total_quantity
FROM product_purchases
WHERE total_quantity = (
  SELECT MAX(total_quantity) 
  FROM product_purchases
)
ORDER BY product_name
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

  youtube_buyers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`,
         UNNEST(hits) AS h,
         UNNEST(h.product) AS p
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
      AND h.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'
      AND p.productQuantity > 0
      AND LOWER(p.v2ProductName) LIKE '%youtube%'
  ),
  -- Step 2: Get all purchases by those visitors, excluding products containing 'YouTube'

           p.productQuantity AS qty
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`,

      AND h.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'

      AND fullVisitorId IN (SELECT fullVisitorId FROM youtube_buyers)
      AND LOWER(p.v2ProductName) NOT LIKE '%youtube%'

-- Step 3: Find the product with the highest total quantity purchased

FROM non_youtube_purchases
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Generate all months from 2008-01 to 2022-12
"monthly_series" AS (
    SELECT 
        DATEADD('month', ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY NULL) - 1, '2008-01-01'::DATE) AS "month_start"
    FROM 
        TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 180)) -- 15 years * 12 months = 180
),
-- Extract and filter IoT publications
"iot_publications" AS (
    SELECT 
        p."publication_number",
        p."country_code",
        p."filing_date",
        -- Extract year-month from filing_date (convert NUMBER to DATE)
        DATE_TRUNC('month', 
            TRY_TO_DATE(CAST(p."filing_date" AS VARCHAR), 'YYYYMMDD')
        ) AS "filing_month"
    FROM 
        "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."abstract_localized") abs
    WHERE 
        p."country_code" = 'US'
        AND p."filing_date" BETWEEN 20080101 AND 20221231
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(CAST(p."filing_date" AS VARCHAR), 'YYYYMMDD') IS NOT NULL
        AND LOWER(abs.value:"text"::STRING) LIKE '%internet of things%'
),
-- Aggregate counts by month
"monthly_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        "filing_month",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "publication_number") AS "publication_count"
    FROM 
        "iot_publications"
    GROUP BY 
        "filing_month"
)
-- Final result with all months
SELECT 
    TO_CHAR(ms."month_start", 'YYYY-MM') AS "year_month",
    COALESCE(mc."publication_count", 0) AS "iot_publication_count"
FROM 
    "monthly_series" ms
LEFT JOIN 
    "monthly_counts" mc 
    ON ms."month_start" = mc."filing_month"
ORDER BY 
    ms."month_start";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Generate a series of months from 2008-01 to 2022-12
WITH RECURSIVE "month_series" AS (
    SELECT DATE_FROM_PARTS(2008, 1, 1) AS "month_start"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD('month', 1, "month_start")
    FROM "month_series"
    WHERE "month_start" < DATE_FROM_PARTS(2022, 12, 1)
),
-- Filter US patents with IoT in English abstract
"iot_patents" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p."publication_number"
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."abstract_localized") f
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND f.value:"language"::TEXT = 'en'
      AND LOWER(f.value:"text"::TEXT) LIKE '%internet of things%'
      AND p."filing_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND p."filing_date" >= 20080101
      AND p."filing_date" <= 20221231
),
-- Aggregate counts by year-month of filing date
"monthly_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_DATE(p."filing_date"::TEXT, 'YYYYMMDD')) AS "month",
        COUNT(DISTINCT p."publication_number") AS "cnt"
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p
    INNER JOIN "iot_patents" iot ON p."publication_number" = iot."publication_number"
    GROUP BY "month"
)
-- Left join with month series to include zero-filing months
SELECT 
    YEAR(m."month_start") AS "year",
    MONTH(m."month_start") AS "month",
    COALESCE(mc."cnt", 0) AS "num_publications"
FROM "month_series" m
LEFT JOIN "monthly_counts" mc ON m."month_start" = mc."month"
ORDER BY m."month_start";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH canadian_patents AS (
    SELECT 
        "publication_date",
        "inventor"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE "country_code" = 'CA'
        AND "publication_date" >= 19600101 
        AND "publication_date" <= 20201231
        AND "inventor" IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_NUMBER(SUBSTRING(CAST("publication_date" AS VARCHAR), 1, 4)) IS NOT NULL
),
valid_patents AS (
    SELECT 
        "publication_date",
        CASE 
            WHEN IS_ARRAY("inventor") THEN ARRAY_SIZE("inventor")
            ELSE 0 
        END AS "inventor_count"
    FROM canadian_patents
    WHERE CASE 
            WHEN IS_ARRAY("inventor") THEN ARRAY_SIZE("inventor")
            ELSE 0 
          END > 0
),
patents_with_year AS (
    SELECT 
        "inventor_count",
        TRY_TO_NUMBER(SUBSTRING(CAST("publication_date" AS VARCHAR), 1, 4)) AS "publication_year"
    FROM valid_patents
    WHERE "publication_year" BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020
),
patents_with_interval AS (
    SELECT 
        "inventor_count",
        "publication_year",
        FLOOR(("publication_year" - 1960) / 5) * 5 + 1960 AS "interval_start_year"
    FROM patents_with_year
)
SELECT 
    CONCAT(
        CAST("interval_start_year" AS VARCHAR),
        '-',
        CAST("interval_start_year" + 4 AS VARCHAR)
    ) AS "five_year_interval",
    ROUND(AVG("inventor_count"), 4) AS "avg_inventors_per_patent",
    COUNT(*) AS "total_patent_publications"
FROM patents_with_interval
GROUP BY 
    "interval_start_year"
ORDER BY 
    "interval_start_year";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH patent_data AS (
    -- Filter Canadian patents with at least one inventor and within year range
    SELECT 
        "publication_date",
        ARRAY_SIZE("inventor_harmonized") AS inventor_count
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE 
        "country_code" = 'CA'
        AND "inventor_harmonized" IS NOT NULL
        AND ARRAY_SIZE("inventor_harmonized") > 0
        AND FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020
),
periods AS (
    -- Assign each patent to a 5-year period based on publication year
    SELECT 
        inventor_count,
        FLOOR(FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) / 5) * 5 AS period_start,
        FLOOR(FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) / 5) * 5 + 4 AS period_end
    FROM patent_data
)
SELECT 
    CONCAT(period_start::VARCHAR, '-', period_end::VARCHAR) AS period_label,
    ROUND(AVG(inventor_count), 4) AS avg_inventors_per_patent,
    COUNT(*) AS total_patent_count
FROM periods
GROUP BY period_start, period_end
ORDER BY period_start;
```
</details>

### 8. sf_bq215 (DB: `PATENTS`)
**Question**: Which US patent (with a B2 kind code and a grant date between 2015 and 2018) has the highest originality score calculated as 1 - (the sum of squared occurrences of distinct 4-digit IPC codes in its backward citations divided by the square of the total occurrences of these 4-digit IPC codes)?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| publication_number   |   originality |
|:---------------------|--------------:|
| US-10105167-B2       |           0.5 |

**OR**

| publication_number   |   originality_score |
|:---------------------|--------------------:|
| US-9293644-B2        |            0.666667 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| publication_number   |   ORIGINALITY |
|:---------------------|--------------:|
| US-9121016-B2        |        0.8366 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH target_patents AS (
    -- Step 1: Filter US B2 patents granted between 2015 and 2018
    SELECT 
        "publication_number",
        "grant_date",
        "citation"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE "country_code" = 'US'
        AND "kind_code" = 'B2'
        AND "grant_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20181231
),
unnested_citations AS (
    -- Step 2: Extract backward citation publication numbers
    SELECT 
        tp."publication_number" AS target_pub,
        cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING AS cited_pub_num
    FROM target_patents tp,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => tp."citation") AS cit
    WHERE cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING IS NOT NULL
),
ipc_codes AS (
    -- Step 3: Get 4-digit IPC codes from each cited patent
    SELECT 
        uc.target_pub,
        LEFT(ipc_item.value:"code"::STRING, 4) AS ipc4
    FROM unnested_citations uc
    INNER JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" cited_pat 
        ON uc.cited_pub_num = cited_pat."publication_number"
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cited_pat."ipc") AS ipc_item
    WHERE ipc_item.value:"code"::STRING IS NOT NULL
        AND LEFT(ipc_item.value:"code"::STRING, 4) != ''
),
ipc_counts AS (
    -- Step 4: Count occurrences of each distinct 4-digit IPC code per target patent
    SELECT 
        target_pub,
        ipc4,
        COUNT(*) AS count_per_ipc
    FROM ipc_codes
    GROUP BY target_pub, ipc4
),
originality_scores AS (
    -- Step 5: Compute originality score for each target patent
    SELECT 
        target_pub,
        SUM(count_per_ipc) AS total_occurrences,
        SUM(count_per_ipc * count_per_ipc) AS sum_squares,
        -- Cast to FLOAT to avoid integer division
        1 - (SUM(count_per_ipc * count_per_ipc)::FLOAT / 
             (SUM(count_per_ipc) * SUM(count_per_ipc))::FLOAT) AS originality
    FROM ipc_counts
    GROUP BY target_pub
    HAVING SUM(count_per_ipc) > 0  -- Exclude patents with no valid IPC codes in citations
)
-- Step 6: Return the patent with the highest originality score
SELECT 
    target_pub AS "publication_number",
    ROUND(originality, 4) AS originality
FROM originality_scores
WHERE originality IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY originality DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query finds the US patent (kind_code = 'B2', grant_date between 2015 and 2018)
-- with the highest originality score, defined as:
-- Originality = 1 - Σ ( (count of occurrence of a 4-digit IPC code among backward citations) / total occurrences )^2
-- The score is rounded to 4 decimal places.

WITH
-- Step 1: US patents with B2 kind and grant date 2015-2018
target_pats AS (
    SELECT "publication_number",
           "citation"
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
    WHERE "country_code" = 'US'
      AND "kind_code" = 'B2'
      AND "grant_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20181231
),

-- Step 2: Flatten backward citations (each citation object should contain a "publication_number")
citations_flattened AS (
    SELECT tp."publication_number" AS patent_number,
           f.value:"publication_number"::STRING AS cited_pub
    FROM target_pats tp,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => tp."citation") f
    WHERE f.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 3: Join to the cited publications and flatten their IPC codes to get 4-digit IPC
cited_ipc AS (
    SELECT cf.patent_number,
           SUBSTR(ipc_u."code", 1, 4) AS ipc4
    FROM citations_flattened cf
    JOIN PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p2
        ON cf.cited_pub = p2."publication_number"
         , LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p2."ipc") ipc_u
    WHERE ipc_u."code" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 4: Compute total occurrences of IPC codes per patent
total_occurrences AS (
    SELECT patent_number,
           COUNT(*) AS total_occ
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY patent_number
),

-- Step 5: Compute count per distinct 4-digit IPC per patent
ipc_counts AS (
    SELECT patent_number,
           ipc4,
           COUNT(*) AS ipc_count
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY patent_number, ipc4
),

-- Step 6: Compute originality score
pat_originality AS (
    SELECT ic.patent_number,
           ROUND(
               1 - SUM(POWER(ic.ipc_count * 1.0 / tot.total_occ, 2)),
               4
           ) AS originality_score
    FROM ipc_counts ic
    JOIN total_occurrences tot
        ON ic.patent_number = tot.patent_number
    GROUP BY ic.patent_number, tot.total_occ
)

-- Step 7: Return the patent with the highest originality
SELECT patent_number,
       originality_score
FROM pat_originality
ORDER BY originality_score DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "families_jan_2015" AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_publication_date"
    FROM "PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE "family_id" IS NOT NULL 
        AND "publication_date" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "family_id"
    HAVING "earliest_publication_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20150131
),

"family_publications" AS (
    SELECT 
        f."family_id",
        f."earliest_publication_date",
        p."publication_number",
        p."country_code",
        p."cpc",
        p."ipc",
        p."citation"
    FROM "families_jan_2015" f
    JOIN "PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PUBLICATIONS" p
        ON f."family_id" = p."family_id"
),

"cpc_codes" AS (
    SELECT 
        fp."family_id",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT cpc_val.value:"code"::STRING, ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cpc_val.value:"code"::STRING) AS "cpc_codes"
    FROM "family_publications" fp,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."cpc") cpc_val
    WHERE cpc_val.value:"code"::STRING IS NOT NULL
        AND cpc_val.value:"code"::STRING != ''
    GROUP BY fp."family_id"
),

"ipc_codes" AS (
    SELECT 
        fp."family_id",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT ipc_val.value:"code"::STRING, ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ipc_val.value:"code"::STRING) AS "ipc_codes"
    FROM "family_publications" fp,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."ipc") ipc_val
    WHERE ipc_val.value:"code"::STRING IS NOT NULL
        AND ipc_val.value:"code"::STRING != ''
    GROUP BY fp."family_id"
),

"cited_publications" AS (
    SELECT 
        fp."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
        cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING AS "cited_publication_number"
    FROM "family_publications" fp,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."citation") cit
    WHERE cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING IS NOT NULL
        AND cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING != ''
),

"cited_families" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        cp."citing_family_id",
        p."family_id" AS "cited_family_id"
    FROM "cited_publications" cp
    JOIN "PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PUBLICATIONS" p
        ON cp."cited_publication_number" = p."publication_number"
    WHERE p."family_id" IS NOT NULL
        AND p."family_id" != cp."citing_family_id"
),

"citing_publications" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        p."publication_number" AS "citing_publication_number",
        fp."family_id" AS "cited_family_id"
    FROM "PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PUBLICATIONS" p,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."citation") cit
    JOIN "family_publications" fp
        ON cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING = fp."publication_number"
    WHERE cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING IS NOT NULL
        AND cit.value:"publication_number"::STRING != ''
),

"citing_families" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        p."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
        cp."cited_family_id"
    FROM "citing_publications" cp
    JOIN "PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PATENTS_GOOGLE"."PUBLICATIONS" p
        ON cp."citing_publication_number" = p."publication_number"
    WHERE p."family_id" IS NOT NULL
        AND p."family_id" != cp."cited_family_id"
),

"aggregated_data" AS (
    SELECT 
        fp."family_id",
        MIN(fp."earliest_publication_date") AS "earliest_publication_date",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT fp."publication_number", ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY fp."publication_number") AS "publication_numbers",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT fp."country_code", ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY fp."country_code") AS "country_codes",
        COALESCE(cc."cpc_codes", '') AS "cpc_codes",
        COALESCE(ic."ipc_codes", '') AS "ipc_codes",
        COALESCE(LISTAGG(DISTINCT cf."cited_family_id", ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cf."cited_family_id"), '') AS "cited_families",
        COALESCE(LISTAGG(DISTINCT cif."citing_family_id", ',') 
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cif."citing_family_id"), '') AS "citing_families"
    FROM "family_publications" fp
    LEFT JOIN "cpc_codes" cc ON fp."family_id" = cc."family_id"
    LEFT JOIN "ipc_codes" ic ON fp."family_id" = ic."family_id"
    LEFT JOIN "cited_families" cf ON fp."family_id" = cf."citing_family_id"
    LEFT JOIN "citing_families" cif ON fp."family_id" = cif."cited_family_id"
    GROUP BY 
        fp."family_id",
        cc."cpc_codes",
        ic."ipc_codes"
)

SELECT 
    "family_id",
    "earliest_publication_date",
    "publication_numbers",
    "country_codes",
    "cpc_codes",
    "ipc_codes",
    "cited_families",
    "citing_families"
FROM "aggregated_data"
ORDER BY "family_id";
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Find families whose earliest publication date is in January 2015
    families_of_interest AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_date"
        FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS
        GROUP BY "family_id"
        HAVING MIN("publication_date") >= 20150101
           AND MIN("publication_date") <= 20150131
    ),

    -- Step 2: All publications belonging to those families
    family_pubs AS (
        SELECT
            p."family_id",
            p."publication_date",
            p."publication_number",
            p."country_code",
            p."cpc",
            p."ipc",
            p."citation"
        FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS p
        INNER JOIN families_of_interest f
            ON p."family_id" = f."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 3: Earliest publication date per family
    earliest_dates AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_date"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 4: Distinct publication numbers, comma-separated, sorted alphabetically
    pub_numbers AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT "publication_number", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "publication_number") AS "publication_numbers"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 5: Distinct country codes, comma-separated, sorted alphabetically
    country_codes AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT "country_code", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "country_code") AS "country_codes"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 6: Distinct CPC codes extracted from the VARIANT array
    cpc_codes AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT c.value:"code"::VARCHAR, ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY c.value:"code"::VARCHAR) AS "cpc_codes"
        FROM family_pubs fp,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."cpc") c
        WHERE c.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
          AND c.value:"code"::VARCHAR != ''
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 7: Distinct IPC codes extracted from the VARIANT array
    ipc_codes AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT i.value:"code"::VARCHAR, ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY i.value:"code"::VARCHAR) AS "ipc_codes"
        FROM family_pubs fp,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."ipc") i
        WHERE i.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
          AND i.value:"code"::VARCHAR != ''
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 8: Families CITED BY this publication family
    -- (Extract publication_numbers from citation list, then find their family_ids)
    cited_family_ids AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT cited_p."family_id", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cited_p."family_id") AS "cited_family_ids"
        FROM family_pubs fp,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."citation") cit
        LEFT JOIN PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS cited_p
            ON cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR = cited_p."publication_number"
        WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
          AND cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR != ''
          AND cited_p."family_id" IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 9: Families that CITE this publication family
    -- (Find other publications whose citation list contains this family's publication_numbers)
    citing_family_ids AS (
        SELECT
            fpn."family_id" AS "cited_family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT flat_cit."citing_family_id", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY flat_cit."citing_family_id") AS "citing_family_ids"
        FROM (
            SELECT DISTINCT "family_id", "publication_number"
            FROM family_pubs
        ) fpn
        INNER JOIN (
            SELECT
                other."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
                cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR AS "cited_pub_number"
            FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS other,
                 LATERAL FLATTEN(input => other."citation") cit
            WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
              AND cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR != ''
        ) flat_cit
            ON flat_cit."cited_pub_number" = fpn."publication_number"
        GROUP BY fpn."family_id"
    )

-- Final SELECT: Combine all pieces per family
SELECT
    ed."family_id",
    ed."earliest_date",
    pn."publication_numbers",
    cc."country_codes",
    COALESCE(cpc."cpc_codes", '') AS "cpc_codes",
    COALESCE(ipc."ipc_codes", '') AS "ipc_codes",
    COALESCE(citing."citing_family_ids", '') AS "citing_family_ids",
    COALESCE(cited."cited_family_ids", '') AS "cited_family_ids"
FROM earliest_dates ed
INNER JOIN families_of_interest foi
    ON ed."family_id" = foi."family_id"
LEFT JOIN pub_numbers pn
    ON ed."family_id" = pn."family_id"
LEFT JOIN country_codes cc
    ON ed."family_id" = cc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN cpc_codes cpc
    ON ed."family_id" = cpc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN ipc_codes ipc
    ON ed."family_id" = ipc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN citing_family_ids citing
    ON ed."family_id" = citing."cited_family_id"
LEFT JOIN cited_family_ids cited
    ON ed."family_id" = cited."citing_family_id"
ORDER BY ed."family_id";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH combined_claims AS (
    SELECT 
        "word_ct",
        "ind_flg",
        "appl_id",
        "claim_no",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS
    WHERE "ind_flg" = '1'
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        "word_ct",
        "ind_flg",
        "appl_id",
        "claim_no",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS_2014
    WHERE "ind_flg" = '1'
),
combined_match AS (
    SELECT 
        "publication_number",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        "publication_number",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH_2014
),
claims_with_pubs AS (
    SELECT 
        cc."word_ct",
        cc."appl_id",
        cc."claim_no",
        cc."pat_no",
        cm."publication_number"
    FROM combined_claims cc
    JOIN combined_match cm ON cc."pat_no" = cm."pat_no"
),
-- Assumption: PATENTS_USPTO.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS contains columns:
-- publication_number, application_number, publication_date
earliest_publications AS (
    SELECT 
        "publication_number",
        "application_number",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "application_number"
            ORDER BY "publication_date" ASC   -- Earliest publication first
        ) AS pub_rank
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
    WHERE "application_number" IS NOT NULL
      AND "publication_number" IS NOT NULL
),
filtered_claims AS (
    SELECT 
        cp."word_ct",
        cp."appl_id",
        cp."claim_no",
        cp."publication_number",
        ep."application_number"
    FROM claims_with_pubs cp
    INNER JOIN earliest_publications ep 
        ON cp."publication_number" = ep."publication_number"
        AND ep.pub_rank = 1   -- Only the earliest publication per application
)
SELECT 
    fc."publication_number" AS "earliest_publication_number",
    fc."appl_id" AS "application_number",   -- or use fc."application_number" from publications if preferred
    fc."claim_no" AS "claim_number",
    fc."word_ct" AS "word_count"
FROM filtered_claims fc
ORDER BY CAST(fc."word_ct" AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Union all independent claims from claims stats tables
claims_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "pat_no",
        "appl_id",
        "claim_no",
        "word_ct"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS
    WHERE "ind_flg" = '1'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        "pat_no",
        "appl_id",
        "claim_no",
        "word_ct"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS_2014
    WHERE "ind_flg" = '1'
),

-- Step 2: Union all match tables to get publication_number for each patent number
match_tables AS (
    SELECT
        "publication_number",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        "publication_number",
        "pat_no"
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH_2014
),

-- Step 3: Join claims stats with match tables on pat_no to get publication numbers
claims_with_pub AS (
    SELECT
        cs."appl_id",
        cs."claim_no",
        cs."word_ct",
        m."publication_number"
    FROM claims_stats cs
    INNER JOIN match_tables m
        ON cs."pat_no" = m."pat_no"
),

-- Step 4: From PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS, for each application_number,
--         find the earliest publication (smallest publication_date)
ranked_publications AS (
    SELECT
        p."publication_number",
        p."application_number",
        p."publication_date",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY p."application_number"
            ORDER BY p."publication_date" ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM PATENTS_USPTO.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p
),

-- Step 5: Keep only the earliest publication per application
earliest_pubs AS (
    SELECT
        "publication_number",
        "application_number"
    FROM ranked_publications
    WHERE rn = 1
)

-- Step 6: Final select - earliest publications with claim details,
--         ordered by highest word count, limited to top 100
SELECT
    ep."publication_number",
    ep."application_number",
    cp."claim_no",
    cp."word_ct"
FROM claims_with_pub cp
INNER JOIN earliest_pubs ep
    ON cp."publication_number" = ep."publication_number"
ORDER BY CAST(cp."word_ct" AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH us_patents_with_app_date AS (
    SELECT 
        p."id" AS "patent_id",
        p."title",
        a."date" AS "application_date"
    FROM "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."PATENT" p
    INNER JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."APPLICATION" a
        ON p."id" = a."patent_id"
    WHERE p."country" = 'US'
),
patents_with_cpc AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        up."patent_id",
        up."title",
        up."application_date"
    FROM us_patents_with_app_date up
    INNER JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."CPC_CURRENT" cpc
        ON up."patent_id" = cpc."patent_id"
    WHERE cpc."subsection_id" IN ('C08', 'C07', 'C12')
),
backward_citations_1yr AS (
    SELECT 
        p."patent_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cit."citation_id") AS "backward_citation_count"
    FROM patents_with_cpc p
    INNER JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."USPATENTCITATION" cit
        ON p."patent_id" = cit."patent_id"
    WHERE 
        TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") >= DATEADD(year, -1, TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date"))
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") <= TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date")
    GROUP BY p."patent_id", p."title", p."application_date"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cit."citation_id") > 0
),
forward_citations_1yr AS (
    SELECT 
        p."patent_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cit."patent_id") AS "forward_citation_count_1yr"
    FROM patents_with_cpc p
    INNER JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."USPATENTCITATION" cit
        ON p."patent_id" = cit."citation_id"
    WHERE 
        TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") >= TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date")
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") <= DATEADD(year, 1, TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date"))
    GROUP BY p."patent_id", p."title", p."application_date"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cit."patent_id") > 0
),
forward_citations_3yr AS (
    SELECT 
        p."patent_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cit."patent_id") AS "forward_citation_count_3yr"
    FROM patents_with_cpc p
    INNER JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."USPATENTCITATION" cit
        ON p."patent_id" = cit."citation_id"
    WHERE 
        TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date") IS NOT NULL
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") >= TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date")
        AND TRY_TO_DATE(cit."date") <= DATEADD(year, 3, TRY_TO_DATE(p."application_date"))
    GROUP BY p."patent_id", p."title", p."application_date"
)
SELECT 
    p."patent_id",
    p."title",
    p."application_date",
    bc."backward_citation_count",
    fc1."forward_citation_count_1yr",
    fc3."forward_citation_count_3yr"
FROM patents_with_cpc p
INNER JOIN backward_citations_1yr bc
    ON p."patent_id" = bc."patent_id"
INNER JOIN forward_citations_1yr fc1
    ON p."patent_id" = fc1."patent_id"
LEFT JOIN forward_citations_3yr fc3
    ON p."patent_id" = fc3."patent_id"
ORDER BY bc."backward_citation_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Get U.S. patents with their application dates
WITH patent_app AS (
    SELECT 
        p."id" AS patent_id,
        p."country",
        a."date"::DATE AS app_date
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT p
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION a 
        ON p."id" = a."patent_id"
    WHERE p."country" = 'US'
),

-- CTE: Count backward citations within 1 year before application date
backward_citations AS (
    SELECT 
        uc."patent_id" AS citing_patent_id,
        COUNT(*) AS backward_count
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc
    JOIN patent_app pa 
        ON uc."patent_id" = pa.patent_id
    WHERE uc."date"::DATE >= DATEADD(day, -365, pa.app_date)
      AND uc."date"::DATE < pa.app_date
    GROUP BY uc."patent_id"
),

-- CTE: Count forward citations (within 1 year and within 3 years after application date)
forward_citations AS (
    SELECT 
        uc."citation_id" AS cited_patent_id,
        COUNT(CASE 
            WHEN uc."date"::DATE >= pa.app_date 
             AND uc."date"::DATE < DATEADD(day, 365, pa.app_date) 
            THEN 1 
        END) AS forward_1yr_count,
        COUNT(CASE 
            WHEN uc."date"::DATE >= pa.app_date 
             AND uc."date"::DATE < DATEADD(day, 365*3, pa.app_date) 
            THEN 1 
        END) AS forward_3yr_count
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc
    JOIN patent_app pa 
        ON uc."citation_id" = pa.patent_id
    GROUP BY uc."citation_id"
),

-- CTE: Patents that have at least one CPC classification (specific CPC categories)
cpc_patents AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "patent_id"
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.CPC_CURRENT
)

-- Final query: Combine all conditions and return the patent with most backward citations
SELECT 
    pa.patent_id,
    bc.backward_count,
    fc.forward_3yr_count AS forward_citations_within_3_years
FROM patent_app pa
JOIN backward_citations bc 
    ON pa.patent_id = bc.citing_patent_id
JOIN forward_citations fc 
    ON pa.patent_id = fc.cited_patent_id
JOIN cpc_patents cpc 
    ON pa.patent_id = cpc.patent_id
WHERE bc.backward_count > 0 
  AND fc.forward_1yr_count > 0
ORDER BY bc.backward_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
        sf."path",

        sc."content"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES" AS sf
    INNER JOIN "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_CONTENTS" AS sc
        ON sf."repo_name" = sc."sample_repo_name"
        AND sf."path" = sc."sample_path"
        AND sf."ref" = sc."sample_ref"
    WHERE sc."content" IS NOT NULL 
        AND TRIM(sc."content") != ''
        AND sc."content" != 'None'
        AND sc."binary" = FALSE
),

file_extensions AS (
    -- Extract file extension from path, handle files without extensions
    SELECT 
        "repo_name",
        "path",
        "ref",
        "content",
        CASE 
            WHEN "path" LIKE '%Dockerfile%' THEN 'dockerfile'
            WHEN "path" LIKE '%.%' THEN LOWER(SPLIT_PART("path", '.', -1))
            ELSE NULL
        END AS "extension"
    FROM joined_files
),

language_mapping AS (
    -- Create mapping of extensions to languages
    SELECT 'Assembly' AS "language", 'asm' AS "extension" UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Assembly', 'nasm' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'C', 'c' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'C', 'h' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'C#', 'cs' UNION ALL

    SELECT 'Elixir', 'exs' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Erlang', 'erl' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Go', 'go' UNION ALL

    SELECT 'HTML', 'html' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'HTML', 'htm' UNION ALL

    SELECT 'JSON', 'json' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Java', 'java' UNION ALL

    SELECT 'JavaScript', 'cjs' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Julia', 'jl' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin', 'kt' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin', 'ktm' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin', 'kts' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Lua', 'lua' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'MATLAB', 'matlab' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'MATLAB', 'm' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown', 'md' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown', 'markdown' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown', 'mdown' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PHP', 'php' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell', 'ps1' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell', 'psd1' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell', 'psm1' UNION ALL

),

mapped_files AS (
    -- Map file extensions to languages
    SELECT 
        fe."repo_name",
        fe."path",
        fe."ref",
        lm."language"
    FROM file_extensions fe
    INNER JOIN language_mapping lm
        ON fe."extension" = lm."extension"
    WHERE fe."extension" IS NOT NULL
)

-- Final aggregation to get top 10 languages
SELECT 
    "language",

FROM mapped_files
```

```sql
WITH

language_map AS (

    SELECT 'Assembly'     , '.nasm'               UNION ALL

    SELECT 'Groovy'       , '.groovy'             UNION ALL

    SELECT 'HTML'         , '.htm'                UNION ALL

    SELECT 'JavaScript'   , '.cjs'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Julia'        , '.jl'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin'       , '.kt'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin'       , '.ktm'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kotlin'       , '.kts'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Lua'          , '.lua'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'MATLAB'       , '.matlab'             UNION ALL
    SELECT 'MATLAB'       , '.m'                  UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown'     , '.md'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown'     , '.markdown'           UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Markdown'     , '.mdown'              UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PHP'          , '.php'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell'   , '.ps1'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell'   , '.psd1'               UNION ALL
    SELECT 'PowerShell'   , '.psm1'               UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Python'       , '.py'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'R'            , '.r'                  UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Ruby'         , '.rb'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Rust'         , '.rs'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'SCSS'         , '.scss'               UNION ALL
    SELECT 'SQL'          , '.sql'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Sass'         , '.sass'               UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Scala'        , '.scala'              UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Shell'        , '.sh'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Shell'        , '.bash'               UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Swift'        , '.swift'              UNION ALL
    SELECT 'TypeScript'   , '.ts'                 UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Vue'          , '.vue'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'XML'          , '.xml'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'YAML'         , '.yml'                UNION ALL
    SELECT 'YAML'         , '.yaml'
),

-- Special filenames that are not extensions (e.g., Dockerfile)
special_files AS (
    SELECT 'Dockerfile' AS "filename", 'Dockerfile' AS "language"
),

-- Base: join files with their content, keep only non‑empty content
file_content AS (
    SELECT
        f."repo_name",
        f."path",
        c."content"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES" f
    INNER JOIN "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_CONTENTS" c
        ON f."repo_name" = c."sample_repo_name"
        AND f."path" = c."sample_path"
    WHERE c."content" IS NOT NULL
      AND c."content" != ''
),

-- Extract the filename (last part of path) and the extension
file_info AS (
    SELECT
        fc."repo_name",
        fc."path",
        -- filname: everything after the last '/'
        SUBSTR(fc."path", LENGTH(fc."path") - POSITION('/' IN REVERSE(fc."path")) + 2) AS "filename",
        -- extension: lowercase and with dot, or empty if no dot
        LOWER(SUBSTR(fc."path", INSTR(REVERSE(fc."path"), '.') + 1)) AS "ext_lower"
    FROM file_content fc
),

-- Determine language for each file
file_language AS (
    SELECT
        fi."repo_name",
        fi."path",
        COALESCE(
            -- First check special filenames
            (SELECT sf."language" FROM special_files sf WHERE sf."filename" = fi."filename"),
            -- Then map by extension (prepend dot)
            (SELECT lm."language" FROM language_map lm WHERE '.' || fi."ext_lower" = lm."extension")
        ) AS "language"
    FROM file_info fi
    WHERE fi."ext_lower" IS NOT NULL   -- ensures we don't miss files with no extension (handled by special_files)
)

-- Final aggregation
SELECT
    fl."language",
    COUNT(*) AS "file_count"
FROM file_language fl
WHERE fl."language" IS NOT NULL   -- only recognized languages
GROUP BY fl."language"
ORDER BY "file_count" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH python_repos AS (
    -- Identify repositories with Python files from SAMPLE_FILES
    SELECT DISTINCT "repo_name"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES"
    WHERE LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py'
    
    UNION
    
    -- Also check SAMPLE_CONTENTS for Python files
    SELECT DISTINCT "sample_repo_name" AS "repo_name"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_CONTENTS"
    WHERE LOWER("sample_path") LIKE '%.py'
),
commits_2016 AS (
    -- Extract commits from 2016 for Python repositories
    SELECT 
        c."repo_name",
        -- Extract month from the committer date (date is in microseconds)
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":date::NUMBER / 1000000)) AS "commit_month",
        COUNT(*) AS "commit_count"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_COMMITS" c
    INNER JOIN python_repos p ON c."repo_name" = p."repo_name"
    WHERE 
        -- Filter for year 2016
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":date::NUMBER / 1000000)) = 2016
    GROUP BY 
        c."repo_name",
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":date::NUMBER / 1000000))
),
monthly_totals AS (
    -- Calculate total commits per month across all Python repos
    SELECT 
        "commit_month",
        SUM("commit_count") AS "total_commits"
    FROM commits_2016
    GROUP BY "commit_month"
),
all_months AS (
    -- Generate all 12 months of 2016 to ensure we include months with zero commits
    SELECT SEQ4() + 1 AS "month_num"
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 12))
)
-- Calculate the average monthly commits, including months with zero commits
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(mt."total_commits", 0)), 4) AS "avg_commits_per_month_2016"
FROM all_months am
LEFT JOIN monthly_totals mt ON am."month_num" = mt."commit_month";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql

    SELECT DISTINCT "repo_name"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES"
    -- The language column is a VARIANT containing an array of language names
    WHERE ARRAY_CONTAINS('Python'::VARIANT, "language")
)

-- Step 2: Count all commits in 2016 for those repositories and compute average per month
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) / 12.0, 4) AS "avg_commits_per_month"
FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_COMMITS" c
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM python_repos pr
    WHERE pr."repo_name" = c."repo_name"
)
-- Extract year from the committer's date (stored as microseconds)
  AND YEAR(TO_TIMESTAMP( (c."committer":"date")::NUMBER / 1000000 )) = 2016;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_files AS (
    SELECT 
        CASE 
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py' THEN '.py'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.c' THEN '.c'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.ipynb' THEN '.ipynb'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.java' THEN '.java'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.js' THEN '.js'
        END AS "file_extension",
        "path",
        -- Calculate directory depth: count of path segments minus 1 (for filename)
        ARRAY_SIZE(SPLIT("path", '/')) - 1 AS "directory_depth"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES"
    WHERE 
        (LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py' OR
         LOWER("path") LIKE '%.c' OR
         LOWER("path") LIKE '%.ipynb' OR
         LOWER("path") LIKE '%.java' OR
         LOWER("path") LIKE '%.js')
        AND "path" IS NOT NULL
),
deep_files AS (
    SELECT 
        "file_extension",
        "path"
    FROM filtered_files
    WHERE "directory_depth" > 10
),
counts AS (
    SELECT 
        "file_extension",
        COUNT(*) AS "file_count",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS "rnk"
    FROM deep_files
    GROUP BY "file_extension"
)
SELECT "file_extension", "file_count"
FROM counts
WHERE "rnk" = 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH file_depth AS (
    SELECT 
        "path",
        LOWER(SPLIT_PART("path", '.', -1)) AS "extension",
        LENGTH("path") - LENGTH(REPLACE("path", '/', '')) AS "directory_depth"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES"
    WHERE "path" LIKE '%.%'
      AND LOWER(SPLIT_PART("path", '.', -1)) IN ('py', 'c', 'ipynb', 'java', 'js')
)
SELECT 
    "extension",
    COUNT(*) AS "file_count"
FROM file_depth
WHERE "directory_depth" > 10
GROUP BY "extension"
ORDER BY "file_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH repo_primary_language AS (
    -- Get primary language for each repo with non-empty language data
    SELECT 
        l."repo_name",
        MAX(lang.value:"name"::STRING) AS "primary_language"
    FROM 
        "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES" l,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") lang
    WHERE 
        lang.value:"bytes"::NUMBER IS NOT NULL
        AND lang.value:"name"::STRING IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        l."repo_name"
),

pull_request_counts AS (
    -- Count PullRequestEvents per repo on Jan 18, 2023
    SELECT 
        d."repo":"name"::STRING AS "repo_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "pr_count"
    FROM 
        "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."DAY"."_20230118" d
    WHERE 
        d."type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
        AND d."repo":"name"::STRING IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        d."repo":"name"::STRING
)

-- Aggregate by language
SELECT 
    COALESCE(rpl."primary_language", 'Unknown') AS "primary_language",
    SUM(prc."pr_count") AS "total_pull_request_events"
FROM 
    pull_request_counts prc
LEFT JOIN 
    repo_primary_language rpl 
    ON prc."repo_name" = rpl."repo_name"
GROUP BY 
    rpl."primary_language"
HAVING 
    SUM(prc."pr_count") >= 100
ORDER BY 
    "total_pull_request_events" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH repo_languages AS (
    -- Parse the language JSON object to extract language names and byte counts
    SELECT 
        l."repo_name",
        f.key AS "language_name",
        f.value::NUMBER AS "bytes"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES" l,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
    WHERE f.key IS NOT NULL
      AND l."language" IS NOT NULL
),
ranked_languages AS (
    -- Rank languages by bytes descending within each repo; rank 1 = primary language
    SELECT 
        "repo_name",
        "language_name",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "repo_name" 
            ORDER BY "bytes" DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM repo_languages
),
primary_languages AS (
    -- Primary language per repository (the one with the highest byte count)
    SELECT 
        "repo_name",
        "language_name" AS "primary_language"
    FROM ranked_languages
    WHERE rn = 1
),
pull_request_repos AS (
    -- Count PullRequestEvents per repository on January 18, 2023
    SELECT 
        d."repo":"name"::STRING AS "repo_name",
        COUNT(*) AS event_count
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."DAY"."_20230118" d
    WHERE d."type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
    GROUP BY d."repo":"name"::STRING
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
)
-- Return distinct primary languages of repos meeting the threshold
SELECT DISTINCT pl."primary_language"
FROM primary_languages pl
INNER JOIN pull_request_repos pr 
    ON pl."repo_name" = pr."repo_name"
ORDER BY pl."primary_language";
```
</details>

### 16. sf_bq251 (DB: `PYPI`)
**Question**: I want to know the GitHub project URLs for the top 3 most downloaded PyPI packages based on download count. First, extract PyPI package metadata including name, version, and project URLs. Filter these URLs to only include those that link to GitHub repositories. Use a regular expression to clean the GitHub URLs by removing unnecessary parts like 'issues', 'pull', 'blob', and 'tree' paths, keeping only the main repository URL. For packages with multiple versions, use only the most recent version based on upload time. Join this data with download metrics to determine the most downloaded packages. Return only the cleaned GitHub repository URLs (without quotation marks) for the top 3 packages by total download count, ensuring that only packages with valid GitHub URLs are included in the results.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                         |
|:-------------------------------------------|
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel              |
| https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy             |

**OR**

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                |
|:----------------------------------|
| https://github.com/redis/redis-py |
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel     |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy    |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| cleaned_github_url                         |
|:-------------------------------------------|
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel              |
| https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy             |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH latest_package_versions AS (
    -- Get the most recent version for each package based on upload_time
    SELECT 
        "name",
        "version",
        "upload_time",
        "project_urls",
        "home_page"
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            "name",
            "version",
            "upload_time",
            "project_urls",
            "home_page",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "name" ORDER BY "upload_time" DESC) AS "rn"
        FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."DISTRIBUTION_METADATA"
    ) ranked
    WHERE "rn" = 1
),

github_urls_extracted AS (
    -- Extract and clean GitHub URLs from project_urls and home_page
    SELECT 
        lpv."name",
        lpv."version",
        -- Clean GitHub URLs by removing unnecessary path segments
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            CASE 
                -- Extract URL from project_urls array elements
                WHEN f.value::STRING LIKE '%github.com%' THEN 
                    TRIM(SPLIT_PART(TRIM(f.value::STRING, '"'), ', ', -1))
                -- Check home_page if it's a GitHub URL
                WHEN lpv."home_page" LIKE '%github.com%' THEN 
                    TRIM(lpv."home_page")
                ELSE NULL
            END,
            -- Remove issues, pull, blob, tree paths and everything after
            '/(issues|pull|blob|tree)(/.*)?$',
            ''
        ) AS "cleaned_github_url"
    FROM latest_package_versions lpv,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => lpv."project_urls") f
    WHERE (
        -- Filter for GitHub URLs only
        (f.value::STRING LIKE '%github.com%')
        OR lpv."home_page" LIKE '%github.com%'
    )
),

unique_github_urls AS (
    -- Deduplicate GitHub URLs per package (take first one if multiple)
    SELECT 
        "name",
        "cleaned_github_url"
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            "name",
            "cleaned_github_url",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "name" ORDER BY "cleaned_github_url") AS "url_rn"
        FROM github_urls_extracted
        WHERE "cleaned_github_url" IS NOT NULL
    ) deduped
    WHERE "url_rn" = 1
),

package_download_counts AS (
    -- Get total download count per package from FILE_DOWNLOADS
    SELECT 
        "project" AS "package_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_downloads"
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."FILE_DOWNLOADS"
    GROUP BY "project"
),

ranked_packages AS (
    -- Join packages with GitHub URLs and download counts, then rank
    SELECT 
        ug."name" AS "package_name",
        ug."cleaned_github_url",
        pdc."total_downloads",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pdc."total_downloads" DESC) AS "download_rank"
    FROM unique_github_urls ug
    INNER JOIN package_download_counts pdc 
        ON ug."name" = pdc."package_name"
)

-- Final result: Top 3 packages by download count with their GitHub URLs
SELECT 
    "cleaned_github_url"
FROM ranked_packages
WHERE "download_rank" <= 3
ORDER BY "download_rank";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE to get the most recent version per package (max upload_time)
WITH latest_metadata AS (
    SELECT 
        "name",
        "project_urls",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "name" ORDER BY "upload_time" DESC) AS rn
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."DISTRIBUTION_METADATA"
),

-- Keep only the latest version row for each package
latest_only AS (
    SELECT "name", "project_urls"
    FROM latest_metadata
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- Extract GitHub URLs from the project_urls VARIANT array
-- Flatten the array, then filter for entries containing 'github.com'
-- Parse the URL part after the label comma and clean it
github_urls AS (
    SELECT 
        l."name",
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            REGEXP_SUBSTR(f.value::STRING, ', (https?://[^,]+)'),  -- extract URL after label
            '(https://github\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+?)(/.*)?$',           -- remove trailing paths
            '\\1'
        ) AS clean_github_url
    FROM latest_only l,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."project_urls") f
    WHERE f.value::STRING LIKE '%github.com%'
),

-- Keep only distinct package/URL combinations (and non-null URLs)
distinct_github AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "name", clean_github_url
    FROM github_urls
    WHERE clean_github_url IS NOT NULL
),

-- Join with download metrics and aggregate total downloads per package
download_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        dg."name",
        dg.clean_github_url,
        COUNT(*) AS total_downloads
    FROM distinct_github dg
    INNER JOIN "PYPI"."PYPI"."FILE_DOWNLOADS" fd
        ON dg."name" = fd."project"
    GROUP BY dg."name", dg.clean_github_url
),

-- Rank by total downloads descending and take top 3
top3 AS (
    SELECT clean_github_url
    FROM download_counts
    ORDER BY total_downloads DESC
    LIMIT 3
)

-- Final output: only the cleaned GitHub URLs
SELECT clean_github_url FROM top3;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH monthly_averages AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wetbulb,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dewpoint,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_20*`
  WHERE
    -- Filter to tables for years 2010-2014
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '10' AND '14'
    -- Ensure data is within the desired year range
    AND year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2014
  GROUP BY
    year, month
  HAVING
    -- Only keep months where all four averages are non-null
    AVG(air_temperature) IS NOT NULL
    AND AVG(wetbulb_temperature) IS NOT NULL
    AND AVG(dewpoint_temperature) IS NOT NULL
    AND AVG(sea_surface_temp) IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(
    ABS(avg_air - avg_wetbulb) +
    ABS(avg_air - avg_dewpoint) +
    ABS(avg_air - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_wetbulb - avg_dewpoint) +
    ABS(avg_wetbulb - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_dewpoint - avg_sst),
    4
  ) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM
  monthly_averages
ORDER BY
  sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH monthly_aggregates AS (
  -- Compute monthly averages of each temperature type for 2010-2014
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air_temp,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wetbulb_temp,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dewpoint_temp,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
  WHERE
    -- Restrict to tables for years 2010 through 2014
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010' AND '2014'
    -- Exclude NULLs
    AND air_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
    -- Exclude IEEE NaN values that appear in the raw data
    AND NOT IS_NAN(air_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(wetbulb_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(dewpoint_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(sea_surface_temp)
  GROUP BY year, month
)
-- Compute the sum of absolute differences between all pairs of temperature averages
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_wetbulb_temp) +      -- |Air - WetBulb|
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_dewpoint_temp) +     -- |Air - DewPoint|
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_sst) +               -- |Air - SST|
    ABS(avg_wetbulb_temp - avg_dewpoint_temp) + -- |WetBulb - DewPoint|
    ABS(avg_wetbulb_temp - avg_sst) +           -- |WetBulb - SST|
    ABS(avg_dewpoint_temp - avg_sst),           -- |DewPoint - SST|
    4
  ) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM monthly_aggregates
ORDER BY sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

```sql
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2024"
    WHERE "event_begin_time" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Convert event_begin_time from microseconds to timestamp and extract date parts
storms_with_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        "event_begin_time",
        "damage_property",
        "event_type",
        "state",
        "cz_name",
        -- Convert microseconds to timestamp (divide by 1,000,000 to get seconds)
        DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01') AS "event_timestamp",
        -- Extract year and month
        YEAR(DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01')) AS "event_year",
        MONTH(DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01')) AS "event_month",
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01')) AS "event_month_start"
    FROM recent_storms
    WHERE "damage_property" IS NOT NULL
      AND "damage_property" > 0
      AND DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01') >= (SELECT "start_date" FROM date_range)
      AND DATEADD(SECOND, "event_begin_time" / 1000000, '1970-01-01') <= (SELECT "end_date" FROM date_range)
),

-- Rank storms by property damage to get top 100
ranked_storms AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "damage_property" DESC) AS "damage_rank"
    FROM storms_with_dates
),

-- Get top 100 storms by property damage
top_100_storms AS (
    SELECT 
        "event_timestamp",
        "event_year",
        "event_month",
        "event_month_start",
        "damage_property",
        "event_type",
        "state",
        "cz_name",
        "damage_rank"
    FROM ranked_storms
    WHERE "damage_rank" <= 100
),

-- Find the month with the highest count of top 100 storms
most_affected_month AS (
    SELECT 
        "event_year",
        "event_month",
        "event_month_start",
        COUNT(*) AS "storm_count"
    FROM top_100_storms
    GROUP BY "event_year", "event_month", "event_month_start"
    ORDER BY "storm_count" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Get all storms (not just top 100) in the most affected month
storms_in_most_affected_month AS (
    SELECT 
        s."event_timestamp",
        s."event_year",
        s."event_month",
        s."damage_property",
        s."event_type",
        s."state",
        s."cz_name"
    FROM storms_with_dates s
    INNER JOIN most_affected_month m
        ON s."event_year" = m."event_year"
        AND s."event_month" = m."event_month"
)

-- Final result: total count of severe storm events in the most affected month
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS "total_severe_storm_events",
    m."event_year",
    m."event_month",
    m."storm_count" AS "top_100_storms_in_month"
FROM storms_in_most_affected_month s
CROSS JOIN most_affected_month m
GROUP BY m."event_year", m."event_month", m."storm_count";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH all_events AS (

    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2010"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"

    UNION ALL

    UNION ALL

    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2013"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2014"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2015"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2016"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2017"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2018"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2019"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2020"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2021"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2022"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2023"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "damage_property", "event_begin_time"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."STORMS_2024"
),
-- Step 2: Identify the top 100 events with highest property damage
top_100 AS (
    SELECT "event_begin_time",
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "damage_property" DESC) AS rn
    FROM all_events
    QUALIFY rn <= 100
),
-- Step 3: Determine the month with the most events among these top 100
most_affected_month AS (
    SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("event_begin_time" / 1000000)) AS "event_month",
           COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM top_100
    GROUP BY "event_month"
    ORDER BY cnt DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Step 4: Count all severe storm events in the entire 15-year period that occurred in that month
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "total_severe_storms_in_most_affected_month"
FROM all_events
WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("event_begin_time" / 1000000)) = (SELECT "event_month" FROM most_affected_month);
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Convert zip code geometries from WKB to GEOGRAPHY
  zip_geoms AS (
    SELECT
      "city",
      "zip_code",
      "state_code" AS "state",
      ST_GEOGFROMWKB("zip_code_geom") AS "zip_geom"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
  ),
  -- Filter hurricanes with valid names and create point geometries (valid lat/lng only)
  hurricane_points AS (
    SELECT
      "sid",
      "name",
      ST_POINT("longitude", "latitude") AS "point_geom"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES"
    WHERE "name" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("name") != ''
      AND "longitude" IS NOT NULL AND "latitude" IS NOT NULL
      AND "longitude" BETWEEN -180 AND 180
      AND "latitude" BETWEEN -90 AND 90
  ),
  -- Join hurricanes to zip codes where the point falls inside the zip geometry
  intersecting AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      z."city",
      z."zip_code",
      z."state",
      h."sid",
      h."name"
    FROM hurricane_points h
    INNER JOIN zip_geoms z
      ON ST_WITHIN(h."point_geom", z."zip_geom")
  )
-- Aggregate per city/zip/state
SELECT
  "city",
  "zip_code",
  "state",
  COUNT(DISTINCT "sid") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
  LISTAGG(DISTINCT "name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "name") AS "hurricane_list"
FROM intersecting
GROUP BY "city", "zip_code", "state"
ORDER BY "count_of_hurricanes" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "hurricane_points" AS (
    -- Get distinct hurricanes (by SID) that are Category 1-5 on Saffir-Simpson scale
    -- and have a non-empty name (exclude unnamed hurricanes)
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "sid",
        "name",
        ST_GEOMPOINT("longitude", "latitude") AS "point_geom"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES"
    WHERE "usa_sshs" >= 1
      AND "name" IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM("name") != ''
),
"zip_hurricane_links" AS (
    -- Spatial join: find which zip codes contain hurricane track points
    SELECT DISTINCT
        z."city",
        z."zip_code",
        z."state_name" AS "state",
        hp."sid",
        hp."name"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES" z
    INNER JOIN "hurricane_points" hp
        ON ST_WITHIN(
            hp."point_geom",
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom")
        )
)
-- Aggregate: count hurricanes and list their names per city/zip/state
SELECT
    "city",
    "zip_code",
    "state",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "sid") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
    LISTAGG(DISTINCT "name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "name") AS "list_of_hurricanes"
FROM "zip_hurricane_links"
GROUP BY "city", "zip_code", "state"
ORDER BY "count_of_hurricanes" DESC, "city", "zip_code";
```
</details>
