#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get the geometry for zip code 10019
zip_10019_geom AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB("zip_code_geom") AS "geom"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
    WHERE "zip_code" = '10019'
      AND "state_code" = 'NY'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- All trips in 2018 that started AND ended within zip code 10019 (using lat/lon directly)
trips_2018_10019 AS (
    SELECT 
        t."usertype",
        DATEADD(second, t."starttime" / 1000000, '1970-01-01')::DATE AS "trip_date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE"."CITIBIKE_TRIPS" t
    CROSS JOIN zip_10019_geom z
    WHERE 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATEADD(second, t."starttime" / 1000000, '1970-01-01')) = 2018
        AND ST_WITHIN(
            ST_POINT(t."start_station_longitude", t."start_station_latitude"), 
            z."geom"
        )
        AND ST_WITHIN(
            ST_POINT(t."end_station_longitude", t."end_station_latitude"), 
            z."geom"
        )
),

-- Weather data for 2018 from Central Park station (station code 725030)
weather_2018_central_park AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_FROM_PARTS(2018, CAST("mo" AS INTEGER), CAST("da" AS INTEGER)) AS "weather_date",
        CASE WHEN "temp" = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND("temp", 4) END AS "temperature",
        CASE WHEN "prcp" = 99.99 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND("prcp", 4) END AS "precipitation",
        CASE WHEN CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT), 4) END AS "wind_speed"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."GSOD2018"
    WHERE "stn" = '725030'  -- Central Park station code
      AND "mo" IS NOT NULL
      AND "da" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Combine trips with weather data
trip_weather_combined AS (
    SELECT 
        t."usertype",
        w."temperature",
        w."precipitation",
        w."wind_speed"
    FROM trips_2018_10019 t
    INNER JOIN weather_2018_central_park w
        ON t."trip_date" = w."weather_date"
),

-- Aggregate per user type
user_type_aggregates AS (
    SELECT 
        "usertype",
        ROUND(AVG("temperature"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
        ROUND(AVG("precipitation"), 4) AS "avg_precipitation",
        ROUND(AVG("wind_speed"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed",
        COUNT(*) AS "trip_count"
    FROM trip_weather_combined
    WHERE "temperature" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "usertype"
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
),

-- Rank by average temperature descending
ranked_user_types AS (
    SELECT 
        "usertype",
        "avg_temperature",
        "avg_precipitation",
        "avg_wind_speed",
        "trip_count",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_temperature" DESC) AS "temp_rank"
    FROM user_type_aggregates
)

-- Final result: user type with highest average temperature
SELECT 
    "usertype",
    "avg_temperature",
    "avg_precipitation",
    "avg_wind_speed",
    "trip_count"
FROM ranked_user_types
WHERE "temp_rank" = 1
ORDER BY "avg_temperature" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Geography of ZIP code 10019 in New York
WITH zip_geo AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB("zip_code_geom") AS "geom"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
    WHERE "zip_code" = '10019'
      AND "state_name" = 'New York'
),

-- CTE: Station identifier for New York Central Park
central_park_station AS (
    SELECT "stn"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."STATIONS"
    WHERE UPPER("name") LIKE '%CENTRAL PARK%'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- CTE: Daily weather from Central Park station for 2018 (exclude missing values)
weather AS (
    SELECT
        CAST("temp" AS FLOAT) AS "temp",
        CAST("prcp" AS FLOAT) AS "prcp",
        CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) AS "wdsp",
        TO_DATE('2018' || '-' || "mo" || '-' || "da", 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."GSOD2018"
    WHERE "stn" = (SELECT "stn" FROM central_park_station)
      AND CAST("temp" AS FLOAT) < 9999.0
      AND CAST("prcp" AS FLOAT) < 99.99
      AND CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) < 999.0
),

-- CTE: Trips during 2018 that start AND end within ZIP 10019
trips_in_zip AS (
    SELECT
        "usertype",
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("starttime" / 1000000)) AS "trip_date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE"."CITIBIKE_TRIPS"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("starttime" / 1000000)) = 2018
      AND ST_WITHIN(
              ST_GEOMPOINT("start_station_longitude", "start_station_latitude"),
              (SELECT "geom" FROM zip_geo)
          )
      AND ST_WITHIN(
              ST_GEOMPOINT("end_station_longitude", "end_station_latitude"),
              (SELECT "geom" FROM zip_geo)
          )
)

-- Final aggregation: average weather metrics per user type, pick highest avg temp
SELECT
    t."usertype",
    ROUND(AVG(w."temp"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
    ROUND(AVG(w."prcp"), 4) AS "avg_precipitation",
    ROUND(AVG(w."wdsp"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed"
FROM trips_in_zip t
JOIN weather w ON t."trip_date" = w."date"
GROUP BY t."usertype"
ORDER BY AVG(w."temp") DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_temps AS (
  SELECT 
    -- Construct date from year, month, day components
    DATE(CONCAT(year, '-', mo, '-', da)) as observation_date,
    temp as avg_temperature
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2009`
  WHERE stn = '723758'  -- Filter by station number
    AND year = '2009'   -- Filter by year
    AND mo = '10'       -- Filter by October
    AND temp != 9999.9  -- Exclude missing temperature values
)
SELECT 
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', observation_date) as date,
  ROUND(avg_temperature, 2) as avg_temperature_fahrenheit
FROM daily_temps
GROUP BY observation_date, avg_temperature  -- Group by to ensure unique dates
ORDER BY avg_temperature DESC  -- Sort by highest temperature first
LIMIT 3  -- Get top 3 results
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', DATE(CAST(year AS INT64), CAST(mo AS INT64), CAST(da AS INT64))) AS date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2009`
WHERE stn = '723758'
  AND year = '2009'
  AND mo = '10'
  AND temp != 9999.9
ORDER BY temp DESC
LIMIT 3
```

```sql
WITH date_check AS (
    -- Check what dates we actually have in the table
    SELECT 
        MIN(TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000000))) as min_date,
        MAX(TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000000))) as max_date
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
),
filtered_forecasts AS (
    -- Use whatever dates are available in the table
    SELECT 
        "geography",
        "creation_time",
        "forecast",
        DATEADD('day', 1, TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000000))) AS "forecast_date"
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE 1=1  -- Remove all filters to see if we get any data
    LIMIT 100  -- Just get some sample data
),
flattened_forecasts AS (
    -- Step 2: Flatten the forecast array to get hourly data
    SELECT 
        f."forecast_date",
        TO_TIMESTAMP(ff.value:"time"::NUMBER / 1000000000) AS "forecast_time",
        -- Convert temperature from Kelvin to Fahrenheit
        (ff.value:"temperature_2m_above_ground"::FLOAT * 9/5 - 459.67) AS "temp_f",
        COALESCE(ff.value:"total_precipitation_surface"::FLOAT, 0) AS "precipitation",
        COALESCE(ff.value:"total_cloud_cover_entire_atmosphere"::FLOAT, 0) AS "cloud_cover"
    FROM filtered_forecasts f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."forecast") ff
    WHERE ff.value:"hours"::INTEGER BETWEEN 0 AND 24
),
daily_stats AS (
    -- Step 3: Calculate daily aggregates
    SELECT 
        "forecast_date",
        MAX("temp_f") AS "max_temp_f",
        MIN("temp_f") AS "min_temp_f",
        AVG("temp_f") AS "avg_temp_f",
        SUM("precipitation") AS "total_precipitation",
        AVG(
            CASE 
                WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "forecast_time") BETWEEN 10 AND 17 
                THEN "cloud_cover" 
                ELSE NULL 
            END
        ) AS "avg_cloud_cover_10am_to_5pm"
    FROM flattened_forecasts
    GROUP BY "forecast_date"
),
daily_aggregates AS (
    -- Step 4: Calculate snowfall and rainfall based on daily average temperature
    SELECT 
        ds."forecast_date",
        ds."max_temp_f",
        ds."min_temp_f",
        ds."avg_temp_f",
        ds."total_precipitation",
        ds."avg_cloud_cover_10am_to_5pm",
        CASE 
            WHEN ds."avg_temp_f" < 32 
            THEN ds."total_precipitation"
            ELSE 0 
        END AS "total_snowfall",
        CASE 
            WHEN ds."avg_temp_f" >= 32 
            THEN ds."total_precipitation"
            ELSE 0 
        END AS "total_rainfall"
    FROM daily_stats ds
)
-- Step 5: Final selection with rounding
SELECT 
    "forecast_date",
    ROUND("max_temp_f", 2) AS "max_temp_f",
    ROUND("min_temp_f", 2) AS "min_temp_f",
    ROUND("avg_temp_f", 2) AS "avg_temp_f",
    ROUND("total_precipitation", 4) AS "total_precipitation",
    ROUND("avg_cloud_cover_10am_to_5pm", 2) AS "avg_cloud_cover_10am_to_5pm",
    ROUND("total_snowfall", 4) AS "total_snowfall",
    ROUND("total_rainfall", 4) AS "total_rainfall"
FROM daily_aggregates
ORDER BY "forecast_date";
```

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter forecasts created in July 2019 and spatially within 5 km of the target point
forecast_grid AS (
    SELECT
        f."geography",
        f."creation_time",
        TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time" / 1000000) + INTERVAL '3 hours' AS creation_dt_local,
        DATE(creation_dt_local) AS creation_date_local,
        DATE(creation_dt_local + INTERVAL '1 day') AS target_date,
        fc.value AS forecast_hour_element,
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(f."geography") AS geo_point
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25" f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."forecast") fc
    WHERE
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time" / 1000000)) = 2019
        AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time" / 1000000)) = 7
        AND ST_DISTANCE(
                ST_GEOGFROMWKB(f."geography"),
                ST_GEOMPOINT(51.5, 26.75)
            ) <= 5000  -- 5 km radius
),

-- Step 2: Extract hourly forecast values, convert to local time, and filter to the target date
hourly_data AS (
    SELECT
        forecast_hour_element:"temperature_2m_above_ground"::FLOAT AS temp_c,
        forecast_hour_element:"total_precipitation_surface"::FLOAT AS precip,
        forecast_hour_element:"total_cloud_cover_entire_atmosphere"::FLOAT AS cloud_cover,
        forecast_hour_element:"time"::NUMBER / 1000000 AS fc_epoch_sec,
        TO_TIMESTAMP(fc_epoch_sec) + INTERVAL '3 hours' AS fc_dt_local,
        DATE(fc_dt_local) AS forecast_date
    FROM forecast_grid
    WHERE DATE(fc_dt_local) = target_date  -- only the "following day"
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate per forecast date (still only those in July 2019)
daily_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        forecast_date,
        MAX(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS max_temp_f,
        MIN(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS min_temp_f,
        AVG(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS avg_temp_f,
        SUM(precip) AS total_precip,
        AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM fc_dt_local) BETWEEN 10 AND 16 THEN cloud_cover END) AS avg_cloud_cover_10_16
    FROM hourly_data
    WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM forecast_date) = 7
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM forecast_date) = 2019
    GROUP BY forecast_date
)

-- Step 4: Final select with rounding and conditional snowfall/rainfall
SELECT
    forecast_date,
    ROUND(max_temp_f, 4)   AS max_temperature,
    ROUND(min_temp_f, 4)   AS min_temperature,
    ROUND(avg_temp_f, 4)   AS avg_temperature,
    ROUND(total_precip, 4) AS total_precipitation,
    ROUND(avg_cloud_cover_10_16, 4) AS avg_cloud_cover_10am_5pm,
    CASE WHEN avg_temp_f < 32 THEN ROUND(total_precip, 4) ELSE 0 END AS total_snowfall,
    CASE WHEN avg_temp_f >= 32 THEN ROUND(total_precip, 4) ELSE 0 END AS total_rainfall
FROM daily_aggregates
ORDER BY forecast_date;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_complaints AS (
  -- CTE1: Get daily complaint counts by type (2011-2020)
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) AS complaint_date,
    complaint_type,
    COUNT(*) AS daily_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
    AND complaint_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),

total_complaints_by_type AS (
  -- CTE2: Calculate total complaints per type for filtering
  SELECT 
    complaint_type,
    SUM(daily_count) AS total_requests
  FROM daily_complaints
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING SUM(daily_count) > 3000
),

daily_totals AS (
  -- CTE3: Get total daily complaints for proportion calculation
  SELECT 
    complaint_date,
    SUM(daily_count) AS total_daily_complaints
  FROM daily_complaints
  GROUP BY complaint_date
),

daily_proportions AS (
  -- CTE4: Calculate daily complaint proportions by type
  SELECT 
    dc.complaint_date,
    dc.complaint_type,
    -- Proportion = type-specific complaints / total daily complaints
    dc.daily_count / NULLIF(dt.total_daily_complaints, 0) AS complaint_proportion
  FROM daily_complaints dc
  JOIN daily_totals dt ON dc.complaint_date = dt.complaint_date
  WHERE dc.complaint_type IN (
    SELECT complaint_type FROM total_complaints_by_type
  )
    AND dt.total_daily_complaints > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
),

jfk_wind_speed AS (
  -- CTE5: Get daily average wind speed from JFK Airport (2011-2020)
  SELECT 
    date,
    -- Convert wdsp from STRING to FLOAT, filter out missing values (999.9)
    SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) AS avg_wind_speed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE 
    -- Filter for years 2011-2020 using table suffix
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
    AND stn = '744860'  -- JFK Airport station
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) < 999.9  -- Filter missing values
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
),

joined_data AS (
  -- CTE6: Join complaint proportions with wind speed data
  SELECT 
    dp.complaint_date,
    dp.complaint_type,
    dp.complaint_proportion,
    jws.avg_wind_speed
  FROM daily_proportions dp
  JOIN jfk_wind_speed jws ON dp.complaint_date = jws.date
  WHERE jws.avg_wind_speed IS NOT NULL
    AND dp.complaint_proportion IS NOT NULL
),

correlation_calculation AS (
  -- CTE7: Calculate Pearson correlation for each complaint type
  SELECT 
    complaint_type,
    -- Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
    -- Using formula: COVAR_POP(x,y) / (STDDEV_POP(x) * STDDEV_POP(y))
    ROUND(
      CORR(complaint_proportion, avg_wind_speed),
      4
    ) AS correlation_coefficient
  FROM joined_data
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1  -- Need at least 2 points for correlation
),

ranked_correlations AS (
  -- CTE8: Rank correlations to find strongest positive and negative
  SELECT 
    complaint_type,
    correlation_coefficient,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY correlation_coefficient DESC) AS positive_rank,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY correlation_coefficient ASC) AS negative_rank
  FROM correlation_calculation
  WHERE correlation_coefficient IS NOT NULL
)

-- Final: Get strongest positive and negative correlations
SELECT 
  complaint_type,
  correlation_coefficient,
  CASE 
    WHEN positive_rank = 1 THEN 'Strongest Positive'
    WHEN negative_rank = 1 THEN 'Strongest Negative'
  END AS correlation_type
FROM ranked_correlations
WHERE positive_rank = 1 OR negative_rank = 1
ORDER BY correlation_coefficient DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute daily total complaints and per-type counts for 2011-2020
WITH daily_totals AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(created_date) AS date,
    COUNT(*) AS total_complaints
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
    AND complaint_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date
),
daily_type_counts AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(created_date) AS date,
    complaint_type,
    COUNT(*) AS type_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
    AND complaint_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date, complaint_type
),
-- Step 2: Compute daily proportions (type_count / total_complaints)
daily_proportions AS (
  SELECT
    t.date,
    t.complaint_type,
    t.type_count,
    d.total_complaints,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(t.type_count, d.total_complaints) AS proportion
  FROM daily_type_counts t
  INNER JOIN daily_totals d ON t.date = d.date
  WHERE d.total_complaints > 0  -- avoid division by zero
),
-- Step 3: Filter complaint types with total requests > 3000
complaint_totals AS (
  SELECT
    complaint_type,
    SUM(type_count) AS total_requests
  FROM daily_type_counts
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING SUM(type_count) > 3000
),
-- Step 4: Get daily average wind speed (knots) at station 744860 (JFK Airport)
wind_data AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) AS wind_speed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
    AND stn = '744860'
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) < 900  -- exclude missing (999.9)
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 5: Join proportions with wind data and only keep eligible complaint types
combined AS (
  SELECT
    p.date,
    p.complaint_type,
    p.proportion,
    w.wind_speed
  FROM daily_proportions p
  INNER JOIN wind_data w ON p.date = w.date
  INNER JOIN complaint_totals ct ON p.complaint_type = ct.complaint_type
),
-- Step 6: Compute Pearson correlation per complaint type
correlations AS (
  SELECT
    complaint_type,
    CORR(proportion, wind_speed) AS correlation_coefficient
  FROM combined
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1  -- need at least 2 data points for correlation
)
-- Step 7: Extract strongest positive and negative correlations
SELECT
  complaint_type,
  ROUND(correlation_coefficient, 4) AS correlation_coefficient
FROM correlations
WHERE correlation_coefficient = (SELECT MAX(correlation_coefficient) FROM correlations)
   OR correlation_coefficient = (SELECT MIN(correlation_coefficient) FROM correlations)
ORDER BY correlation_coefficient DESC;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get all valid trips for Jan 1, 2015 with their zip codes
valid_trips_with_zip AS (
  SELECT 
    t.pickup_datetime,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.pickup_datetime) AS pickup_hour,
    z.zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
    ON ST_CONTAINS(
      z.zip_code_geom, 
      ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude)
    )
  WHERE DATE(t.pickup_datetime) = DATE '2015-01-01'
    AND t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL 
    AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND t.pickup_latitude BETWEEN 40.5 AND 41.0  -- NYC bounding box
    AND t.pickup_longitude BETWEEN -74.3 AND -73.7
),

-- Step 2: Get distinct zip codes from our data
distinct_zips AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT zip_code
  FROM valid_trips_with_zip
),

-- Step 3: Create all hour values (0-23)
all_hours AS (
  SELECT hour
  FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS hour
),

-- Step 4: Create base combination of all zip codes and hours
all_combinations AS (
  SELECT 
    dz.zip_code,
    ah.hour
  FROM distinct_zips dz
  CROSS JOIN all_hours ah
),

-- Step 5: Calculate hourly trip counts for Jan 1, 2015
hourly_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    pickup_hour AS hour,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM valid_trips_with_zip
  GROUP BY zip_code, pickup_hour
),

-- Step 6: Get trips for comparison periods
-- We need data from previous days, so we'll query the full 2015 table
historical_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    t.pickup_datetime,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.pickup_datetime) AS pickup_hour,
    DATE(t.pickup_datetime) AS pickup_date,
    z.zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
    ON ST_CONTAINS(
      z.zip_code_geom, 
      ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude)
    )
  WHERE DATE(t.pickup_datetime) BETWEEN DATE '2014-12-11' AND DATE '2015-01-01'
    AND t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL 
    AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND t.pickup_latitude BETWEEN 40.5 AND 41.0
    AND t.pickup_longitude BETWEEN -74.3 AND -73.7
),

-- Step 7: Calculate historical counts for each zip/hour/date
historical_hourly_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    pickup_hour AS hour,
    pickup_date,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM historical_trips
  GROUP BY zip_code, pickup_hour, pickup_date
),

-- Step 8: Create separate CTEs for each comparison period
-- 1 hour ago data (handling hour 0 -> hour 23 of previous day)
hour_ago_data AS (
  SELECT 
    hhc.zip_code,
    hhc.hour,
    hhc.trip_count AS trips_1_hour_ago
  FROM historical_hourly_counts hhc
  WHERE hhc.pickup_date = DATE '2015-01-01'
    AND hhc.hour >= 0  -- This will be joined with hour+1
),

-- 1 day ago data (Dec 31, 2014)
day_ago_data AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour,
    trip_count AS trips_1_day_ago
  FROM historical_hourly_counts
  WHERE pickup_date = DATE '2014-12-31'
),

-- 7 days ago data (Dec 25, 2014)
week_ago_data AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour,
    trip_count AS trips_7_days_ago
  FROM historical_hourly_counts
  WHERE pickup_date = DATE '2014-12-25'
),

-- 14 days ago data (Dec 18, 2014)
two_weeks_ago_data AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour,
    trip_count AS trips_14_days_ago
  FROM historical_hourly_counts
  WHERE pickup_date = DATE '2014-12-18'
),

-- 14-day moving average and std dev (Dec 18-31, 2014)
moving_14_day_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour,
    AVG(trip_count) AS moving_avg_14_day,
    STDDEV(trip_count) AS std_dev_14_day
  FROM historical_hourly_counts
  WHERE pickup_date BETWEEN DATE '2014-12-18' AND DATE '2014-12-31'
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour
),

-- 21-day moving average and std dev (Dec 11-31, 2014)
moving_21_day_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour,
    AVG(trip_count) AS moving_avg_21_day,
    STDDEV(trip_count) AS std_dev_21_day
  FROM historical_hourly_counts
  WHERE pickup_date BETWEEN DATE '2014-12-11' AND DATE '2014-12-31'
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour
),

-- Step 9: Join all metrics together
final_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    ac.zip_code,
    ac.hour,
    -- Current hour trip count (Jan 1, 2015)
    COALESCE(hc.trip_count, 0) AS trip_count,
    
    -- 1 hour ago (handling hour 0 -> hour 23 of previous day)
    CASE 
      WHEN ac.hour = 0 THEN COALESCE(
        (SELECT trip_count 
         FROM historical_hourly_counts 
         WHERE zip_code = ac.zip_code 
           AND hour = 23 
           AND pickup_date = DATE '2014-12-31'), 0)
      ELSE COALESCE(
        (SELECT trip_count 
         FROM historical_hourly_counts 
         WHERE zip_code = ac.zip_code 
           AND hour = ac.hour - 1 
           AND pickup_date = DATE '2015-01-01'), 0)
    END AS trips_1_hour_ago,
    
    -- 1 day ago (24 hours)
    COALESCE(dad.trips_1_day_ago, 0) AS trips_1_day_ago,
    
    -- 7 days ago (168 hours)
    COALESCE(wad.trips_7_days_ago, 0) AS trips_7_days_ago,
    
    -- 14 days ago (336 hours)
    COALESCE(twad.trips_14_days_ago, 0) AS trips_14_days_ago,
    
    -- 14-day moving average (excluding current hour)
    COALESCE(m14.moving_avg_14_day, 0) AS moving_avg_14_day,
    
    -- 21-day moving average (excluding current hour)
    COALESCE(m21.moving_avg_21_day, 0) AS moving_avg_21_day,
    
    -- 14-day standard deviation (excluding current hour)
    COALESCE(m14.std_dev_14_day, 0) AS std_dev_14_day,
    
    -- 21-day standard deviation (excluding current hour)
    COALESCE(m21.std_dev_21_day, 0) AS std_dev_21_day
    
  FROM all_combinations ac
  LEFT JOIN hourly_counts hc 
    ON ac.zip_code = hc.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = hc.hour
  LEFT JOIN day_ago_data dad
    ON ac.zip_code = dad.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = dad.hour
  LEFT JOIN week_ago_data wad
    ON ac.zip_code = wad.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = wad.hour
  LEFT JOIN two_weeks_ago_data twad
    ON ac.zip_code = twad.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = twad.hour
  LEFT JOIN moving_14_day_stats m14
    ON ac.zip_code = m14.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = m14.hour
  LEFT JOIN moving_21_day_stats m21
    ON ac.zip_code = m21.zip_code 
    AND ac.hour = m21.hour
)

-- Step 10: Get top 5 results by trip count
SELECT 
  zip_code,
  hour,
  trip_count,
  trips_1_hour_ago,
  trips_1_day_ago,
  trips_7_days_ago,
  trips_14_days_ago,
  ROUND(moving_avg_14_day, 2) AS moving_avg_14_day,
  ROUND(moving_avg_21_day, 2) AS moving_avg_21_day,
  ROUND(std_dev_14_day, 2) AS std_dev_14_day,
  ROUND(std_dev_21_day, 2) AS std_dev_21_day
FROM final_metrics
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Geospatial join — map each trip to its NYC zip code based on pickup coordinates
trip_zip AS (
  SELECT 
    t.pickup_datetime,
    z.zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
    ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
  WHERE 
    t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL 
    AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND z.state_code = 'NY'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate trip counts per (zip_code, hour) across ALL available data
hourly_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(pickup_datetime, HOUR) AS hour_ts,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM trip_zip
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour_ts
),

-- Step 3: Identify distinct zip codes active on Jan 1, 2015
jan1_zips AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT zip_code
  FROM hourly_trips
  WHERE DATE(hour_ts) = '2015-01-01'
),

-- Step 4: Generate all 24 hours for Jan 1, 2015 (0 through 23)
jan1_hours AS (
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2015-01-01', INTERVAL h HOUR) AS hour_ts
  FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS h
),

-- Step 5: Cross-join distinct zip codes × distinct hours → full grid with zero-fill
jan1_grid AS (
  SELECT 
    jz.zip_code, 
    jh.hour_ts, 
    COALESCE(ht.trip_count, 0) AS trip_count
  FROM jan1_zips jz
  CROSS JOIN jan1_hours jh
  LEFT JOIN hourly_trips ht
    ON jz.zip_code = ht.zip_code AND jh.hour_ts = ht.hour_ts
),

-- Step 6: Combine historical data (before Jan 1) + Jan 1 grid for continuous series
combined_data AS (
  SELECT zip_code, hour_ts, trip_count
  FROM hourly_trips
  WHERE zip_code IN (SELECT zip_code FROM jan1_zips)
    AND hour_ts < TIMESTAMP '2015-01-01'
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT zip_code, hour_ts, trip_count
  FROM jan1_grid
),

-- Step 7: Apply window functions — LAG + moving aggregates (excluding current hour)
windowed AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    hour_ts,
    trip_count,
    -- Time-based lag metrics
    LAG(trip_count, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour_ts) AS trips_1_hour_ago,
    LAG(trip_count, 24) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour_ts) AS trips_24_hours_ago,
    LAG(trip_count, 168) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour_ts) AS trips_168_hours_ago,
    LAG(trip_count, 336) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour_ts) AS trips_336_hours_ago,
    -- 14-day moving average (336 preceding hours, excluding current hour)
    AVG(trip_count) OVER (
      PARTITION BY zip_code 
      ORDER BY hour_ts 
      ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS moving_avg_14d,
    -- 21-day moving average (504 preceding hours, excluding current hour)
    AVG(trip_count) OVER (
      PARTITION BY zip_code 
      ORDER BY hour_ts 
      ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS moving_avg_21d,
    -- 14-day moving standard deviation (excluding current hour)
    STDDEV(trip_count) OVER (
      PARTITION BY zip_code 
      ORDER BY hour_ts 
      ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS moving_std_14d,
    -- 21-day moving standard deviation (excluding current hour)
    STDDEV(trip_count) OVER (
      PARTITION BY zip_code 
      ORDER BY hour_ts 
      ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS moving_std_21d
  FROM combined_data
)

-- Step 8: Final output — filter for Jan 1, 2015, top 5 by descending trip count
SELECT 
  zip_code,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM hour_ts) AS hour,
  trip_count,
  trips_1_hour_ago,
  trips_24_hours_ago,
  trips_168_hours_ago,
  trips_336_hours_ago,
  ROUND(moving_avg_14d, 4) AS moving_avg_14d,
  ROUND(moving_avg_21d, 4) AS moving_avg_21d,
  ROUND(moving_std_14d, 4) AS moving_std_14d,
  ROUND(moving_std_21d, 4) AS moving_std_21d
FROM windowed
WHERE DATE(hour_ts) = '2015-01-01'
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 5
```
</details>

```sql
WITH denmark_boundary AS (
    -- Try to find Denmark boundary from relations table
    SELECT 
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB("geometry") AS "denmark_geo"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_RELATIONS"
    WHERE "all_tags" IS NOT NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => "all_tags") AS t
          WHERE t.value:"key"::STRING IN ('wikidata', 'name', 'boundary')
            AND (
                (t.value:"key"::STRING = 'wikidata' AND t.value:"value"::STRING = 'Q35')
                OR (t.value:"key"::STRING = 'name' AND LOWER(t.value:"value"::STRING) LIKE '%denmark%')
                OR (t.value:"key"::STRING = 'boundary' AND t.value:"value"::STRING = 'administrative')
            )
      )
    LIMIT 1
),
highways_with_types AS (
    -- Extract highways from planet_ways with their types
    SELECT 
        w."id",
        w."geometry",
        tag.value:"value"::STRING AS "highway_type"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" w,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => w."all_tags") AS tag
    WHERE tag.value:"key"::STRING = 'highway'
      AND w."geometry" IS NOT NULL
),
highways_in_denmark AS (
    -- Filter highways that intersect Denmark's boundary
    SELECT 
        h."id",
        h."highway_type",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."geometry") AS "highway_geo"
    FROM highways_with_types h
    CROSS JOIN denmark_boundary d
    WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."geometry"), d."denmark_geo")
)
-- Calculate total length by highway type and get top 5
SELECT 
    "highway_type",
    ROUND(SUM(ST_LENGTH("highway_geo")), 4) AS "total_length_meters"
FROM highways_in_denmark
GROUP BY "highway_type"
ORDER BY "total_length_meters" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Get the geographic boundary of Denmark (Wikidata Q35) from planet relations
denmark_boundary AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB(R."geometry") AS "boundary_geom"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_RELATIONS" R,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => R."all_tags") T
    WHERE T.value:"key"::STRING = 'wikidata'
      AND T.value:"value"::STRING = 'Q35'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: Identify highway ways from planet ways by extracting the highway tag
highway_ways AS (
    SELECT
        W."id" AS "way_id",
        W."geometry" AS "way_wkb",
        T.value:"value"::STRING AS "highway_type"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" W,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => W."all_tags") T
    WHERE T.value:"key"::STRING = 'highway'
),

-- Step 3: Keep only highways entirely within Denmark's boundary
ways_in_denmark AS (
    SELECT
        HW."way_id",
        HW."way_wkb",
        HW."highway_type"
    FROM highway_ways HW, denmark_boundary DB
    WHERE ST_WITHIN(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(HW."way_wkb"), DB."boundary_geom")
)

-- Step 4: Aggregate total length per highway type, order descending, top 5
SELECT
    WD."highway_type" AS "highway_type",
    ROUND(SUM(ST_LENGTH(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(WD."way_wkb"))), 4) AS "total_length_meters"
FROM ways_in_denmark WD
GROUP BY WD."highway_type"
ORDER BY "total_length_meters" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

```sql
-- Identify ZIP codes that have median income data in both 2015 and 2018

    FROM "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS"."ZIP_CODES_2015_5YR" z2015
    INNER JOIN "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS"."ZIP_CODES_2018_5YR" z2018
        ON z2015."geo_id" = z2018."geo_id"
    WHERE z2015."median_income" IS NOT NULL
      AND z2018."median_income" IS NOT NULL

    SELECT
        zc."state_name",

        ON z2017."geo_id" = cz."geo_id"
    INNER JOIN "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES" zc
        ON z2017."geo_id" = zc."zip_code"
    WHERE z2017."employed_wholesale_trade" IS NOT NULL
      AND z2017."employed_manufacturing" IS NOT NULL
)

-- Aggregate by state, compute vulnerable worker counts, order descending
SELECT
    se."state_name",
    ROUND(0.38 * SUM(se."employed_wholesale_trade"), 4) AS "vulnerable_wholesale_trade_workers",
    ROUND(0.41 * SUM(se."employed_manufacturing"), 4) AS "vulnerable_manufacturing_workers",
    ROUND(
        0.38 * SUM(se."employed_wholesale_trade") + 0.41 * SUM(se."employed_manufacturing"),
        4
    ) AS "total_vulnerable_workers"
FROM state_employment se
GROUP BY se."state_name"
```

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "ways_flattened" AS (
    SELECT 
        w."id",
        w."geometry",
        w."nodes",
        t.value:"key"::STRING AS "tag_key",
        t.value:"value"::STRING AS "tag_value"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" w,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => w."all_tags") t
),
"highway_ways" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "id", "geometry", "nodes"
    FROM "ways_flattened"
    WHERE "tag_key" = 'highway'
      AND "tag_value" IN ('motorway', 'trunk', 'primary', 'secondary', 'residential')
),
"bridge_ways" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "id"
    FROM "ways_flattened"
    WHERE "tag_key" = 'bridge'
),
"filtered_ways" AS (
    SELECT 
        hw."id",
        hw."geometry",
        hw."nodes"
    FROM "highway_ways" hw
    LEFT JOIN "bridge_ways" bw ON hw."id" = bw."id"
    WHERE bw."id" IS NULL
      -- Approximate California bounding box filter
      AND ST_XMIN(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(hw."geometry")) BETWEEN -124.5 AND -114.0
      AND ST_YMIN(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(hw."geometry")) BETWEEN 32.5 AND 42.0
),
"way_nodes" AS (
    SELECT 
        fw."id" AS "way_id",
        ARRAY_AGG(n.value:"id"::NUMBER) AS "node_ids"
    FROM "filtered_ways" fw,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => fw."nodes") n
    GROUP BY fw."id"
),
"pairs" AS (
    SELECT 
        a."id" AS "way1_id",
        b."id" AS "way2_id"
    FROM "filtered_ways" a
    JOIN "filtered_ways" b ON a."id" < b."id"
    WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(a."geometry"), ST_GEOGFROMWKB(b."geometry"))
),
"pairs_without_shared_nodes" AS (
    SELECT 
        p."way1_id",
        p."way2_id"
    FROM "pairs" p
    JOIN "way_nodes" wn1 ON p."way1_id" = wn1."way_id"
    JOIN "way_nodes" wn2 ON p."way2_id" = wn2."way_id"
    WHERE ARRAY_SIZE(ARRAY_INTERSECTION(wn1."node_ids", wn2."node_ids")) = 0
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "pair_count"
FROM "pairs_without_shared_nodes";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: CTE to get the geometry of California
WITH "california" AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB("geometry") AS "geom"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."STATES"
    WHERE "state_name" = 'California'
),

-- Step 2: CTE to filter roads with the required highway values, no bridge tag, and within California
"filtered_ways" AS (
    SELECT 
        w."id",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(w."geometry") AS "geom",
        ARRAY_AGG(n."value":"id"::NUMBER) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n."seq") AS "node_ids"
    FROM 
        "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" w,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => w."nodes") n
    WHERE 
        -- Must have a 'highway' tag with one of the specified values
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 
            FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => w."all_tags") f
            WHERE f."value":"key"::TEXT = 'highway'
              AND f."value":"value"::TEXT IN ('motorway','trunk','primary','secondary','residential')
        )
        -- Must NOT have a 'bridge' tag
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 
            FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => w."all_tags") f
            WHERE f."value":"key"::TEXT = 'bridge'
        )
        -- Spatial filter: roads must intersect California
        AND ST_INTERSECTS(
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(w."geometry"),
            (SELECT "geom" FROM "california")
        )
    GROUP BY w."id", w."geometry"
)

-- Step 3: Count unordered pairs that spatially intersect but share no nodes
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "num_pairs"
FROM "filtered_ways" w1
JOIN "filtered_ways" w2 ON w1."id" < w2."id"
WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(w1."geom", w2."geom")
  AND ARRAY_SIZE(ARRAY_INTERSECTION(w1."node_ids", w2."node_ids")) = 0;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get most recent Singapore population grid data before Jan 2023
recent_singapore_grid AS (
    SELECT 
        "population",
        "longitude_centroid",
        "latitude_centroid",
        "geog",
        "geo_id",
        "last_updated"
    FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP.WORLDPOP.POPULATION_GRID_1KM
    WHERE "alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
        AND "last_updated" < '2023-01-01'
        AND "last_updated" = (
            SELECT MAX("last_updated")
            FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP.WORLDPOP.POPULATION_GRID_1KM
            WHERE "alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
                AND "last_updated" < '2023-01-01'
        )
),

-- Step 2: Create bounding region from all grid centroids (using ST_ENVELOPE as convex hull is not available)
grid_bounding_region AS (
    SELECT 
        ST_ENVELOPE(
            ST_COLLECT(
                ST_POINT("longitude_centroid", "latitude_centroid")
            )
        ) AS "bounding_geometry"
    FROM recent_singapore_grid
),

-- Step 3: Find hospitals within the bounding region
hospitals_in_region AS (
    SELECT 
        "geometry" AS "hospital_geom",
        "layer_code"
    FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_LAYERS
    WHERE "layer_code" IN (2110, 2120)
        AND ST_INTERSECTS(
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB("geometry"),
            (SELECT "bounding_geometry" FROM grid_bounding_region)
        )
),

-- Step 4: Calculate distance from each grid cell to nearest hospital
grid_with_distances AS (
    SELECT 
        g."geo_id",
        g."population",
        g."longitude_centroid",
        g."latitude_centroid",
        MIN(
            ST_DISTANCE(
                ST_POINT(g."longitude_centroid", g."latitude_centroid"),
                ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."hospital_geom")
            )
        ) AS "distance_to_nearest_hospital"
    FROM recent_singapore_grid g
    CROSS JOIN hospitals_in_region h
    GROUP BY g."geo_id", g."population", g."longitude_centroid", g."latitude_centroid"
),

-- Step 5: Find the grid cell with maximum distance to nearest hospital
farthest_grid_cell AS (
    SELECT 
        "geo_id",
        "population",
        "distance_to_nearest_hospital"
    FROM grid_with_distances
    ORDER BY "distance_to_nearest_hospital" DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 6: Return the population of the farthest grid cell
SELECT 
    "population" AS "total_population_of_farthest_grid_cell",
    "geo_id",
    "distance_to_nearest_hospital"
FROM farthest_grid_cell;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get the most recent population grid data for Singapore before January 2023
-- Use ROW_NUMBER to take the latest update per grid cell
WITH latest_pop AS (
    SELECT
        p."geo_id",
        p."population",
        p."longitude_centroid",
        p."latitude_centroid",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p."geo_id" ORDER BY p."last_updated" DESC) AS rn
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."WORLDPOP"."POPULATION_GRID_1KM" p
    WHERE p."alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
      AND p."last_updated" < '2023-01-01'
),
-- Filter to keep only the latest record for each grid
pop_grid AS (
    SELECT "geo_id", "population", "longitude_centroid", "latitude_centroid"
    FROM latest_pop
    WHERE rn = 1
),
-- Step 2: Compute convex hull of all grid centroids
convex_hull AS (
    SELECT ST_CONVEXHULL(ST_GEOMPOINT("longitude_centroid", "latitude_centroid")) AS hull_geom
    FROM pop_grid
),
-- Step 3: Identify hospitals (layer_code 2110 or 2120) that intersect the convex hull
hospitals AS (
    SELECT
        l."geometry",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(l."geometry") AS hosp_geom
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_LAYERS" l,
         convex_hull ch
    WHERE l."layer_code" IN (2110, 2120)
      AND ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(l."geometry"), ch."hull_geom")
),
-- Step 4: For each grid cell, compute the minimum distance to any hospital
grid_distances AS (
    SELECT
        pg."geo_id",
        pg."population",
        MIN(ST_DISTANCE(
            ST_GEOMPOINT(pg."longitude_centroid", pg."latitude_centroid"),
            h."hosp_geom"
        )) AS min_dist
    FROM pop_grid pg
    CROSS JOIN hospitals h
    GROUP BY pg."geo_id", pg."population"
)
-- Step 5: Find the grid cell farthest from any hospital and output its population
SELECT "population"
FROM grid_distances
ORDER BY "min_dist" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH date_series AS (
    -- Generate all dates from 2018-08-30 to 2018-09-30 (32 days)
    SELECT 
        DATEADD(day, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) - 1, '2018-08-30'::DATE) AS "date"
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 32))
),
contract_creations AS (
    -- Extract successful contract creations with categorization
    SELECT 
        DATEADD('second', "block_timestamp" / 1000000, '1970-01-01'::TIMESTAMP)::DATE AS "creation_date",
        CASE 
            WHEN "trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external'
            ELSE 'internal'
        END AS "creation_type"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_ETHEREUM"."TRACES"
    WHERE "trace_type" = 'create'
        AND "status" = 1  -- Successful creations only
        AND "block_timestamp" >= 1535587200000000  -- 2018-08-30 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
        AND "block_timestamp" < 1538352000000000   -- 2018-10-01 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
),
daily_counts AS (
    -- Count creations per day per type
    SELECT 
        "creation_date" AS "date",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creation_type" = 'external' THEN 1 END) AS "external_daily",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creation_type" = 'internal' THEN 1 END) AS "internal_daily"
    FROM contract_creations
    GROUP BY "creation_date"
)
-- Final cumulative counts
SELECT 
    ds."date",
    COALESCE(SUM(dc."external_daily") OVER (ORDER BY ds."date" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 0) AS "cumulative_external",
    COALESCE(SUM(dc."internal_daily") OVER (ORDER BY ds."date" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 0) AS "cumulative_internal"
FROM date_series ds
LEFT JOIN daily_counts dc ON ds."date" = dc."date"
WHERE ds."date" <= '2018-09-30'::DATE
ORDER BY ds."date";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Generate a complete date spine for the range Aug 30, 2018 to Sep 30, 2018 (32 days)
WITH date_spine AS (
    SELECT
        DATEADD('day', seq.seq, '2018-08-30'::DATE) AS "date"
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 0) - 1 AS seq
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 32))
    ) AS seq
),

-- Identify all successful contract creations in the date range
contract_creations AS (
    SELECT
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("block_timestamp" / 1000000)) AS "date",
        CASE
            WHEN "trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external_user'
            ELSE 'contract'
        END AS "creator_type",
        1 AS "cnt"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRACES
    WHERE "trace_type" = 'create'
      AND "status" = 1
      AND "block_timestamp" >= 1535587200000000   -- Aug 30, 2018 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
      AND "block_timestamp" < 1538352000000000    -- Oct 1, 2018 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds (exclusive)
),

-- Aggregate daily counts per creator type
daily_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ds."date",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cc."creator_type" = 'external_user' THEN cc."cnt" ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "ext_user_created",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cc."creator_type" = 'contract' THEN cc."cnt" ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "contract_created"
    FROM date_spine ds
    LEFT JOIN contract_creations cc
        ON ds."date" = cc."date"
    GROUP BY ds."date"
)

-- Compute cumulative sums ensuring strictly increasing totals
SELECT
    "date",
    SUM("ext_user_created") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS "cumulative_ext_user_created",
    SUM("contract_created") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS "cumulative_contract_created"
FROM daily_counts
ORDER BY "date";
```
</details>

| Xe1LEsU759oVWW5Cw7JGw9Yr2zZnjCS2L9 | pubkeyhash | -441212000000 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH april_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        t."hash" AS "transaction_hash",
        t."inputs" AS "inputs",
        t."outputs" AS "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."TRANSACTIONS" t
    WHERE t."block_timestamp_month" = '2023-04-01'
),

-- Extract all input entries with negative values
input_entries AS (
    SELECT 
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(inp.value:"addresses"::ARRAY, ',') AS "address",
        inp.value:"type"::STRING AS "type",
        -SUM(inp.value:"value"::NUMBER) AS "amount"
    FROM april_transactions t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."inputs") inp
    WHERE inp.value:"addresses" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
),

-- Extract all output entries with positive values
output_entries AS (
    SELECT 
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(outp.value:"addresses"::ARRAY, ',') AS "address",
        outp.value:"type"::STRING AS "type",
        SUM(outp.value:"value"::NUMBER) AS "amount"
    FROM april_transactions t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."outputs") outp
    WHERE outp.value:"addresses" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
),

-- Combine all entries and calculate net balance
combined_balances AS (
    SELECT "address", "type", "amount" FROM input_entries
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "address", "type", "amount" FROM output_entries
),

-- Calculate final balance per address and type
final_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("amount") AS "balance"
    FROM combined_balances
    WHERE "address" IS NOT NULL AND "address" != ''
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
),

-- Find highest and lowest balances
highest_balance AS (
    SELECT "address", "type", "balance"
    FROM final_balances
    ORDER BY "balance" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),

lowest_balance AS (
    SELECT "address", "type", "balance"
    FROM final_balances
    ORDER BY "balance" ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Combine results
SELECT * FROM highest_balance
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM lowest_balance
ORDER BY "balance" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all Dash transactions that occurred in April 2023
WITH "april_transactions" AS (
    SELECT "hash" AS "tx_hash"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2023-04-01'
),

-- Step 2: Extract outputs (credits) with concatenated address and positive value
"output_credits" AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING("addresses", ',') AS "address",
        "value" AS "net_contribution"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."OUTPUTS" o
    JOIN "april_transactions" t ON o."transaction_hash" = t."tx_hash"
),

-- Step 3: Extract inputs (debits) with concatenated address and negative value
"input_debits" AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING("addresses", ',') AS "address",
        -"value" AS "net_contribution"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."INPUTS" i
    JOIN "april_transactions" t ON i."transaction_hash" = t."tx_hash"
),

-- Step 4: Combine credits and debits
"all_movements" AS (
    SELECT "address", "net_contribution" FROM "output_credits"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "address", "net_contribution" FROM "input_debits"
),

-- Step 5: Compute net balance per address (sum of all contributions)
"address_balances" AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        ROUND(SUM("net_contribution"), 4) AS "balance"
    FROM "all_movements"
    GROUP BY "address"
)

-- Step 6: Find the highest and lowest balances across all addresses
SELECT
    MAX("balance") AS "highest_balance",
    MIN("balance") AS "lowest_balance"
FROM "address_balances";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH daily_creations AS (
    -- Extract and categorize daily contract creations
    SELECT
        DATEADD('microsecond', "block_timestamp", '1970-01-01')::DATE AS "creation_date",
        CASE 
            WHEN "trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external'
            ELSE 'contract' 
        END AS "creator_type",
        COUNT(*) AS "daily_count"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_ETHEREUM"."TRACES"
    WHERE "trace_type" = 'create'
        AND "status" = 1
        AND "block_timestamp" >= 1483228800000000  -- 2017-01-01 in microseconds
        AND "block_timestamp" < 1640995200000000   -- 2022-01-01 in microseconds (exclusive)
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
date_series AS (
    -- Generate all dates from 2017-01-01 to 2021-12-31
    SELECT
        DATEADD('day', SEQ4(), '2017-01-01')::DATE AS "date"
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 1826))  -- 1826 days from 2017-01-01 to 2021-12-31 inclusive
),
daily_counts AS (
    -- Join date series with daily creations, filling zeros for missing days
    SELECT
        ds."date",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN dc."creator_type" = 'external' THEN dc."daily_count" END), 0) AS "external_daily",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN dc."creator_type" = 'contract' THEN dc."daily_count" END), 0) AS "contract_daily"
    FROM date_series ds
    LEFT JOIN daily_creations dc ON ds."date" = dc."creation_date"
    GROUP BY ds."date"
    ORDER BY ds."date"
)
-- Compute cumulative sums
SELECT
    "date",
    SUM("external_daily") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS "cumulative_external",
    SUM("contract_daily") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS "cumulative_contract"
FROM daily_counts
ORDER BY "date";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE date_series ("date") AS (
    -- Start date: 2017-01-01
    SELECT DATE('2017-01-01')
    UNION ALL
    -- Recursively add one day until 2021-12-31
    SELECT DATEADD(DAY, 1, "date")
    FROM date_series
    WHERE "date" < DATE('2021-12-31')
),
creations AS (
    -- Extract creation dates and classify each create trace
    SELECT 
        DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."block_timestamp" / 1000000)) AS "creation_date",
        CASE 
            WHEN t."trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external'   -- EOA-created (top-level)
            ELSE 'contract'                                    -- Contract-created (internal)
        END AS "creator_type"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRACES t
    WHERE t."trace_type" = 'create'
      AND t."status" = 1                                      -- Only successful creations
      AND t."block_timestamp" >= 1483228800000000             -- 2017-01-01 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
      AND t."block_timestamp" < 1640995200000000              -- 2022-01-01 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
),
daily_counts AS (
    -- Aggregate new contract creations by date and category
    SELECT 
        "creation_date",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creator_type" = 'external' THEN 1 END) AS "external_created",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creator_type" = 'contract' THEN 1 END) AS "contract_created"
    FROM creations
    GROUP BY "creation_date"
)
SELECT 
    d."date",
    -- Cumulative sum of externally-created contracts (monotonically increasing)
    SUM(COALESCE(dc."external_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."date") AS "external_created_cumulative",
    -- Cumulative sum of contract-created contracts (monotonically increasing)
    SUM(COALESCE(dc."contract_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."date") AS "contract_created_cumulative"
FROM date_series d
LEFT JOIN daily_counts dc 
    ON d."date" = dc."creation_date"
ORDER BY d."date"
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH transaction_period AS (
    SELECT 
        "hash",
        "block_timestamp",
        "inputs",
        "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp" >= 1393632000000000  -- 2014-03-01
        AND "block_timestamp" < 1396310400000000  -- 2014-04-01
        AND "inputs" IS NOT NULL
        AND "outputs" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Extract and flatten inputs (debits/negative)
input_entries AS (
    SELECT 
        t."hash" AS "transaction_hash",
        COALESCE(inp.value:"type"::STRING, 'unknown') AS "address_type",
        addr.value::STRING AS "address",
        -1 * COALESCE(inp.value:"value"::NUMBER, 0) AS "amount"
    FROM transaction_period t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."inputs") inp,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => COALESCE(inp.value:"addresses", PARSE_JSON('["unknown"]'))) addr
    WHERE inp.value:"value" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Extract and flatten outputs (credits/positive)
output_entries AS (
    SELECT 
        t."hash" AS "transaction_hash",
        COALESCE(out.value:"type"::STRING, 'unknown') AS "address_type",
        addr.value::STRING AS "address",
        COALESCE(out.value:"value"::NUMBER, 0) AS "amount"
    FROM transaction_period t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."outputs") out,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => COALESCE(out.value:"addresses", PARSE_JSON('["unknown"]'))) addr
    WHERE out.value:"value" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Combine all entries
all_entries AS (
    SELECT "address", "address_type", "amount" FROM input_entries
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "address", "address_type", "amount" FROM output_entries
),

-- Calculate final balance per address and type
address_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        "address",
        "address_type",
        SUM("amount") AS "final_balance"
    FROM all_entries
    WHERE "address" != 'unknown'
    GROUP BY "address", "address_type"
)

-- Group by address type and find max/min final balances
SELECT 
    "address_type",
    MAX("final_balance") AS "max_final_balance",
    MIN("final_balance") AS "min_final_balance",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "address") AS "unique_addresses"
FROM address_balances
WHERE "address_type" IS NOT NULL
    AND "address_type" != 'unknown'
GROUP BY "address_type"
ORDER BY "address_type";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter transactions within March 2014 (block_timestamp_month represents the month)
filtered_txns AS (
    SELECT
        "hash",
        "inputs",
        "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2014-03-01'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest inputs as debits (negative values)
-- Each input entry represents money spent FROM an address
input_entries AS (
    SELECT
        f."hash",
        inp.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        inp.value:"type"::STRING     AS "type",
        -inp.value:"value"::NUMBER   AS "balance_change"   -- debit = negative
    FROM filtered_txns f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."inputs") inp
),

-- Step 3: Unnest outputs as credits (positive values)
-- Each output entry represents money received BY an address
output_entries AS (
    SELECT
        f."hash",
        out.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        out.value:"type"::STRING     AS "type",
        out.value:"value"::NUMBER    AS "balance_change"   -- credit = positive
    FROM filtered_txns f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."outputs") out
),

-- Step 4: Combine all balance changes from inputs and outputs
all_entries AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_entries
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_entries
),

-- Step 5: Compute final balance per address (and its associated type)
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("balance_change") AS "final_balance"
    FROM all_entries
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)

-- Step 6: Group by address type to get max and min final balances
SELECT
    "type"            AS "address_type",
    MAX("final_balance") AS "max_balance",
    MIN("final_balance") AS "min_balance"
FROM address_balances
GROUP BY "type"
ORDER BY "type";
```
</details>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH bnb_token AS (
  SELECT 
    "address",
    TRY_CAST("decimals" AS NUMERIC) AS "decimals"
  FROM "ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN"."ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN"."TOKENS"
  WHERE LOWER("symbol") = 'bnb'
  LIMIT 1
),
transfers AS (
  SELECT 
    "from_address",
    "to_address",
    TRY_CAST("value" AS NUMERIC) AS "value_num"
  FROM "ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN"."ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN"."TOKEN_TRANSFERS"
  WHERE "token_address" = (SELECT "address" FROM bnb_token)
    AND "from_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
    AND "to_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
),
address_net AS (
  SELECT 
    "address",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "direction" = 'in' THEN "value_num" ELSE -"value_num" END) AS "net_balance"
  FROM (
    SELECT "to_address" AS "address", "value_num", 'in' AS "direction"
    FROM transfers
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "from_address" AS "address", "value_num", 'out' AS "direction"
    FROM transfers
  ) t
  GROUP BY "address"
)
SELECT 
  SUM("net_balance") / POWER(10, COALESCE((SELECT "decimals" FROM bnb_token), 18)) AS "total_circulating_supply"
FROM address_net
WHERE "net_balance" > 0;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the BNB token contract address
WITH bnb_token AS (
    SELECT "address"
    FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKENS
    WHERE LOWER("symbol") = LOWER('BNB')
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: Get all token transfers for BNB, excluding zero-address transactions
valid_transfers AS (
    SELECT
        "from_address",
        "to_address",
        TRY_CAST("value" AS DOUBLE) AS "transfer_value"
    FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
    WHERE "token_address" = (SELECT "address" FROM bnb_token)
      -- Exclude transactions where sender or receiver is the zero address
      AND "from_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
      AND "to_address"   != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
),

-- Step 3: Compute total received per address
received AS (
    SELECT "to_address" AS "address", SUM("transfer_value") AS "total_received"
    FROM valid_transfers
    GROUP BY "to_address"
),

-- Step 4: Compute total sent per address
sent AS (
    SELECT "from_address" AS "address", SUM("transfer_value") AS "total_sent"
    FROM valid_transfers
    GROUP BY "from_address"
),

-- Step 5: Combine to get net balance per address
balances AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(r."address", s."address") AS "address",
        COALESCE(r."total_received", 0) - COALESCE(s."total_sent", 0) AS "balance"
    FROM received r
    FULL OUTER JOIN sent s
        ON r."address" = s."address"
)

-- Step 6: Sum all positive (non-zero) balances, divide by 10^18 for decimal adjustment
SELECT SUM("balance") / 1e18 AS "total_circulating_supply"
FROM balances
WHERE "balance" > 0;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Find all GHCN stations within 50km of NYC that have valid PRCP data in 2016
stations_with_data AS (
  SELECT 
    s.id AS station_id,
    s.name AS station_name,
    s.latitude,
    s.longitude,
    ST_DISTANCE(
      ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude),
      ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
    ) AS distance_meters
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` s
  WHERE ST_DISTANCE(
    ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
  ) <= 50000
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_2016` d
    WHERE d.id = s.id
      AND d.element = 'PRCP'
      AND d.value IS NOT NULL
      -- Allow blank (space) or NULL flags to indicate unflagged data
      AND (d.qflag IS NULL OR d.qflag = ' ' OR d.qflag = '')
      AND (d.mflag IS NULL OR d.mflag = ' ' OR d.mflag = '')
  )
),

-- Pick the nearest station among those with data
nearest_station AS (
  SELECT station_id, station_name, latitude, longitude, distance_meters
  FROM stations_with_data
  ORDER BY distance_meters
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Daily precipitation from the nearest station (2016)
daily_precipitation AS (
  SELECT 
    d.date,
    d.value / 10.0 AS precipitation_mm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_2016` d
  INNER JOIN nearest_station ns ON d.id = ns.station_id
  WHERE d.element = 'PRCP'
    AND d.value IS NOT NULL
    AND (d.qflag IS NULL OR d.qflag = ' ' OR d.qflag = '')
    AND (d.mflag IS NULL OR d.mflag = ' ' OR d.mflag = '')
),

-- Categorize days as rainy (>5mm) or non-rainy
weather_categories AS (
  SELECT 
    date,
    CASE 
      WHEN precipitation_mm > 5 THEN 'rainy'
      ELSE 'non-rainy'
    END AS weather_category
  FROM daily_precipitation
),

-- Daily Citibike trips in 2016
daily_citibike_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(starttime) AS trip_date,
    COUNT(*) AS daily_trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
    AND starttime IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY trip_date
)

-- Final comparison
SELECT 
  wc.weather_category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dct.trip_date) AS number_of_days,
  ROUND(AVG(dct.daily_trip_count), 2) AS avg_daily_trips,
  ROUND(MIN(dct.daily_trip_count), 2) AS min_daily_trips,
  ROUND(MAX(dct.daily_trip_count), 2) AS max_daily_trips
FROM daily_citibike_trips dct
INNER JOIN weather_categories wc ON dct.trip_date = wc.date
GROUP BY wc.weather_category
ORDER BY wc.weather_category;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the nearest GHCN station within 50 km of Times Square
WITH nearest_station AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations`
  WHERE ST_DISTANCE(
    ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
  ) <= 50000
  ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE(
    ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
  )
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: Get daily precipitation for that station in 2016 (valid, unflagged)
precipitation AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(g.date) AS dt,
    g.value / 10.0 AS prcp_mm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_all` g
  JOIN nearest_station n ON g.id = n.id
  WHERE g.element = 'PRCP'
    AND g.date BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31'
    AND (g.qflag IS NULL OR g.qflag = '')   -- quality flag absent
    AND (g.mflag IS NULL OR g.mflag = '')   -- measurement flag absent
    AND g.value IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 3: Daily CitiBike trip counts in 2016
daily_trips AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(starttime) AS trip_date,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
  WHERE starttime >= '2016-01-01' AND starttime < '2017-01-01'
  GROUP BY trip_date
)

-- Step 4: Classify days, compute average trips per category
SELECT
  CASE WHEN p.prcp_mm > 5 THEN 'Rainy' ELSE 'Non-Rainy' END AS day_category,
  AVG(COALESCE(d.trip_count, 0)) AS avg_daily_trips
FROM precipitation p
LEFT JOIN daily_trips d ON p.dt = d.trip_date
GROUP BY day_category
ORDER BY day_category;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH species_1995_counts AS (
  -- Count living trees per species in 1995
  SELECT 
    UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) AS scientific_name_upper,
    COUNT(*) AS living_count_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995` t95
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = UPPER(t95.spc_latin)
  WHERE 
    -- Filter out dead trees in 1995
    -- Based on sample data, status has values like 'Good', 'Poor'
    -- We'll exclude any rows where status indicates death
    LOWER(t95.status) NOT LIKE '%dead%'
  GROUP BY 1
),
species_2015_counts AS (
  -- Count living trees per species in 2015
  SELECT 
    UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) AS scientific_name_upper,
    COUNT(*) AS living_count_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_2015` t15
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = UPPER(t15.spc_latin)
  WHERE 
    -- Filter for alive trees in 2015
    -- Based on schema, status column indicates if tree is alive, dead, or stump
    LOWER(t15.status) = 'alive'
  GROUP BY 1
),
species_differences AS (
  -- Calculate difference per species (1995 - 2015)
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(s95.scientific_name_upper, s15.scientific_name_upper) AS scientific_name_upper,
    COALESCE(s95.living_count_1995, 0) AS living_count_1995,
    COALESCE(s15.living_count_2015, 0) AS living_count_2015,
    COALESCE(s95.living_count_1995, 0) - COALESCE(s15.living_count_2015, 0) AS count_difference
  FROM species_1995_counts s95
  FULL OUTER JOIN species_2015_counts s15
    ON s95.scientific_name_upper = s15.scientific_name_upper
)
-- Final aggregation by fall color
SELECT 
  ts.fall_color,
  SUM(sd.count_difference) AS total_change_in_living_trees
FROM species_differences sd
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
  ON sd.scientific_name_upper = UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name)
WHERE ts.fall_color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ts.fall_color
ORDER BY total_change_in_living_trees DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Count trees NOT marked as dead in 1995 per species
WITH counts_1995 AS (
  SELECT 
    spc_latin,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995`
  WHERE IFNULL(status, '') != 'Dead'
  GROUP BY spc_latin
),

-- CTE: Count trees marked as Alive in 2015 per species
counts_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    spc_latin,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_2015`
  WHERE status = 'Alive'
  GROUP BY spc_latin
),

-- CTE: Compute difference per species matched via uppercase scientific name
species_diff AS (
  SELECT 
    ts.species_scientific_name,
    ts.fall_color,
    COALESCE(c95.cnt_1995, 0) - COALESCE(c15.cnt_2015, 0) AS tree_count_change
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
  LEFT JOIN counts_1995 c95
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = c95.spc_latin
  LEFT JOIN counts_2015 c15
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = c15.spc_latin
)

-- Final: Group by fall_color and sum the changes
SELECT 
  fall_color,
  SUM(tree_count_change) AS total_change
FROM species_diff
WHERE fall_color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY fall_color
ORDER BY fall_color;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH trip_data AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', start_date) AS year_month,
    ROUND(duration_sec / 60.0, 2) AS duration_minutes,
    start_date,
    trip_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
  WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL 
    AND duration_sec IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  year_month,
  -- First trip duration
  MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN duration_minutes END) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
  -- Last trip duration
  MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN duration_minutes END) AS last_trip_duration_minutes,
  -- Highest trip duration
  MAX(duration_minutes) AS highest_trip_duration_minutes,
  -- Lowest trip duration
  MIN(duration_minutes) AS lowest_trip_duration_minutes
FROM (
  SELECT 
    year_month,
    duration_minutes,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year_month ORDER BY start_date, trip_id) AS rn_asc,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year_month ORDER BY start_date DESC, trip_id DESC) AS rn_desc
  FROM trip_data
) ranked
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE 1: Extract year-month key and convert seconds to minutes
WITH year_month_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', start_date) AS year_month,
    start_date,
    duration_sec / 60.0 AS duration_min
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
),
-- CTE 2: Rank trips within each year-month by start date chronologically
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    year_month,
    duration_min,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
    ) AS rn_first,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date DESC
    ) AS rn_last
  FROM year_month_trips
)
-- Final aggregation: first, last, highest, lowest duration per year-month
SELECT 
  year_month,
  MAX(CASE WHEN rn_first = 1 THEN duration_min END) AS first_trip_duration_min,
  MAX(CASE WHEN rn_last = 1 THEN duration_min END) AS last_trip_duration_min,
  MAX(duration_min) AS highest_trip_duration_min,
  MIN(duration_min) AS lowest_trip_duration_min
FROM ranked
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH berkeley_stations AS (
  -- Identify all stations in Berkeley by name pattern
  SELECT 
    station_id,
    name,
    station_geom
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info`
  WHERE LOWER(name) LIKE '%berkeley%'
),

qualifying_trips AS (
  -- Get trips that start OR end in Berkeley with distance > 1000m
  SELECT 
    t.trip_id,
    t.duration_sec,
    -- Calculate distance between start and end stations in meters
    ST_DISTANCE(t.start_station_geom, t.end_station_geom) AS distance_meters,
    -- Calculate speed: distance (m) / time (s)
    ST_DISTANCE(t.start_station_geom, t.end_station_geom) / t.duration_sec AS speed_m_per_s
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` t
  WHERE 
    -- Ensure we have valid duration and geometry data
    t.duration_sec > 0
    AND t.start_station_geom IS NOT NULL
    AND t.end_station_geom IS NOT NULL
    -- Trip must start OR end in Berkeley
    -- CAST station_id to STRING for comparison since bikeshare_station_info.station_id is STRING
    AND (
      CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING) IN (SELECT station_id FROM berkeley_stations)
      OR CAST(t.end_station_id AS STRING) IN (SELECT station_id FROM berkeley_stations)
    )
)

-- Get the highest average speed, rounded to 1 decimal
SELECT 
  ROUND(MAX(speed_m_per_s), 1) AS highest_avg_speed_m_per_s
FROM qualifying_trips
WHERE 
  -- Filter for trips longer than 1000 meters
  distance_meters > 1000
  -- Additional safety check for valid speed calculation
  AND speed_m_per_s IS NOT NULL
  AND speed_m_per_s > 0;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Query to find highest average speed for Berkeley bike trips with distance > 1000m
WITH berkeley_trips AS (
  SELECT
    trip_id,
    duration_sec,
    -- Calculate distance in meters between start and end stations using geospatial function
    ST_DISTANCE(start_station_geom, end_station_geom) AS distance_m
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
  WHERE
    -- Both start and end stations must be in Berkeley to qualify as "trips in Berkeley"
    (LOWER(start_station_name) LIKE '%berkeley%' AND LOWER(end_station_name) LIKE '%berkeley%')
    AND duration_sec > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
)
SELECT
  -- Highest average speed = max(distance / time), rounded to 1 decimal as requested
  ROUND(MAX(distance_m / duration_sec), 1) AS highest_avg_speed_m_s
FROM
  berkeley_trips
WHERE
  distance_m > 1000  -- Only trips with distance > 1000 meters
```
</details>

```sql
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE()) - ft."member_birth_year" BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'

LEFT JOIN "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO" si
```

```sql
WITH filtered_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        t."trip_id",
        t."duration_sec",

        t."start_station_name",
        t."start_station_name" || ' - ' || t."end_station_name" AS "route",
        t."bike_number",
        t."subscriber_type",
        t."member_birth_year",
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") AS "age",
        CASE 
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
            ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
        END AS "age_class",
        t."member_gender",
        t."start_station_id"
    FROM SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_TRIPS t
    WHERE 
        t."start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" != 'None'
        AND TO_TIMESTAMP(t."start_date" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2017-07-01'::TIMESTAMP AND '2017-12-31 23:59:59'::TIMESTAMP
),
trips_with_region AS (
    SELECT 
        f."trip_id",
        f."duration_sec",
        f."start_date",
        f."start_station_name",
        f."route",
        f."bike_number",
        f."subscriber_type",
        f."member_birth_year",
        f."age",
        f."age_class",
        f."member_gender",
        r."name" AS "region_name"
    FROM filtered_trips f
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO si
        ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS VARCHAR) = si."station_id"
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_REGIONS r
        ON si."region_id" = r."region_id"
)
SELECT 
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    "start_date",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "age",
    "age_class",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM trips_with_region
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH session_durations AS (
    SELECT 
        "session_id",
        MIN("browser") AS "browser",
        (MAX("created_at") - MIN("created_at")) / 1000000 AS duration_seconds
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."EVENTS"
    GROUP BY "session_id"
)
SELECT 
    "browser",
    ROUND(AVG(duration_seconds), 2) AS avg_session_duration
FROM session_durations
GROUP BY "browser"
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
ORDER BY avg_session_duration ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "session_durations" AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate duration (in seconds) for each session within each browser
    SELECT 
        "browser",
        "session_id",
        (MAX("created_at") - MIN("created_at")) / 1000000.0 AS "session_duration_seconds"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."EVENTS"
    GROUP BY "browser", "session_id"
),
"browser_stats" AS (
    -- Step 2: Aggregate by browser: average session duration + session count
    SELECT 
        "browser",
        AVG("session_duration_seconds") AS "avg_session_duration",
        COUNT("session_id") AS "total_sessions"
    FROM "session_durations"
    GROUP BY "browser"
    HAVING COUNT("session_id") > 10   -- Only browsers with more than 10 sessions
)
-- Step 3: Get the 3 browsers with the shortest average session duration
SELECT 
    "browser",
    ROUND("avg_session_duration", 4) AS "avg_session_duration"
FROM "browser_stats"
ORDER BY "avg_session_duration" ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_users AS (
    SELECT 
        "id",
        "age",
        "gender",
        "created_at"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE 
        "created_at" >= 1546300800000000  -- 2019-01-01 00:00:00 in microseconds
        AND "created_at" <= 1651363199999999  -- 2022-04-30 23:59:59.999999 in microseconds
        AND "gender" IN ('M', 'F')
),

gender_age_bounds AS (
    SELECT 
        "gender",
        MIN("age") AS "min_age",
        MAX("age") AS "max_age"
    FROM filtered_users
    GROUP BY "gender"
),

age_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        "gender",
        "age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "id") AS "user_count"
    FROM filtered_users
    GROUP BY "gender", "age"
)

SELECT 
    ac."gender",
    CASE 
        WHEN ac."age" = gab."min_age" THEN 'youngest'
        WHEN ac."age" = gab."max_age" THEN 'oldest'
    END AS "age_group",
    ac."age",
    ac."user_count"
FROM age_counts ac
INNER JOIN gender_age_bounds gab
    ON ac."gender" = gab."gender"
WHERE ac."age" = gab."min_age" OR ac."age" = gab."max_age"
ORDER BY ac."gender", "age_group";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: users who signed up in the specified date range
WITH filtered_users AS (
    SELECT 
        "id",
        "gender",
        "age"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE "gender" IN ('M', 'F')  -- only male and female as requested
      AND TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000) >= '2019-01-01'
      AND TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000) <= '2022-04-30'
),

-- CTE: minimum and maximum age per gender
age_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        "gender",
        MIN("age") AS min_age,
        MAX("age") AS max_age
    FROM filtered_users
    GROUP BY "gender"
),

-- CTE: count of users with the minimum age per gender
youngest AS (
    SELECT 
        f."gender",
        'youngest' AS age_group,
        a.min_age AS age,
        COUNT(DISTINCT f."id") AS user_count
    FROM filtered_users f
    JOIN age_stats a 
        ON f."gender" = a."gender" AND f."age" = a.min_age
    GROUP BY f."gender", a.min_age
),

-- CTE: count of users with the maximum age per gender
oldest AS (
    SELECT 
        f."gender",
        'oldest' AS age_group,
        a.max_age AS age,
        COUNT(DISTINCT f."id") AS user_count
    FROM filtered_users f
    JOIN age_stats a 
        ON f."gender" = a."gender" AND f."age" = a.max_age
    GROUP BY f."gender", a.max_age
)

-- Combine results
SELECT * FROM youngest
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM oldest
ORDER BY "gender", age_group;
```
</details>

```sql
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE "created_at" >= 1546300800000000
      AND "created_at" < 1577836800000000
),

-- Step 2: Non-cancelled orders made in 2019
orders_2019 AS (
    SELECT "order_id", "user_id", "num_of_item"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."ORDERS"
    WHERE "created_at" >= 1546300800000000
      AND "created_at" < 1577836800000000
      AND "status" != 'Cancelled'
),

-- Step 3: Compute the total value of each order
order_values AS (
    SELECT 
        o."order_id",
        o."user_id",
        SUM(oi."sale_price") AS order_total
    FROM orders_2019 o
    INNER JOIN "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."ORDER_ITEMS" oi
        ON o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    WHERE oi."status" != 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY o."order_id", o."user_id"
),

-- Step 4: Compute average order value per user
user_avg_order_value AS (
    SELECT 
        ov."user_id",
        ROUND(SUM(ov."order_total") / COUNT(ov."order_id"), 4) AS avg_order_value
    FROM order_values ov
    GROUP BY ov."user_id"
)

-- Step 5: Get top 10 users by average order value
SELECT 
    u."email"
FROM user_avg_order_value um
INNER JOIN users_2019 u
    ON um."user_id" = u."id"
ORDER BY um."avg_order_value" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>
