<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| reference_sequence_name          |   variant_density |   total_variants |   length |
|:---------------------------------|------------------:|-----------------:|---------:|
| gi|1098476186|gb|MNPR01010508.1| |          0.005888 |               17 |     2887 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH variant_counts AS (
    -- Count variants from first transcriptome table
    SELECT 
        "reference_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "variant_count"
    FROM "GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."MNPR01_TRANSCRIPTOME_201703"
    GROUP BY "reference_name"
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Count variants from second variant table
    SELECT 
        "reference_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "variant_count"
    FROM "GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."MNPR01_201703"
    GROUP BY "reference_name"
),
aggregated_variants AS (
    -- Aggregate counts from both tables
    SELECT 
        "reference_name",
        SUM("variant_count") AS "total_variants"
    FROM variant_counts
    GROUP BY "reference_name"
),
density_calculation AS (
    -- Calculate variant density by joining with reference lengths
    SELECT 
        av."reference_name",
        ref."name",
        ref."length",
        av."total_variants",
        -- Calculate density: variants per base pair, handle division by zero
        CASE 
            WHEN ref."length" > 0 
            THEN ROUND(av."total_variants"::FLOAT / ref."length", 6)
            ELSE 0 
        END AS "variant_density",
        -- Add window function for ranking
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY CASE 
            WHEN ref."length" > 0 
            THEN av."total_variants"::FLOAT / ref."length" 
            ELSE 0 
        END DESC) AS density_rank
    FROM aggregated_variants av
    JOIN "GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."GENOMICS_CANNABIS"."MNPR01_REFERENCE_201703" ref
        ON av."reference_name" = ref."name"
)
-- Return the reference sequence with highest density
SELECT 
    "reference_name" AS "reference_sequence_name",
    "variant_density",
    "total_variants",
    "length"
FROM density_calculation
WHERE density_rank = 1
ORDER BY "variant_density" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT 
    r."name" AS "reference_sequence_name"
FROM 
    GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703 v
    INNER JOIN GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_REFERENCE_201703 r
        ON v."reference_name" = r."name"
GROUP BY 
    r."name",
    r."length"
ORDER BY 
    COUNT(*) / r."length" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH under_25 AS (
  -- Sum population for ages 0 through 24 across both sexes per country in 2017
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    year,
    SUM(
      COALESCE(population_age_0, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_1, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_2, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_3, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_4, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_5, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_6, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_7, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_8, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_9, 0) +

      COALESCE(population_age_16, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_17, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_18, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_19, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_20, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_21, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_22, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_23, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_24, 0)
    ) AS population_under_25
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_age_sex`
  WHERE year = 2017
  GROUP BY country_name, year
),
total_pop AS (
  -- Get total midyear population for each country in 2017
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    year,
    midyear_population AS total_population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population`
  WHERE year = 2017
)
SELECT 
  u.country_name
FROM under_25 u
JOIN total_pop t 
  ON u.country_name = t.country_name AND u.year = t.year
ORDER BY 
  (u.population_under_25 / t.total_population) * 100 DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH country_stats AS (
  -- Step 1: Aggregate COVID-19 data by country for May 10, 2020
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    SUM(cumulative_confirmed) AS total_confirmed,
    SUM(cumulative_recovered) AS total_recovered
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
  WHERE date = DATE('2020-05-10')
    AND country_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY country_name
  HAVING SUM(cumulative_confirmed) > 50000  -- Filter countries with >50k cases
),
recovery_rates AS (
  -- Step 2: Calculate recovery rate percentage for each country
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    total_confirmed,
    total_recovered,
    -- Calculate recovery rate safely (handle NULL/zero denominator)
    ROUND(
      SAFE_DIVIDE(total_recovered, total_confirmed) * 100, 
      2
    ) AS recovery_rate_percent
  FROM country_stats
  WHERE total_confirmed > 0  -- Ensure valid denominator
)
-- Step 3: Get top 3 countries by recovery rate
SELECT 
  country_name,
  recovery_rate_percent
FROM recovery_rates
WHERE recovery_rate_percent IS NOT NULL  -- Exclude countries with no recovery data
ORDER BY recovery_rate_percent DESC  -- Highest recovery rates first
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE date = '2020-05-10'
  AND subregion1_code IS NULL
  AND subregion2_code IS NULL
  AND locality_code IS NULL
  AND cumulative_confirmed > 50000
  AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
  AND cumulative_recovered IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY recovery_rate_percentage DESC
LIMIT 3
```

```sql
WITH population_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    value AS population_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  WHERE 
    indicator_code = 'SP.POP.TOTL' 
    AND year = 2018
    AND value IS NOT NULL
),

covid_cases_june_2020 AS (
  SELECT 
    country_code,
    country_name,
    MAX(cumulative_confirmed) AS total_confirmed_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
  WHERE 
    date <= '2020-06-30'
    AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
    AND country_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY country_code, country_name
)

SELECT 
  c.country_code,
  c.country_name,
  p.population_2018,
  c.total_confirmed_cases,
  ROUND(
    (c.total_confirmed_cases * 100.0 / NULLIF(p.population_2018, 0)), 
    4
  ) AS infection_percentage
FROM covid_cases_june_2020 c
LEFT JOIN population_2018 p
  ON UPPER(TRIM(c.country_name)) = UPPER(TRIM(p.country_name))
WHERE p.population_2018 IS NOT NULL
  AND c.total_confirmed_cases > 0
ORDER BY infection_percentage DESC;
```

```sql
WITH

    SELECT
      country_code,
      country_name,
      SUM(cumulative_confirmed) AS total_confirmed
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
    WHERE date = '2020-06-30'
      AND country_code IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY country_code, country_name
  ),
  country_mapping AS (
    SELECT
      country_code AS wb_3_code,
      two_alpha_code
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.country_summary`
  ),
  population_data AS (
    SELECT
      country_code,
      year_2018
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
    WHERE year_2018 IS NOT NULL
  )
SELECT
  c.country_name,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(c.total_confirmed * 100.0, p.year_2018), 4) AS percentage_confirmed
FROM covid_agg c
LEFT JOIN country_mapping m ON c.country_code = m.two_alpha_code
LEFT JOIN population_data p ON m.wb_3_code = p.country_code
ORDER BY c.country_name;  -- optional, for readability
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH cases AS (
  SELECT 
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE country_or_region IN ('United States', 'France', 'China', 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Germany', 'Iran')
    AND _4_20_20 IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),
population AS (
  SELECT 
    short_name,
    SAFE_CAST(latest_population_census AS INT64) AS population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary`
  WHERE short_name IN ('United States', 'France', 'China', 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Germany', 'Iran')
    AND latest_population_census != 'None'
    AND latest_population_census IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  c.country_or_region,
  c.total_cases,
  p.population,
  ROUND((c.total_cases / p.population) * 100000, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM cases c
JOIN population p
  ON c.country_or_region = p.short_name
ORDER BY c.country_or_region;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Aggregate confirmed cases for the target countries as of April 20, 2020
WITH confirmed_agg AS (
  SELECT
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE country_or_region IN ('United States', 'France', 'China', 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Germany', 'Iran')
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),

-- CTE: Manual mapping from country names in the COVID data to World Bank short names
country_mapping AS (
  SELECT 'United States' AS covid_name, 'United States' AS wb_short_name UNION ALL
  SELECT 'France', 'France' UNION ALL
  SELECT 'China', 'China' UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Italy', 'Italy' UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Spain', 'Spain' UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Germany', 'Germany' UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Iran', 'Iran, Islamic Rep.'
),

-- CTE: Get World Bank country codes for the target countries
country_info AS (
  SELECT
    m.covid_name,
    cs.country_code
  FROM country_mapping m
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary` cs
    ON cs.short_name = m.wb_short_name
),

-- CTE: Sum all 2020 population entries per country (World Bank data)
population_agg AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    SUM(population) AS total_population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.population`
  WHERE year = 2020
  GROUP BY country_code
)

-- Final query: join and compute cases per 100,000 people
SELECT
  ca.country_or_region AS country,
  ca.total_cases,
  ROUND(ca.total_cases * 100000.0 / pa.total_population, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM confirmed_agg ca
INNER JOIN country_info ci ON ca.country_or_region = ci.covid_name
LEFT JOIN population_agg pa ON ci.country_code = pa.country_code
ORDER BY country;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH state_daily_new_cases AS (
  -- Calculate daily new cases for each state
  SELECT 
    date,
    state_name,
    confirmed_cases,
    LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS prev_cases,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
    AND confirmed_cases IS NOT NULL
),

state_daily_ranks AS (
  -- Rank states by daily new cases for each day
  SELECT 
    date,
    state_name,
    daily_new_cases,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS daily_rank
  FROM state_daily_new_cases
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL
    AND daily_new_cases >= 0  -- Filter out negative values (data corrections)
),

state_top5_daily AS (
  -- Get top 5 states for each day
  SELECT 
    date,
    state_name,
    daily_new_cases,
    daily_rank
  FROM state_daily_ranks
  WHERE daily_rank <= 5
),

state_appearance_counts AS (
  -- Count how many times each state appears in daily top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT date) AS days_in_top5
  FROM state_top5_daily
  GROUP BY state_name
),

state_ranking AS (
  -- Rank states by appearance count
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    appearance_count,
    days_in_top5,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY appearance_count DESC, state_name) AS state_rank
  FROM state_appearance_counts
),

fourth_state AS (
  -- Identify the 4th ranked state
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    appearance_count,
    days_in_top5
  FROM state_ranking
  WHERE state_rank = 4
),

-- Now analyze counties within the 4th state
county_daily_new_cases AS (
  -- Calculate daily new cases for each county in the 4th state
  SELECT 
    c.date,
    c.state_name,
    c.county,
    c.confirmed_cases,
    LAG(c.confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY c.state_name, c.county ORDER BY c.date) AS prev_cases,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY c.state_name, c.county ORDER BY c.date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  INNER JOIN fourth_state fs ON c.state_name = fs.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
    AND c.confirmed_cases IS NOT NULL
),

county_daily_ranks AS (
  -- Rank counties within the state by daily new cases
  SELECT 
    date,
    state_name,
    county,
    daily_new_cases,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS daily_rank
  FROM county_daily_new_cases
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL
    AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),

county_top5_daily AS (
  -- Get top 5 counties for each day
  SELECT 
    date,
    state_name,
    county,
    daily_new_cases,
    daily_rank
  FROM county_daily_ranks
  WHERE daily_rank <= 5
),

county_appearance_counts AS (
  -- Count how many times each county appears in daily top 5
  SELECT 
    county,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT date) AS days_in_top5,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, county) AS county_rank
  FROM county_top5_daily
  GROUP BY county
)

-- Final results: State ranking and top counties for 4th state
SELECT 
  -- State ranking summary
  (SELECT state_name FROM fourth_state) AS fourth_state_name,
  (SELECT appearance_count FROM fourth_state) AS state_appearance_count,
  (SELECT days_in_top5 FROM fourth_state) AS state_days_in_top5,
  
  -- Top 5 counties in the 4th state
  county,
  appearance_count AS county_appearance_count,
  days_in_top5 AS county_days_in_top5,
  county_rank
FROM county_appearance_counts
WHERE county_rank <= 5
ORDER BY county_rank;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH state_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 1: Compute daily new confirmed cases per state
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
state_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 2: Rank states by daily new cases per day, keep top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM state_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
state_top5_daily AS (
  -- Keep only the top 5 states for each day based on daily new cases
  SELECT state_name, date
  FROM state_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
state_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 3: Count how many times each state appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM state_top5_daily
  GROUP BY state_name
),
state_overall_rank AS (
  -- Step 4: Rank states by their appearance frequency (highest first)
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    appearance_count,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY appearance_count DESC) AS overall_rank
  FROM state_appearance_freq
),
target_state AS (
  -- Step 5: Identify the state that ranks 4th overall
  SELECT state_name FROM state_overall_rank WHERE overall_rank = 4
),
county_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 6: Compute daily new confirmed cases per county for the target state only
  SELECT 
    c.county,
    c.state_name,
    c.date,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY c.county, c.state_name ORDER BY c.date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  INNER JOIN target_state t ON c.state_name = t.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
county_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 7: Rank counties by daily new cases per day
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM county_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
county_top5_daily AS (
  -- Step 8: Keep only the top 5 counties for each day
  SELECT county, state_name, date
  FROM county_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
county_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 9: Count how many times each county appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM county_top5_daily
  GROUP BY county, state_name
)
-- Step 10: Return the top 5 counties by appearance frequency
SELECT 
  county,
  appearance_count
FROM county_appearance_freq
ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
LIMIT 5
```
</details>

### 54. bq087 (DB: `covid19_symptom_search`)
**Question**: Please calculate the overall percentage change in the average weekly search frequency for the symptom 'Anosmia' across the five New York City counties—Bronx County, Queens County, Kings County, New York County, and Richmond County—by comparing the combined data from January 1, 2019, through December 31, 2019, with the combined data from January 1, 2020, through December 31, 2020.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   (T2.AVG_FREQ_2020 - T1.AVG_FREQ_2019) * 100 / T1.AVG_FREQ_2019 |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
|                                                          573.452 |

**OR**

|   percentage_change |
|--------------------:|
|             575.186 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   avg_weekly_frequency_2019 |   avg_weekly_frequency_2020 |   percentage_change |
|----------------------------:|----------------------------:|--------------------:|
|                      0.0531 |                      0.3577 |             573.452 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH yearly_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', date)) AS year,
    AVG(SAFE_CAST(symptom_Anosmia AS FLOAT64)) AS avg_freq
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_weekly`
  WHERE sub_region_1_code = 'US-NY'
    AND sub_region_2 IN (
      'Bronx County', 'Queens County', 'Kings County', 
      'New York County', 'Richmond County'
    )
    AND ((date >= '2019-01-01' AND date <= '2019-12-31')
         OR (date >= '2020-01-01' AND date <= '2020-12-31'))
    AND symptom_Anosmia IS NOT NULL
    AND symptom_Anosmia != 'None'
  GROUP BY year
  HAVING year IN (2019, 2020)
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN avg_freq END), 4) AS avg_weekly_frequency_2019,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN avg_freq END), 4) AS avg_weekly_frequency_2020,
  ROUND(
    ((MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN avg_freq END) - 
      MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN avg_freq END)) / 
     MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN avg_freq END)) * 100, 
    4
  ) AS percentage_change
FROM yearly_stats;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
  -- Weekly Anosmia values for the 5 NYC counties in 2019
  data_2019 AS (
    SELECT SAFE_CAST(symptom_anosmia AS FLOAT64) AS value
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_1_weekly`
    WHERE country_region = 'United States'
      AND sub_region_2 IN ('Bronx County', 'Queens County', 'Kings County', 'New York County', 'Richmond County')
      AND date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
      AND symptom_anosmia != 'None'
      AND symptom_anosmia IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- Weekly Anosmia values for the same counties in 2020
  data_2020 AS (
    SELECT SAFE_CAST(symptom_anosmia AS FLOAT64) AS value
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_1_weekly`
    WHERE country_region = 'United States'
      AND sub_region_2 IN ('Bronx County', 'Queens County', 'Kings County', 'New York County', 'Richmond County')
      AND date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
      AND symptom_anosmia != 'None'
      AND symptom_anosmia IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- Averages for each year
  avgs AS (
    SELECT
      (SELECT AVG(value) FROM data_2019) AS avg_2019,
      (SELECT AVG(value) FROM data_2020) AS avg_2020
  )
-- Percentage change
SELECT 
  ROUND((avg_2020 - avg_2019) / avg_2019 * 100, 4) AS percentage_change
FROM avgs;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH california_population AS (
  -- Get population for California counties from 2018 5-year ACS

    geo_id AS county_fips,
    population_1_year_and_over AS population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`

    AND population_1_year_and_over > 0
),

vaccine_sites_union AS (
  -- Combine all vaccine site tables and deduplicate by facility_place_id per county

    facility_place_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_transit`
  WHERE facility_sub_region_1_code = 'US-CA'
    AND facility_sub_region_2_code IS NOT NULL
),

county_vaccine_counts AS (
  -- Count unique vaccine sites per county
  SELECT 
    county_fips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT facility_place_id) AS vaccine_site_count
  FROM vaccine_sites_union
  GROUP BY county_fips
)

-- Final calculation: vaccine sites per 1000 people
SELECT 
  cp.county_fips,
  cp.population,
  COALESCE(cvc.vaccine_site_count, 0) AS vaccine_site_count,
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(cvc.vaccine_site_count, 0) / NULLIF(cp.population, 0) * 1000,
    4
  ) AS vaccine_sites_per_1000_people
FROM california_population cp
LEFT JOIN county_vaccine_counts cvc
  ON cp.county_fips = cvc.county_fips
ORDER BY vaccine_sites_per_1000_people DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH vaccine_sites AS (
  -- Count distinct vaccination sites per county in California
  SELECT
    facility_sub_region_2_code AS county_fips,
    ANY_VALUE(facility_sub_region_2) AS county_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT facility_place_id) AS site_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`
  WHERE facility_sub_region_1 = 'California'
  GROUP BY facility_sub_region_2_code
),
county_population AS (
  -- Get 2018 5-year ACS population estimates for California counties
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    total_pop
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`
  WHERE geo_id LIKE '06%'  -- California FIPS state code prefix
)
SELECT
  vs.county_name,
  ROUND(vs.site_count / cp.total_pop * 1000, 4) AS sites_per_1000_people
FROM vaccine_sites vs
INNER JOIN county_population cp
  ON vs.county_fips = cp.geo_id
ORDER BY vs.county_name
```
</details>

```sql
WITH california_tracts AS (
  -- Get all census tracts in California
  SELECT 
    tract_ce,
    geo_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california`
),
income_2015 AS (
  -- Get median income for 2015
  -- Note: Assuming censustract_2015_5yr exists with same structure as 2018
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
income_2018 AS (
  -- Get median income for 2018
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
combined_data AS (
  -- Combine all data
  SELECT 
    ct.tract_ce,
    ct.geo_id,
    i15.median_income_2015,
    i18.median_income_2018,
    -- Calculate the increase
    (i18.median_income_2018 - i15.median_income_2015) AS income_increase
  FROM california_tracts ct
  LEFT JOIN income_2015 i15 ON ct.geo_id = i15.geo_id
  LEFT JOIN income_2018 i18 ON ct.geo_id = i18.geo_id
  WHERE i15.median_income_2015 IS NOT NULL 
    AND i18.median_income_2018 IS NOT NULL
)
-- Find the tract with the largest increase
SELECT 
  tract_ce,
  geo_id,
  median_income_2015,
  median_income_2018,
  income_increase
FROM combined_data
ORDER BY income_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
income_change AS (
  SELECT 
    ct.tract_ce,
    ct.geo_id,
    i15.median_income_2015,
    i18.median_income_2018,
    (i18.median_income_2018 - i15.median_income_2015) AS income_increase
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california` ct
  INNER JOIN income_2015 i15 ON ct.geo_id = i15.geo_id
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18 ON ct.geo_id = i18.geo_id
  WHERE ct.state_fips_code = '06'
)
SELECT 
  tract_ce
FROM income_change
ORDER BY income_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_shots AS (
  SELECT 
    pbp.shot_type,
    pbp.event_coord_x,
    pbp.event_coord_y,
    pbp.team_basket,
    pbp.shot_made,
    pbp.game_id,
    -- Apply coordinate adjustment for consistency (always left basket perspective)
    CASE 
      WHEN pbp.event_coord_x < 564 THEN pbp.event_coord_x
      ELSE 1128 - pbp.event_coord_x
    END AS adjusted_x,
    CASE 
      WHEN pbp.event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - pbp.event_coord_y
      ELSE pbp.event_coord_y
    END AS adjusted_y,
    -- Determine if shot is on correct side based on team_basket
    CASE 
      WHEN pbp.team_basket = 'left' AND pbp.event_coord_x < 564 THEN TRUE
      WHEN pbp.team_basket = 'right' AND pbp.event_coord_x >= 564 THEN TRUE
      ELSE FALSE
    END AS is_correct_side
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr` pbp
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_games_sr` games
    ON pbp.game_id = games.game_id
  WHERE 
    -- Date filter: shots before March 15, 2018
    games.gametime < TIMESTAMP('2018-03-15')
    -- Exclude null values
    AND pbp.shot_type IS NOT NULL 
    AND pbp.shot_type != 'None'
    AND pbp.event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
    AND pbp.event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
    -- Only include shot attempts (where shot_type indicates a shot)
    AND pbp.shot_type IN ('jump shot', 'layup', 'hook shot', 'dunk', 'tip shot')
),

game_shot_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    game_id,
    shot_type,
    COUNT(*) AS shot_attempts,
    SUM(CAST(shot_made AS INT64)) AS successful_shots,
    AVG(adjusted_x) AS avg_adjusted_x,
    AVG(adjusted_y) AS avg_adjusted_y
  FROM filtered_shots
  WHERE is_correct_side = TRUE  -- Only shots on correct side of court
  GROUP BY game_id, shot_type
)

SELECT 
  shot_type,
  ROUND(AVG(avg_adjusted_x), 4) AS avg_x_coordinate,
  ROUND(AVG(avg_adjusted_y), 4) AS avg_y_coordinate,
  ROUND(AVG(shot_attempts), 4) AS avg_shot_attempts_per_game,
  ROUND(AVG(successful_shots), 4) AS avg_successful_shots_per_game,
  COUNT(DISTINCT game_id) AS games_with_shot_type
FROM game_shot_stats
GROUP BY shot_type
ORDER BY shot_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter and prepare all valid shots
  filtered_shots AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      -- Adjust X: mirror right-side shots to left-side orientation
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
        ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
      END AS adjusted_x,
      -- Adjust Y: mirror accordingly based on which half the shot was on
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
        ELSE event_coord_y
      END AS adjusted_y,
      shot_made,
      game_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
    WHERE
      -- Exclude null or 'None' shot types
      shot_type IS NOT NULL
      AND shot_type != 'None'
      -- Exclude null coordinates
      AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
      AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
      -- Only shots before March 15, 2018
      AND scheduled_date < '2018-03-15'
      -- Ensure shots are on the correct side of the court based on team's basket
      AND (
        (team_basket = 'left' AND event_coord_x < 564)
        OR (team_basket = 'right' AND event_coord_x >= 564)
      )
  ),

  -- Step 2: Per-game counts of attempts and made shots for each shot type
  per_game_counts AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      game_id,
      COUNT(*) AS shot_attempts,
      COUNTIF(shot_made) AS shots_made
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type, game_id
  ),

  -- Step 3: Overall average coordinates per shot type (across all individual shots)
  coord_averages AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      AVG(adjusted_x) AS avg_adjusted_x,
      AVG(adjusted_y) AS avg_adjusted_y
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type
  )

-- Step 4: Combine coordinate averages with per-game averages
SELECT
  c.shot_type,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_x, 4) AS avg_adjusted_x,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_y, 4) AS avg_adjusted_y,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shot_attempts), 4) AS avg_shot_attempts,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shots_made), 4) AS avg_shots_made
FROM coord_averages c
JOIN per_game_counts p
  ON c.shot_type = p.shot_type
GROUP BY c.shot_type, c.avg_adjusted_x, c.avg_adjusted_y
ORDER BY c.shot_type;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH historical_games AS (
  -- Extract historical tournament games from 2014 onwards
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    win_school_ncaa AS team_school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS team_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    'win' AS label,
    win_pts AS points,
    lose_pts AS opponent_points,
    win_name AS team_name,
    lose_name AS opponent_name,
    round
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    lose_school_ncaa AS team_school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS team_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_pts AS points,
    win_pts AS opponent_points,
    lose_name AS team_name,
    win_name AS opponent_name,
    round
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
),

tournament_2018 AS (
  -- Extract 2018 tournament results
  SELECT 
    season,
    school_ncaa AS team_school_ncaa,
    seed AS team_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    label,
    points,
    opponent_points,
    name AS team_name,
    opponent_name,
    round
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
),

all_tournament_games AS (
  -- Combine historical (2014-2017) and 2018 games
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  WHERE season < 2018  -- Historical games up to 2017
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT * FROM tournament_2018  -- Add 2018 games
),

-- Join team metrics
games_with_team_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    g.*,
    t.efficiency_rank AS team_efficiency_rank,
    t.pace_rank AS team_pace_rank,
    t.pace_rating AS team_pace_rating,
    t.efficiency_rating AS team_efficiency_rating
  FROM all_tournament_games g
  LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` t
    ON LOWER(TRIM(g.team_school_ncaa)) = LOWER(TRIM(t.team))
    AND g.season = t.season
),

-- Join opponent metrics
games_with_all_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    g.*,
    o.efficiency_rank AS opponent_efficiency_rank,
    o.pace_rank AS opponent_pace_rank,
    o.pace_rating AS opponent_pace_rating,
    o.efficiency_rating AS opponent_efficiency_rating
  FROM games_with_team_metrics g
  LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` o
    ON LOWER(TRIM(g.opponent_school_ncaa)) = LOWER(TRIM(o.team))
    AND g.season = o.season
)

-- Final dataset with calculated differences
SELECT 
  season,
  label,
  team_seed,
  team_school_ncaa,
  team_name,
  opponent_seed,
  opponent_school_ncaa,
  opponent_name,
  points,
  opponent_points,
  round,
  
  -- Team metrics
  team_efficiency_rank,
  team_pace_rank,
  team_pace_rating,
  team_efficiency_rating,
  
  -- Opponent metrics
  opponent_efficiency_rank,
  opponent_pace_rank,
  opponent_pace_rating,
  opponent_efficiency_rating,
  
  -- Differences (opponent - team)
  ROUND(opponent_efficiency_rank - team_efficiency_rank, 4) AS efficiency_rank_diff,
  ROUND(opponent_pace_rank - team_pace_rank, 4) AS pace_rank_diff,
  ROUND(opponent_pace_rating - team_pace_rating, 4) AS pace_rating_diff,
  ROUND(opponent_efficiency_rating - team_efficiency_rating, 4) AS efficiency_rating_diff
  
FROM games_with_all_metrics
WHERE 
  team_efficiency_rank IS NOT NULL 
  AND opponent_efficiency_rank IS NOT NULL
  AND team_pace_rank IS NOT NULL 
  AND opponent_pace_rank IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY season, round, team_school_ncaa;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH historical_games AS (
  -- Winning team rows from historical tournament games (2014-2017)
  -- Using academic_year as the season identifier
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
  UNION ALL
  -- Losing team rows from historical tournament games (2014-2017)
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
),

games_2018 AS (
  -- 2018 tournament results are already in row-per-team format with label
  SELECT 
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),

all_games AS (
  -- Combine all tournament game data from 2014 onwards
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM games_2018
)

SELECT 
  g.season,
  g.label,
  g.seed,
  g.school_ncaa,
  g.opponent_seed,
  g.opponent_school_ncaa,
  -- Team pace metrics
  tm.pace_rank,
  tm.poss_40min,
  tm.pace_rating,
  -- Team efficiency metrics
  tm.efficiency_rank,
  tm.pts_100poss,
  tm.efficiency_rating,
  -- Opponent pace metrics
  opp.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  opp.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  opp.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  -- Opponent efficiency metrics
  opp.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  opp.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  opp.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  -- Feature-engineered differences (opponent metric minus team metric)
  opp.pace_rank - tm.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  opp.poss_40min - tm.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  opp.pace_rating - tm.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rank - tm.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  opp.pts_100poss - tm.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rating - tm.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games g
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` tm
  ON g.school_ncaa = tm.team AND g.season = tm.season
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` opp
  ON g.opponent_school_ncaa = opp.team AND g.season = opp.season
ORDER BY g.season, g.school_ncaa
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH utah_counties AS (
  -- Get Utah counties by state FIPS code
  SELECT county_fips_code, county_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties`
  WHERE state_fips_code = '49'
),
employment_2000 AS (
  -- Average construction employment in 2000 across four quarters
  SELECT area_fips, AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_emp_2000
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('q1', 'q2', 'q3', 'q4')
    AND area_fips IN (SELECT county_fips_code FROM utah_counties)
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
),
employment_2018 AS (
  -- Average construction employment in 2018 across four quarters
  SELECT area_fips, AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_emp_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('q1', 'q2', 'q3', 'q4')
    AND area_fips IN (SELECT county_fips_code FROM utah_counties)
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
),
pct_increases AS (
  -- Calculate percentage increase for each county
  SELECT
    c.county_name,
    e2000.avg_emp_2000,
    e2018.avg_emp_2018,
    ROUND((e2018.avg_emp_2018 - e2000.avg_emp_2000) / e2000.avg_emp_2000 * 100, 2) AS pct_increase
  FROM utah_counties c
  INNER JOIN employment_2000 e2000 ON c.county_fips_code = e2000.area_fips
  INNER JOIN employment_2018 e2018 ON c.county_fips_code = e2018.area_fips
  WHERE e2000.avg_emp_2000 > 0  -- Avoid division by zero and negative averages
)
-- Return the county with the greatest percentage increase
SELECT county_name, pct_increase
FROM pct_increases
ORDER BY pct_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH yearly_avg_construction AS (
  -- For each Utah county and each year, average the construction employment
  -- from the 3rd month of all 4 quarters (March, June, September, December)
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    CAST(SUBSTR(_TABLE_SUFFIX, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_empl
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2000_q1' AND '2018_q4'
    -- Utah state FIPS code is 49
    AND area_fips LIKE '49%'
  GROUP BY area_fips, year
),
yearly_comparison AS (
  -- Pivot to get 2000 and 2018 averages side by side per county
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2000 THEN avg_empl END) AS avg_empl_2000,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2018 THEN avg_empl END) AS avg_empl_2018
  FROM yearly_avg_construction
  WHERE year IN (2000, 2018)
  GROUP BY area_fips
  -- Keep only counties with valid data in both years
  HAVING avg_empl_2000 IS NOT NULL 
     AND avg_empl_2018 IS NOT NULL
     AND avg_empl_2000 > 0
),
pct_change AS (
  -- Calculate the percentage increase from 2000 to 2018
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    ROUND((avg_empl_2018 - avg_empl_2000) / avg_empl_2000 * 100, 4) AS pct_increase
  FROM yearly_comparison
),
ranked AS (
  -- Rank counties by percentage increase descending
  SELECT 
    p.area_fips,
    p.pct_increase,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.pct_increase DESC) AS rn
  FROM pct_change p
)
-- Join with counties table to get the county name
SELECT 
  c.lsad_name AS county_name,
  r.pct_increase AS percentage_increase
FROM ranked r
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` c
  ON r.area_fips = c.county_fips_code
WHERE r.rn = 1;
```
</details>

```sql
    'BLS Tech Sectors' AS metric,
    NULL AS race_asian,  -- Not available in this BLS table
    ROUND(AVG(percent_black_or_african_american), 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_hispanic_or_latino), 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    NULL AS race_white,  -- Not available in this BLS table
    ROUND(AVG(percent_women), 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(1 - AVG(percent_women), 4) AS gender_us_men  -- Calculate men percentage
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.full_csv-latest-data-is-2023`
  WHERE LOWER(industry) IN (
    'internet publishing and broadcasting and web search portals',
    'computer systems design and related services'
  )
  -- Group by to ensure we get average across both sectors
  GROUP BY metric
)

-- Combine all three data sources into a single report
SELECT 
  metric,
  race_asian,
  race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_white,
  gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men
FROM google_hiring_2021

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  metric,
  race_asian,
  race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_white,
  gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men
FROM google_representation_2021

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  metric,
  race_asian,
  race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_white,
  gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men
FROM bls_tech_sectors

ORDER BY 
  CASE metric
    WHEN 'Google Hiring (2021)' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Google Representation (2021)' THEN 2
    WHEN 'BLS Tech Sectors' THEN 3
  END;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combined 2021 report comparing racial and gender distributions across:
-- Google's overall workforce hiring, Google's overall workforce representation,
-- and BLS data for technology sectors (Internet publishing/broadcasting/web search portals
-- and Computer systems design/related services).
-- Uses weighted averaging for BLS sectors to produce a single set of percentages.

WITH
-- Google non‑intersectional hiring data for overall workforce, 2021
google_hiring AS (
  SELECT
    race_asian,
    race_black,
    race_hispanic_latinx,
    race_white,
    gender_us_women,
    gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Google non‑intersectional representation data for overall workforce, 2021
google_representation AS (
  SELECT
    race_asian,
    race_black,
    race_hispanic_latinx,
    race_white,
    gender_us_women,
    gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
  LIMIT 1
),

-- BLS data for the specified technology sectors, 2021, with weighted averages
bls_tech AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(percent_asian * total_employed_in_thousands) / NULLIF(SUM(total_employed_in_thousands), 0) AS weighted_asian,
    SUM(percent_black_or_african_american * total_employed_in_thousands) / NULLIF(SUM(total_employed_in_thousands), 0) AS weighted_black,
    SUM(percent_hispanic_or_latino * total_employed_in_thousands) / NULLIF(SUM(total_employed_in_thousands), 0) AS weighted_hispanic,
    SUM(percent_white * total_employed_in_thousands) / NULLIF(SUM(total_employed_in_thousands), 0) AS weighted_white,
    SUM(percent_women * total_employed_in_thousands) / NULLIF(SUM(total_employed_in_thousands), 0) AS weighted_women
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.full_csv-latest-data-is-2023`
  WHERE year = 2021
    AND (
      LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%internet%' OR
      LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%web search%' OR
      LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%computer systems design%' OR
      LOWER(sector) LIKE '%internet%' OR
      LOWER(sector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
    )
),

-- Unpivot Google hiring data into rows per race/gender category
unpivoted_hiring AS (
  SELECT 'Google Hiring' AS source, 'Race' AS category_type, 'Asian' AS category_name, ROUND(race_asian, 4) AS percentage FROM google_hiring
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Hiring', 'Race', 'Black', ROUND(race_black, 4) FROM google_hiring
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Hiring', 'Race', 'Hispanic/Latinx', ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) FROM google_hiring
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Hiring', 'Race', 'White', ROUND(race_white, 4) FROM google_hiring
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Hiring', 'Gender', 'U.S. Women', ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) FROM google_hiring
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Hiring', 'Gender', 'U.S. Men', ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) FROM google_hiring
),

-- Unpivot Google representation data
unpivoted_representation AS (
  SELECT 'Google Representation' AS source, 'Race' AS category_type, 'Asian' AS category_name, ROUND(race_asian, 4) FROM google_representation
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Representation', 'Race', 'Black', ROUND(race_black, 4) FROM google_representation
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Representation', 'Race', 'Hispanic/Latinx', ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) FROM google_representation
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Representation', 'Race', 'White', ROUND(race_white, 4) FROM google_representation
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Representation', 'Gender', 'U.S. Women', ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) FROM google_representation
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Google Representation', 'Gender', 'U.S. Men', ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) FROM google_representation
),

-- Unpivot BLS weighted averages; U.S. Men = 1 - weighted_women
unpivoted_bls AS (
  SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors' AS source, 'Race' AS category_type, 'Asian' AS category_name, ROUND(weighted_asian, 4) FROM bls_tech
  UNION ALL SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors', 'Race', 'Black', ROUND(weighted_black, 4) FROM bls_tech
  UNION ALL SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors', 'Race', 'Hispanic/Latinx', ROUND(weighted_hispanic, 4) FROM bls_tech
  UNION ALL SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors', 'Race', 'White', ROUND(weighted_white, 4) FROM bls_tech
  UNION ALL SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors', 'Gender', 'U.S. Women', ROUND(weighted_women, 4) FROM bls_tech
  UNION ALL SELECT 'BLS Tech Sectors', 'Gender', 'U.S. Men', ROUND(1 - weighted_women, 4) FROM bls_tech
)

-- Combine all sources into one report
SELECT source, category_type, category_name, percentage
FROM unpivoted_hiring
UNION ALL
SELECT source, category_type, category_name, percentage
FROM unpivoted_representation
UNION ALL
SELECT source, category_type, category_name, percentage
FROM unpivoted_bls
ORDER BY source, category_type, category_name;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH flattened_licenses AS (
    -- Extract individual licenses from the Licenses array for each package
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pv."System",
        pv."Name" AS "PackageName",
        TRIM(f.value::STRING, '"') AS "License"
    FROM "DEPS_DEV_V1"."DEPS_DEV_V1"."PACKAGEVERSIONS" pv,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pv."Licenses") f
    WHERE pv."Licenses" IS NOT NULL
        AND ARRAY_SIZE(pv."Licenses") > 0
        AND TRIM(f.value::STRING, '"') != ''
),
license_counts AS (
    -- Count how many packages use each license in each system
    SELECT
        "System",
        "License",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "PackageName") AS "PackageCount"
    FROM flattened_licenses
    WHERE "License" IS NOT NULL
        AND "License" != ''
    GROUP BY "System", "License"
),
ranked_licenses AS (
    -- Rank licenses by frequency within each system
    SELECT
        "System",
        "License",
        "PackageCount",
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "System" ORDER BY "PackageCount" DESC) AS "Rank"
    FROM license_counts
)
-- Select the most frequent license(s) for each system
SELECT
    "System",
    "License",
    "PackageCount" AS "Frequency"
FROM ranked_licenses
WHERE "Rank" = 1
ORDER BY "System", "License";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH flattened_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        p."System",
        p."Name",
        f.value::STRING AS license
    FROM DEPS_DEV_V1.DEPS_DEV_V1.PACKAGEVERSIONS p,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."Licenses") f
    WHERE p."System" IS NOT NULL
      AND p."Licenses" IS NOT NULL
),
package_license_count AS (
    SELECT 
        "System",
        license,
        COUNT(DISTINCT "Name") AS package_count
    FROM flattened_licenses
    GROUP BY "System", license
),
ranked_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        "System",
        license,
        package_count,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "System" 
            ORDER BY package_count DESC, license ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM package_license_count
)
SELECT 
    "System" AS system,
    license AS most_frequent_license
FROM ranked_licenses
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY "System";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Find the highest number of motor vehicle theft incidents in any single month during 2016
WITH monthly_counts AS (
  -- Step 1: Filter for 2016 and motor vehicle theft, then count per month
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,  -- Extract month number (1-12)
    COUNT(*) AS incident_count          -- Count incidents per month
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2016      -- Filter for year 2016
    AND primary_type = 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT'  -- Filter for motor vehicle theft
  GROUP BY
    month                                -- Group by month to get monthly totals
)
-- Step 2: Find the maximum monthly count
SELECT
  MAX(incident_count) AS highest_monthly_incidents
FROM
  monthly_counts;
```

```sql
FROM (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE LOWER(primary_type) LIKE '%motor%vehicle%theft%'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2016
  GROUP BY year, month
)
```

```sql
WITH drug_name_matches AS (
    -- Match by trade names
    SELECT DISTINCT k."drugId" AS "matched_drug_id"
    FROM "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."KNOWNDRUGSAGGREGATED" k,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => k."tradeNames":"list") t
    WHERE t.value:"element"::STRING IN ('Keytruda', 'Vioxx', 'Premarin', 'Humira')
    
    UNION
    
    -- Match by synonyms
    SELECT DISTINCT k."drugId" AS "matched_drug_id"
    FROM "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."KNOWNDRUGSAGGREGATED" k,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => k."synonyms":"list") s
    WHERE s.value:"element"::STRING IN ('Keytruda', 'Vioxx', 'Premarin', 'Humira')
    
    UNION
    
    -- Match by preferred name
    SELECT DISTINCT k."drugId" AS "matched_drug_id"
    FROM "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."KNOWNDRUGSAGGREGATED" k
    WHERE k."prefName" IN ('Keytruda', 'Vioxx', 'Premarin', 'Humira')
)

SELECT 
    m."id" AS "drug_id",
    m."drugType" AS "drug_type",
    m."hasBeenWithdrawn" AS "withdrawal_status"
FROM "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."MOLECULE" m
INNER JOIN drug_name_matches dnm ON m."id" = dnm."matched_drug_id"
WHERE m."isApproved" = TRUE
    AND m."blackBoxWarning" = TRUE
    AND m."drugType" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY m."id";
```

```sql
    AND LOWER(TRIM(f.value:"element"::STRING)) IN ('keytruda', 'vioxx', 'premarin', 'humira')
)
SELECT
  m."id" AS "drug_id",
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH impc_associations AS (
    -- Get direct associations for EFO_0000676 from IMPC (case-insensitive)
    SELECT 
        "targetId", 
        "evidenceCount"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYDATASOURCEDIRECT
    WHERE "diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676' 
        AND LOWER("datasourceId") = 'impc'
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Get indirect associations for EFO_0000676 from IMPC (case-insensitive)
    SELECT 
        "targetId", 
        "evidenceCount"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYDATASOURCEINDIRECT
    WHERE "diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676' 
        AND LOWER("datasourceId") = 'impc'
),
max_score AS (
    -- Find the maximum evidenceCount (overall score)
    SELECT MAX("evidenceCount") AS "max_evidenceCount"
    FROM impc_associations
)
-- Get approved symbols for targets with the maximum score
SELECT DISTINCT
    t."approvedSymbol"
FROM impc_associations a
JOIN max_score m ON a."evidenceCount" = m."max_evidenceCount"
JOIN OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.TARGETS t 
    ON a."targetId" = t."id"
ORDER BY t."approvedSymbol";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify targets associated with disease EFO_0000676 from IMPC data source
impc_targets AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "targetId"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYDATASOURCEDIRECT
    WHERE "diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
      AND "datasourceId" = 'IMPC'
),

-- Step 2: Get overall scores for those targets and rank them
ranked_targets AS (
    SELECT
        ao."targetId",
        ao."score",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ao."score" DESC) AS "score_rank"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYOVERALLDIRECT ao
    WHERE ao."diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
      AND ao."targetId" IN (SELECT "targetId" FROM impc_targets)
)

-- Step 3: Retrieve the approved symbol for the target(s) with the highest overall score
SELECT 
    t."approvedSymbol"
FROM ranked_targets rt
JOIN OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.TARGETS t
    ON rt."targetId" = t."id"
WHERE rt."score_rank" = 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: For each study and gene, select the variant with the lowest p-value.

-- Step 2: For each gene, get the best p-value across all studies.

    SELECT 
        "gene_id",
        MIN("min_pval") AS "best_pval"
    FROM 
        best_variant_per_gene_study
    GROUP BY 
        "gene_id"
)
-- Step 3: Rank genes by best_pval and return the top 10 with gene names.
SELECT 
    b."gene_id",
    g."gene_name",
    b."best_pval"
FROM 
    best_pval_per_gene b
    LEFT JOIN "OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_2"."OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS"."GENES" g 
        ON b."gene_id" = g."gene_id"
ORDER BY 
    b."best_pval" ASC,
    b."gene_id"
LIMIT 10;
```

```sql
WITH best_variant_per_gene_study AS (
    -- For each (study, gene), pick the variant row with the lowest p-value
    SELECT 
        dvg."study_id",
        dvg."gene_id",
        dvg."tag_chrom",
        dvg."tag_pos",
        dvg."tag_ref",
        dvg."tag_alt",
        dvg."pval",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY dvg."study_id", dvg."gene_id" 
            ORDER BY dvg."pval" ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM "OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_2"."OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS"."DISEASE_VARIANT_GENE" dvg
    WHERE dvg."pval" IS NOT NULL
),
best_per_gene AS (
    -- For each gene, get its smallest p-value across all studies
    SELECT 
        bv."gene_id",
        MIN(bv."pval") AS best_pval
    FROM best_variant_per_gene_study bv
    WHERE bv.rn = 1
    GROUP BY bv."gene_id"
),
ranked_genes AS (
    -- Rank genes by their best p-value
    SELECT 
        bg."gene_id",
        bg."best_pval",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY bg."best_pval" ASC) AS gene_rank
    FROM best_per_gene bg
)
-- Return top 10 genes with gene names, ordered by p-value
SELECT 
    g."gene_name",
    g."gene_id",
    ROUND(rg."best_pval", 4) AS best_pval
FROM ranked_genes rg
JOIN "OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_2"."OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS"."GENES" g
    ON rg."gene_id" = g."gene_id"
WHERE rg.gene_rank <= 10
ORDER BY rg."best_pval" ASC;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Calculate the difference in average intrinsic value between feeling-lucky and momentum strategies for long trades.
-- Intrinsic value = StrikePrice - LastPx (profit for long CFD trades).
-- Strategies are identified via TargetCompID patterns.
SELECT
  ROUND(
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%lucky%' OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%feeling%'
        THEN StrikePrice - LastPx
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ) -
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momo%' OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momentum%'
        THEN StrikePrice - LastPx
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ),
    4
  ) AS avg_intrinsic_value_difference
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`,
  UNNEST(Sides) AS side_info
WHERE
  side_info.Side = 'LONG'
  AND (
    LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%lucky%'
    OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%feeling%'
    OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momo%'
    OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momentum%'
  );
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Unnest sides, filter for LONG side, compute intrinsic value
WITH long_trades AS (
  SELECT
    t.StrikePrice,
    t.LastPx,
    -- Intrinsic value for a long CFD = closing price (StrikePrice) - entry price (LastPx)
    t.StrikePrice - t.LastPx AS intrinsic_value,
    -- Extract strategy from TargetCompID (assume 'MOMOES' for momentum, 'LUCKY' for feeling-lucky)
    CASE
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%MOMOES%' THEN 'momentum'
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%LUCKY%' THEN 'feeling-lucky'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS strategy
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS side
  WHERE side.Side = 'LONG'
),
-- Step 2: Compute average intrinsic value per strategy (only the two of interest)
avg_intrinsic AS (
  SELECT
    strategy,
    ROUND(AVG(intrinsic_value), 4) AS avg_value
  FROM long_trades
  WHERE strategy IS NOT NULL   -- exclude rows that don't match either strategy
  GROUP BY strategy
),
-- Step 3: Pivot to get difference (feeling-lucky minus momentum)
differences AS (
  SELECT
    ROUND((SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'feeling-lucky') -
          (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'momentum'), 4) AS difference
)
-- Step 4: Return the single number
SELECT difference
FROM differences;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH plot_calculations AS (
  SELECT 
    c.state_code_name AS state,
    pt.plot_inventory_year AS year,
    c.proportion_basis AS plot_type,
    -- Calculate subplot area: E � P � A_s when proportion_basis = 'SUBP'
    CASE 
      WHEN c.proportion_basis = 'SUBP' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot > 0 
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * c.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot
      ELSE 0 
    END AS subplot_area,
    -- Calculate macroplot area: E � P � A_m when proportion_basis = 'MACR'
    CASE 
      WHEN c.proportion_basis = 'MACR' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot > 0
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * c.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot
      ELSE 0 
    END AS macroplot_area
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` c
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot_tree` pt
    ON c.plot_sequence_number = pt.plot_sequence_number
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` pop
    ON c.plot_sequence_number = pop.plot_sequence_number
  WHERE c.condition_status_code = 1
    AND pt.plot_inventory_year IN (2015, 2016, 2017)
),

state_year_aggregates AS (
  SELECT 
    state,
    year,
    -- Average subplot size (excluding zeros)
    AVG(CASE WHEN subplot_area > 0 THEN subplot_area END) AS avg_subplot_size,
    -- Average macroplot size (excluding zeros)
    AVG(CASE WHEN macroplot_area > 0 THEN macroplot_area END) AS avg_macroplot_size
  FROM plot_calculations
  GROUP BY state, year
),

ranked_states AS (
  SELECT 
    'subplot' AS plot_type,
    year,
    state,
    avg_subplot_size AS average_size,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_subplot_size DESC) AS rank
  FROM state_year_aggregates
  WHERE avg_subplot_size IS NOT NULL
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT 
    'macroplot' AS plot_type,
    year,
    state,
    avg_macroplot_size AS average_size,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_macroplot_size DESC) AS rank
  FROM state_year_aggregates
  WHERE avg_macroplot_size IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT 
  plot_type,
  year,
  state,
  ROUND(average_size, 4) AS average_size
FROM ranked_states
WHERE rank = 1
ORDER BY plot_type, year;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH plot_sizes AS (
  -- Calculate subplot and macroplot sizes for each condition record
  -- Subplot Size = expansion_factor × condition_proportion_unadjusted × adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot
  -- Macroplot Size = expansion_factor × condition_proportion_unadjusted × adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot
  SELECT 
    pt.plot_inventory_year AS year,
    pt.plot_state_code_name AS state_name,
    cond.proportion_basis,
    -- Subplot size calculation (only applicable when proportion_basis = 'SUBP')
    CASE 
      WHEN cond.proportion_basis = 'SUBP' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot > 0 
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * cond.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot
      ELSE NULL 
    END AS subplot_size,
    -- Macroplot size calculation (only applicable when proportion_basis = 'MACR')
    CASE 
      WHEN cond.proportion_basis = 'MACR' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot > 0 
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * cond.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot
      ELSE NULL 
    END AS macroplot_size
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` pop
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` cond
    ON pop.plot_sequence_number = cond.plot_sequence_number
    AND pop.state_code = cond.state_code
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot_tree` pt
    ON pop.plot_sequence_number = pt.plot_sequence_number
  WHERE pop.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
    AND cond.condition_status_code = 1
    AND pt.plot_inventory_year IN (2015, 2016, 2017)
),
avg_sizes AS (
  -- Calculate average sizes per year and state (nulls are automatically excluded by AVG)
  SELECT 
    year,
    state_name,
    ROUND(AVG(subplot_size), 4) AS avg_subplot_size,
    ROUND(AVG(macroplot_size), 4) AS avg_macroplot_size
  FROM plot_sizes
  GROUP BY year, state_name
),
ranked AS (
  -- Rank states by average subplot size and macroplot size per year
  SELECT 
    year,
    state_name,
    avg_subplot_size,
    avg_macroplot_size,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_subplot_size DESC NULLS LAST) AS subplot_rank,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_macroplot_size DESC NULLS LAST) AS macroplot_rank
  FROM avg_sizes
)
-- Get the top-ranked state for each plot type and each year
SELECT 'Subplot' AS plot_type, CAST(year AS STRING) AS year, state_name, avg_subplot_size AS avg_size
FROM ranked
WHERE subplot_rank = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Macroplot' AS plot_type, CAST(year AS STRING) AS year, state_name, avg_macroplot_size AS avg_size
FROM ranked
WHERE macroplot_rank = 1
ORDER BY year, plot_type;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH qualified_days AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM eventdate) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM eventdate) AS month,
    EXTRACT(DAY FROM eventdate) AS day,
    DATE(eventdate) AS sighting_date,
    COUNT(*) AS sighting_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE LOWER(species) = 'sterna paradisaea'
    AND decimallatitude > 40
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM eventdate) >= 2  -- After January
    AND eventdate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, month, day, sighting_date
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
),

year_earliest AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    MIN(sighting_date) AS earliest_date,
    -- Get the count for the earliest date
    ARRAY_AGG(
      STRUCT(sighting_date, sighting_count) 
      ORDER BY sighting_date 
      LIMIT 1
    )[OFFSET(0)] AS earliest_day_info
  FROM qualified_days
  GROUP BY year
)

SELECT 
  year,
  earliest_day_info.sighting_date,
  earliest_day_info.sighting_count
FROM year_earliest
ORDER BY earliest_date
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter for Sterna paradisaea, north of 40° latitude, after January,
--         and count sightings per day, keeping only days with >10 sightings
WITH daily_sightings AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    day,
    COUNT(*) AS sightings_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE LOWER(species) LIKE '%sterna paradisaea%'
    AND decimallatitude > 40
    AND month > 1  -- After January
    AND year IS NOT NULL
    AND month IS NOT NULL
    AND day IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, month, day
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
),

-- Step 2: For each year, find the first date (earliest month+day) with >10 sightings
yearly_first_date AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    day,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year
      ORDER BY month ASC, day ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM daily_sightings
)

-- Step 3: Among all years, the one with the earliest calendar date (month, day) wins
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  day
FROM yearly_first_date
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY month ASC, day ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
  agg."port_state"                  AS "state",
  agg."storm_years",
  agg."total_storms",
  agg."storm_names",
  agg."avg_storm_category",
  agg."avg_wind_speed",
  sc."state_centroid"               AS "port_geometry",
  ST_MAKEPOINT(agg."avg_lon", agg."avg_lat") AS "storm_geometry"
FROM aggregated agg
JOIN state_centroids sc ON agg."port_state" = sc."state"
ORDER BY agg."port_state"
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify ports in region 6585 that lie within U.S. state boundaries
WITH ports_us AS (
    SELECT
        p."port_name",
        p."region_number",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(p."port_geom") AS "port_geog",
        s."state_name"
    FROM "NOAA_PORTS"."GEO_INTERNATIONAL_PORTS"."WORLD_PORT_INDEX" p
    JOIN "NOAA_PORTS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."STATES" s
        ON ST_WITHIN(
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(p."port_geom"),
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(s."state_geom")
        )
    WHERE p."region_number" = '6585'
      AND p."country" = 'US'
),

-- Step 2: Filter North Atlantic named storms with wind >=35 kt and SS cat >=0 (tropical storm+)
hurricanes_filtered AS (
    SELECT
        h."sid",
        h."name",
        h."season",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."latitude", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "lat",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."longitude", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "lon",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_wind", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "wind",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_sshs", 'None') AS INT) AS "category",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_r34_ne", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "r34_ne",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_r34_se", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "r34_se",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_r34_sw", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "r34_sw",
        TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_r34_nw", 'None') AS FLOAT) AS "r34_nw"
    FROM "NOAA_PORTS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES" h
    WHERE h."basin" = 'NA'
      AND h."name" IS NOT NULL
      AND h."name" != 'NOT_NAMED'
      AND TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_wind", 'None') AS FLOAT) >= 35
      AND TRY_CAST(NULLIF(h."usa_sshs", 'None') AS INT) >= 0
),

-- Step 3: For each hurricane observation, construct the 34-kt wind area polygon
-- using the provided azimuth_to_geog_point logic (converted to inline calculation).
storm_polygons AS (
    SELECT
        "sid",
        "name",
        "season",
        "wind",
        "category",
        "lat",
        "lon",
        -- Compute the four quadrant points
        ST_MAKEPOINT(
            57.2958 * (
                "lon" * (3.14159 / 180) +
                ATAN2(
                    SIN(RADIANS(45)) * SIN(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS("lat")),
                    COS(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) - SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                            SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                            COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(45))
                        )
                    )
                )
            ),
            57.2958 * ASIN(
                SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_ne" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(45))
            )
        ) AS "ne_point",
        ST_MAKEPOINT(
            57.2958 * (
                "lon" * (3.14159 / 180) +
                ATAN2(
                    SIN(RADIANS(135)) * SIN(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS("lat")),
                    COS(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) - SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                            SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                            COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(135))
                        )
                    )
                )
            ),
            57.2958 * ASIN(
                SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_se" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(135))
            )
        ) AS "se_point",
        ST_MAKEPOINT(
            57.2958 * (
                "lon" * (3.14159 / 180) +
                ATAN2(
                    SIN(RADIANS(225)) * SIN(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS("lat")),
                    COS(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) - SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                            SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                            COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(225))
                        )
                    )
                )
            ),
            57.2958 * ASIN(
                SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_sw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(225))
            )
        ) AS "sw_point",
        ST_MAKEPOINT(
            57.2958 * (
                "lon" * (3.14159 / 180) +
                ATAN2(
                    SIN(RADIANS(315)) * SIN(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS("lat")),
                    COS(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) - SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                            SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                            COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(315))
                        )
                    )
                )
            ),
            57.2958 * ASIN(
                SIN(RADIANS("lat")) * COS(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) +
                COS(RADIANS("lat")) * SIN(("r34_nw" * 1.61) / 6378.1) * COS(RADIANS(315))
            )
        ) AS "nw_point"
    FROM hurricanes_filtered
    WHERE "r34_ne" IS NOT NULL
      AND "r34_se" IS NOT NULL
      AND "r34_sw" IS NOT NULL
      AND "r34_nw" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Convert the four points into a closed polygon representing the storm area
storm_geom AS (
    SELECT
        "sid",
        "name",
        "season",
        "wind",
        "category",
        ST_MAKEPOLYGON(
            ST_MAKELINE(
                ST_MAKELINE(
                    ST_MAKELINE(
                        ST_MAKELINE("ne_point", "se_point"),
                        "sw_point"
                    ),
                    "nw_point"
                ),
                "ne_point"
            )
        ) AS "storm_polygon"
    FROM storm_polygons
),

-- Step 4: Join ports with storm areas that contain the port
port_storms AS (
    SELECT
        pu."port_name",
        pu."state_name",
        pu."port_geog",
        sg."sid",
        sg."name",
        sg."season",
        sg."wind",
        sg."category",
        sg."storm_polygon"
    FROM ports_us pu
    JOIN storm_geom sg
        ON ST_WITHIN(pu."port_geog", sg."storm_polygon")
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate per port
port_aggregated AS (
    SELECT
        "port_name",
        "state_name",
        "port_geog",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT "season", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "season") AS "distinct_years",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "sid") AS "total_distinct_storms",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT "name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "name") AS "distinct_storm_names",
        ROUND(AVG("category"), 4) AS "average_storm_category",
        ROUND(AVG("wind"), 4) AS "average_wind_speed",
        ST_UNION_AGG("storm_polygon") AS "tropical_storm_area_geometry"
    FROM port_storms
    GROUP BY "port_name", "state_name", "port_geog"
)

-- Step 6: Final output
SELECT
    "port_name",
    "state_name",
    "distinct_years",
    "total_distinct_storms",
    "distinct_storm_names",
    "average_storm_category",
    "average_wind_speed",
    "port_geog" AS "port_geometry",
    "tropical_storm_area_geometry"
FROM port_aggregated
ORDER BY "port_name";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- First, let's check if state_zone '6585' exists
region_check AS (
  SELECT 
    state_zone,
    state,
    name AS port_name,
    shortname AS port_shortname,
    COUNT(*) as region_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.nws_forecast_regions`
  WHERE state_zone = '6585'
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
),

-- Named tropical storms in North Atlantic with wind >= 35 knots
named_storms AS (
  SELECT 
    sid,
    name,
    usa_latitude,
    usa_longitude,
    -- Use 34kt wind radii for storm extent
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(usa_r34_ne AS INT64), 0) AS r34_ne,
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(usa_r34_se AS INT64), 0) AS r34_se,
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(usa_r34_sw AS INT64), 0) AS r34_sw,
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(usa_r34_nw AS INT64), 0) AS r34_nw,
    usa_wind
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
  WHERE basin = 'NA'
    AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
    AND LOWER(name) NOT LIKE '%not_named%'
    AND usa_wind >= 35
    AND usa_latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND usa_longitude IS NOT NULL
),

-- Count total named storms for debugging
storm_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sid) as total_named_storms
  FROM named_storms
),

-- Create storm polygons using wind radii - simplified approach
storm_polygons AS (
  SELECT 
    ns.sid,
    ns.name,
    ns.usa_latitude,
    ns.usa_longitude,
    -- Create a circular buffer around the storm center using the maximum wind radius
    ST_BUFFER(
      ST_GEOGPOINT(ns.usa_longitude, ns.usa_latitude),
      -- Use the maximum wind radius in meters (1 nautical mile = 1852 meters)
      GREATEST(
        COALESCE(ns.r34_ne, 0),
        COALESCE(ns.r34_se, 0),
        COALESCE(ns.r34_sw, 0),
        COALESCE(ns.r34_nw, 0)
      ) * 1852  -- Convert nautical miles to meters
    ) AS storm_area
  FROM named_storms ns
  WHERE GREATEST(
    COALESCE(ns.r34_ne, 0),
    COALESCE(ns.r34_se, 0),
    COALESCE(ns.r34_sw, 0),
    COALESCE(ns.r34_nw, 0)
  ) > 0  -- Only include storms with some wind radius
),

-- Count storms with polygons for debugging
polygon_storm_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sid) as storms_with_polygons
  FROM storm_polygons
),

-- Try multiple potential port locations for region '6585'
-- Since we don't know the exact location, let's try several major US ports
potential_ports AS (
  SELECT 
    '6585' as state_zone,
    'LA' as state,
    'Port of New Orleans' as port_name,
    'New Orleans' as port_shortname,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-90.0715, 29.9511) AS port_location  -- New Orleans
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    '6585' as state_zone,
    'TX' as state,
    'Port of Houston' as port_name,
    'Houston' as port_shortname,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-95.3698, 29.7604) AS port_location  -- Houston
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    '6585' as state_zone,
    'FL' as state,
    'Port of Miami' as port_name,
    'Miami' as port_shortname,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-80.1918, 25.7617) AS port_location  -- Miami
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    '6585' as state_zone,
    'NY' as state,
    'Port of New York' as port_name,
    'New York' as port_shortname,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128) AS port_location  -- New York
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    '6585' as state_zone,
    'CA' as state,
    'Port of Los Angeles' as port_name,
    'Los Angeles' as port_shortname,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-118.2437, 34.0522) AS port_location  -- Los Angeles
),

-- Count port occurrences in storm areas
port_occurrences AS (
  SELECT 
    pp.state_zone,
    pp.state,
    pp.port_name,
    pp.port_shortname,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sp.sid) AS storm_occurrence_count,
    STRING_AGG(DISTINCT sp.name, ', ' ORDER BY sp.name) as storm_names
  FROM potential_ports pp
  CROSS JOIN storm_polygons sp
  WHERE ST_WITHIN(pp.port_location, sp.storm_area)
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
),

-- Rank ports by occurrence frequency
ranked_ports AS (
  SELECT 
    state_zone,
    state,
    port_name,
    port_shortname,
    storm_occurrence_count,
    storm_names,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY storm_occurrence_count DESC) AS rank
  FROM port_occurrences
)

-- Return the most frequent port with debugging info
SELECT 
  state_zone AS region_number,
  state,
  port_name,
  port_shortname,
  storm_occurrence_count,
  storm_names,
  (SELECT total_named_storms FROM storm_count) as total_named_storms,
  (SELECT storms_with_polygons FROM polygon_storm_count) as storms_with_polygons,
  (SELECT region_count FROM region_check LIMIT 1) as region_6585_exists
FROM ranked_ports
WHERE rank = 1
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
-- Define temporary functions as required
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION nautical_miles_conversion(input_nautical_miles FLOAT64)
RETURNS FLOAT64
AS (
  input_nautical_miles * 1.15078
);

CREATE TEMP FUNCTION azimuth_to_geog_point(input_lat FLOAT64, input_lon FLOAT64, azimuth FLOAT64, distance FLOAT64)
RETURNS GEOGRAPHY
AS (
  ST_MAKEPOINT(
    57.2958 * (
      input_lon * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
        SIN(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)),
        COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
          57.2958 * ASIN(
            SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
            COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    57.2958 * ASIN(
      SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
      COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
    )
  )
);

WITH
  -- Filter hurricanes: North Atlantic, named, wind >= 35 kt, non-null quadrant radii
  hurricane_obs AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      usa_r34_ne,
      usa_r34_se,
      usa_r34_sw,
      usa_r34_nw
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
    WHERE basin = 'NA'
      AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
      AND usa_wind >= 35
      AND usa_r34_ne IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_se IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_sw IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_nw IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- Build polygons representing the 34-kt wind field (four quadrant points)
  storm_polygons AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      ST_MAKEPOLYGON(
        -- Build a closed linestring: p1 -> p2 -> p3 -> p4 -> p1
        ST_MAKELINE(
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne),
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 135, usa_r34_se)
          ),
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 225, usa_r34_sw),
            ST_MAKELINE(
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 315, usa_r34_nw),
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne)  -- close the loop
            )
          )
        )
      ) AS storm_area
    FROM hurricane_obs
  ),
  -- U.S. states (50 states + DC)
  us_states AS (
    SELECT state_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states`
    WHERE state_name IN (
      'Alabama','Alaska','Arizona','Arkansas','California','Colorado','Connecticut','Delaware',
      'Florida','Georgia','Hawaii','Idaho','Illinois','Indiana','Iowa','Kansas','Kentucky',
      'Louisiana','Maine','Maryland','Massachusetts','Michigan','Minnesota','Mississippi',
      'Missouri','Montana','Nebraska','Nevada','New Hampshire','New Jersey','New Mexico',
      'New York','North Carolina','North Dakota','Ohio','Oklahoma','Oregon','Pennsylvania',
      'Rhode Island','South Carolina','South Dakota','Tennessee','Texas','Utah','Vermont',
      'Virginia','Washington','West Virginia','Wisconsin','Wyoming','District of Columbia'
    )
  ),
  -- Ports with region_number '6585' that lie within a U.S. state boundary
  ports_in_us AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      p.port_name,
      p.port_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` p
    CROSS JOIN us_states s
    WHERE p.region_number = '6585'
      AND ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
  ),
  -- Count how many storm polygons contain each port
  port_storm_counts AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_name,
      COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM ports_in_us p
    JOIN storm_polygons sp
      ON ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, sp.storm_area)
    GROUP BY p.port_name
  )
-- Return the port with the highest count
SELECT port_name
FROM port_storm_counts
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>
