```sql
        ROUND(AVG("duration_minutes"), 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
    FROM active_station_trips
    GROUP BY "station_id"
),

-- Step 3: Compute the grand total of trips from all active stations
overall_total AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "grand_total"
    FROM station_stats
),

-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips (DENSE_RANK includes ties)
ranked_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        "total_trips",
        "avg_duration_minutes",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM station_stats
)

-- Step 5: Final selection of top 15 stations (including ties)
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND("total_trips" * 100.0 / (SELECT "grand_total" FROM overall_total), 4) AS "percentage",
    "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM ranked_stations
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH grid_qianjiang AS (
  -- Get all GRID IDs for organizations in Qianjiang city
  SELECT id AS grid_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.grid`
  WHERE LOWER(address.city) = 'qianjiang'
),
publication_grid_associations AS (
  -- Find publications associated with Qianjiang GRID organizations
  -- through authors' affiliations
  SELECT DISTINCT p.id AS publication_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p,
    UNNEST(authors) AS author,
    UNNEST(author.affiliations_address) AS affiliation
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.date_inserted) >= 2021
    AND affiliation.grid_id IN (SELECT grid_id FROM grid_qianjiang)
  
  UNION DISTINCT
  
  -- Through funding details
  SELECT DISTINCT p.id AS publication_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p,
    UNNEST(funding_details) AS funding
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.date_inserted) >= 2021
    AND funding.grid_id IN (SELECT grid_id FROM grid_qianjiang)
  
  UNION DISTINCT
  
  -- Through research_orgs (if they contain GRID IDs)
  SELECT DISTINCT p.id AS publication_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p,
    UNNEST(research_orgs) AS org_id
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.date_inserted) >= 2021
    AND org_id IN (SELECT grid_id FROM grid_qianjiang)
),
qualified_publications AS (
  -- Get the venue information for qualified publications
  SELECT 
    p.id,
    -- Priority logic for venue title
    COALESCE(
      -- 1. Journal title (if exists and not empty/None)
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.journal.title, 'None'), ''),
      -- 2. Proceedings title (preferred then original)
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.proceedings_title.preferred, 'None'), ''),
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.proceedings_title.original, 'None'), ''),
      -- 3. Book title (preferred then original)
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.book_title.preferred, 'None'), ''),
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.book_title.original, 'None'), ''),
      -- 4. Book series title (preferred then original)
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.book_series_title.preferred, 'None'), ''),
      NULLIF(NULLIF(p.book_series_title.original, 'None'), ''),
      -- Fallback if none available
      'No venue title available'
    ) AS venue_title
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p
  INNER JOIN publication_grid_associations a ON p.id = a.publication_id
)
-- Final result: venue titles for qualified publications
SELECT DISTINCT venue_title
FROM qualified_publications
WHERE venue_title != 'No venue title available'
ORDER BY venue_title;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Retrieve venue titles of publications meeting two conditions:
-- 1. date_inserted from 2021 onwards
-- 2. associated (via supporting grants) with a grid organisation whose city is 'Qianjiang'
-- For each publication pick the first available: journal.title, proceedings_title.preferred, book_title.preferred, book_series_title.preferred
SELECT DISTINCT
  COALESCE(
    journal.title,
    proceedings_title.preferred,
    book_title.preferred,
    book_series_title.preferred
  ) AS venue_title
FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_inserted) >= 2021
  -- Check if the publication is linked to any grant whose organisation_details contain a city 'Qianjiang'
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST(p.supporting_grant_ids) AS grant_id
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.grants` g
      ON g.id = grant_id
    LEFT JOIN UNNEST(g.organisation_details) AS org
    WHERE org.city = 'Qianjiang'
  )
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH all_activities AS (
  -- Step 1: All activities with non-null standard values (regardless of pChEMBL)
  SELECT
    activity_id,
    molregno,
    assay_id,
    standard_type,
    standard_value,
    standard_relation,
    pchembl_value,
    doc_id,
    potential_duplicate,
    SAFE_CAST(standard_value AS FLOAT64) AS standard_value_num,
    SAFE_CAST(pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) AS pchembl_value_num
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_29`
  WHERE standard_value IS NOT NULL 
    AND standard_value != 'None'
),

activity_counts AS (
  -- Step 2: Count total activities and duplicates per (molecule, assay, standard_type)
  SELECT
    molregno,
    assay_id,
    standard_type,
    COUNT(*) AS total_activities,
    SUM(CASE WHEN potential_duplicate = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS duplicate_count
  FROM all_activities
  GROUP BY molregno, assay_id, standard_type
  HAVING total_activities < 5 AND duplicate_count < 2
),

activities_with_counts AS (
  -- Step 3: Keep only activities that meet the count criteria and have pChEMBL > 10
  SELECT
    a.activity_id,
    a.molregno,
    a.assay_id,
    a.standard_type,
    a.standard_value,
    a.standard_relation,
    a.pchembl_value,
    a.doc_id,
    a.potential_duplicate,
    a.standard_value_num,
    a.pchembl_value_num
  FROM all_activities a
  JOIN activity_counts ac
    ON a.molregno = ac.molregno
   AND a.assay_id = ac.assay_id
   AND a.standard_type = ac.standard_type
  WHERE a.pchembl_value IS NOT NULL
    AND a.pchembl_value != 'None'
    AND a.pchembl_value_num > 10
),

activities_with_properties AS (
  -- Step 4: Join with compound properties and structures
  SELECT
    ac.*,
    cp.heavy_atoms,
    cs.canonical_smiles,
    SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) AS heavy_atoms_num
  FROM activities_with_counts ac
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties_29` cp
    ON ac.molregno = cp.molregno
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures_29` cs
    ON ac.molregno = cs.molregno
  WHERE cp.heavy_atoms IS NOT NULL 
    AND cp.heavy_atoms != 'None'
    AND SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
),

docs_with_rank AS (
  -- Step 5: Prepare documents with percent rank
  SELECT
    doc_id,
    journal,
    year,
    first_page,
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY journal, year
      ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64)
    ) AS pct_rank
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs_29`
  WHERE journal IS NOT NULL
    AND year IS NOT NULL
    AND first_page IS NOT NULL
),

docs_with_synthetic_date AS (
  -- Step 6: Compute synthetic publication date (fixed MOD and FLOOR type issues)
  SELECT
    doc_id,
    journal,
    year,
    first_page,
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), 1970) AS pub_year,
    CAST(FLOOR(IFNULL(pct_rank, 0) * 11) AS INT64) + 1 AS pub_month,
    MOD(CAST(FLOOR(IFNULL(pct_rank, 0) * 308) AS INT64), 28) + 1 AS pub_day
  FROM docs_with_rank
),

activities_with_dates AS (
  -- Step 7: Attach synthetic publication dates
  SELECT
    ap.*,
    d.pub_year,
    d.pub_month,
    d.pub_day,
    DATE(d.pub_year, d.pub_month, d.pub_day) AS publication_date
  FROM activities_with_properties ap
  LEFT JOIN docs_with_synthetic_date d
    ON ap.doc_id = d.doc_id
),

molecule_pairs AS (
  -- Step 8: Create pairs of different molecules in same assay and standard type
  SELECT
    a1.molregno AS molregno1,
    a2.molregno AS molregno2,
    a1.assay_id,
    a1.standard_type,
    a1.activity_id AS activity_id1,
    a2.activity_id AS activity_id2,
    a1.canonical_smiles AS smiles1,
    a2.canonical_smiles AS smiles2,
    a1.heavy_atoms_num AS heavy_atoms1,
    a2.heavy_atoms_num AS heavy_atoms2,
    a1.standard_value_num AS standard_value1,
    a2.standard_value_num AS standard_value2,
    a1.standard_relation AS relation1,
    a2.standard_relation AS relation2,
    a1.publication_date AS pub_date1,
    a2.publication_date AS pub_date2,
    a1.doc_id AS doc_id1,
    a2.doc_id AS doc_id2
  FROM activities_with_dates a1
  JOIN activities_with_dates a2
    ON a1.assay_id = a2.assay_id
   AND a1.standard_type = a2.standard_type
   AND a1.molregno < a2.molregno
)

-- Step 9: Final selection with required fields
SELECT
  molregno1,
  molregno2,
  assay_id,
  standard_type,
  GREATEST(heavy_atoms1, heavy_atoms2) AS max_heavy_atoms,
  GREATEST(pub_date1, pub_date2) AS latest_publication_date,
  GREATEST(doc_id1, doc_id2) AS highest_doc_id,
  CASE
    WHEN relation1 IN ('=', '~') AND relation2 IN ('=', '~') 
         AND ROUND(standard_value1, 4) = ROUND(standard_value2, 4) THEN 'no-change'
    WHEN (relation1 IN ('>', '>>') OR relation2 IN ('<', '<<'))
         AND standard_value1 > standard_value2 THEN 'decrease'
    WHEN (relation1 IN ('<', '<<') OR relation2 IN ('>', '>>'))
         AND standard_value1 < standard_value2 THEN 'increase'
    WHEN relation1 = '=' AND relation2 = '=' THEN
      CASE
        WHEN standard_value1 > standard_value2 THEN 'decrease'
        WHEN standard_value1 < standard_value2 THEN 'increase'
        ELSE 'no-change'
      END
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS standard_change_classification,
  TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(activity_id1, smiles1)))) AS uuid_molecule1,
  TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(activity_id2, smiles2)))) AS uuid_molecule2,
  -- Additional verification columns (optional)
  activity_id1,
  activity_id2,
  heavy_atoms1,
  heavy_atoms2,
  standard_value1,
  standard_value2,
  relation1,
  relation2,
  pub_date1,
  pub_date2
FROM molecule_pairs
WHERE pub_date1 IS NOT NULL 
  AND pub_date2 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY assay_id, molregno1, molregno2;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Use tables from ChEMBL release 29 (based on external knowledge)
WITH 
-- Compute synthetic publication date for each document
docs_with_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    journal,
    year,
    first_page,
    -- Year: use publication year, default 1970 if missing
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), 1970) AS pub_year,
    -- Percent rank within same journal and year, ordered by first page numeric value
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY journal, year 
      ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64)
    ) AS pct_rank
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs_29`
  WHERE journal IS NOT NULL AND year IS NOT NULL AND first_page IS NOT NULL
),
-- Compute month and day from percent rank, then construct date
doc_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    pub_year,
    -- Month: floor(pct_rank * 11) + 1
    FLOOR(pct_rank * 11) + 1 AS pub_month,
    -- Day: (floor(pct_rank * 308) % 28) + 1
    MOD(FLOOR(pct_rank * 308), 28) + 1 AS pub_day
  FROM docs_with_date
),
-- Prepare filtered activities with all required conditions
filtered_activities AS (
  SELECT 
    a.activity_id,
    a.assay_id,
    a.standard_type,
    a.molregno,
    a.doc_id,
    a.standard_value,
    a.standard_relation,
    a.pchembl_value,
    -- Heavy atoms (cast to int)
    SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) AS heavy_atoms,
    -- Canonical SMILES
    cs.canonical_smiles,
    -- Document date
    dd.pub_year,
    dd.pub_month,
    dd.pub_day,
    -- Synthetic date as DATE
    DATE(dd.pub_year, dd.pub_month, dd.pub_day) AS pub_date,
    -- Count activities per (molregno, assay) and duplicate count
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS activity_count,
    COUNTIF(a.potential_duplicate = '1') OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS duplicate_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_29` a
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties_29` cp
    ON a.molregno = cp.molregno
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures_29` cs
    ON a.molregno = cs.molregno
  JOIN doc_date dd
    ON a.doc_id = dd.doc_id
  WHERE 
    -- Non-null standard value
    a.standard_value IS NOT NULL
    -- pChEMBL > 10
    AND SAFE_CAST(a.pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) > 10
    -- Heavy atoms between 10 and 15 inclusive
    AND SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
    -- Standard relation must be '=' for unambiguous comparison
    AND a.standard_relation = '='
)
-- Now find pairs of different molecules in same assay and standard type
SELECT 
  -- Maximum heavy atom count (as integer)
  GREATEST(a.heavy_atoms, b.heavy_atoms) AS max_heavy_atom_count,
  -- Latest publication date
  GREATEST(a.pub_date, b.pub_date) AS latest_publication_date,
  -- Highest document ID
  GREATEST(a.doc_id, b.doc_id) AS highest_doc_id,
  -- Classify change in standard values
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) > SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'decrease'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) < SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'increase'
    ELSE 'no-change'
  END AS change_classification,
  -- UUID generated from both activity IDs and both canonical SMILES
  TO_HEX(
    MD5(
      TO_JSON_STRING(
        STRUCT(a.activity_id AS a1, b.activity_id AS a2, a.canonical_smiles AS s1, b.canonical_smiles AS s2)
      )
    )
  ) AS pair_uuid
FROM filtered_activities a
JOIN filtered_activities b
  ON a.assay_id = b.assay_id
    AND a.standard_type = b.standard_type
    AND a.molregno < b.molregno
WHERE 
  -- Both molecules must satisfy the activity count conditions
  a.activity_count < 5
  AND b.activity_count < 5
  AND a.duplicate_count < 2
  AND b.duplicate_count < 2;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH committees_with_candidates AS (
  -- Get committees that supported at least one candidate in 2016
  SELECT DISTINCT cmte_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016`
),
small_dollar_totals AS (
  -- Calculate total small-dollar contributions per committee
  SELECT 
    cmte_id,
    SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_contributions_2016`
  WHERE transaction_amt > 0 
    AND transaction_amt < 200
  GROUP BY cmte_id
  HAVING SUM(transaction_amt) > 0
),
qualifying_committees AS (
  -- Committees that have both candidates and small-dollar contributions
  SELECT 
    cc.cmte_id
  FROM committees_with_candidates cc
  INNER JOIN small_dollar_totals sdt
    ON cc.cmte_id = sdt.cmte_id
),
committee_candidate_info AS (
  -- Get candidate details for each qualifying committee
  SELECT 
    qc.cmte_id,
    cc.cand_id,
    c.cand_name
  FROM qualifying_committees qc
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` cc
    ON qc.cmte_id = cc.cmte_id
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016` c
    ON cc.cand_id = c.cand_id
)
-- Final result with all required columns
SELECT 
  cmt.cmte_nm AS committee_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cci.cand_id) AS num_unique_candidates,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT cci.cand_name, ', ' ORDER BY cci.cand_name) AS candidate_names,
  ROUND(sdt.total_small_dollar, 2) AS total_small_dollar_sum
FROM qualifying_committees qc
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_2016` cmt
  ON qc.cmte_id = cmt.cmte_id
INNER JOIN small_dollar_totals sdt
  ON qc.cmte_id = sdt.cmte_id
INNER JOIN committee_candidate_info cci
  ON qc.cmte_id = cci.cmte_id
GROUP BY 
  cmt.cmte_nm,
  sdt.total_small_dollar
ORDER BY committee_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH small_dollar_committees AS (
    -- Find committees with individual contributions > $0 and < $200, summing to > $0
    SELECT 
        cmte_id,
        SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_contributions_2016`
    WHERE transaction_amt > 0 AND transaction_amt < 200
    GROUP BY cmte_id
    HAVING SUM(transaction_amt) > 0
),
committee_candidate_links AS (
    -- Get committees that supported at least one candidate in the 2016 election cycle
    SELECT DISTINCT
        cc.cmte_id,
        cc.cand_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` cc
    WHERE cc.fec_election_yr = 2016
),
qualifying_committees AS (
    -- Committees that have small-dollar contributions AND support at least one candidate
    SELECT 
        sdc.cmte_id,
        sdc.total_small_dollar
    FROM small_dollar_committees sdc
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM committee_candidate_links ccl 
        WHERE ccl.cmte_id = sdc.cmte_id
    )
),
committee_candidates AS (
    -- Resolve committee names and linked candidate names for qualifying committees
    SELECT 
        qc.cmte_id,
        c.cmte_nm,
        qc.total_small_dollar,
        cand.cand_id,
        cand.cand_name
    FROM qualifying_committees qc
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_2016` c ON qc.cmte_id = c.cmte_id
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` cc ON qc.cmte_id = cc.cmte_id
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016` cand ON cc.cand_id = cand.cand_id
    WHERE cc.fec_election_yr = 2016
)
-- Final aggregation: one row per committee with candidate list, count, and total
SELECT 
    cmte_nm AS committee_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cand_id) AS unique_candidates_count,
    STRING_AGG(cand_name, ', ' ORDER BY cand_name) AS candidates_names,
    total_small_dollar
FROM committee_candidates
GROUP BY cmte_id, cmte_nm, total_small_dollar
ORDER BY cmte_nm;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH cleaned_food_events AS (
  SELECT 
    report_number,
    -- Original columns
    products_role,
    date_started,
    products_industry_code,
    date_created,
    reactions,
    consumer_age_unit,
    products_brand_name,
    consumer_gender,
    products_industry_name,
    consumer_age,
    outcomes,
    
    -- Data cleansing operations
    -- 1. Split reactions and outcomes into arrays by commas
    SPLIT(reactions, ', ') AS reactions_array,
    SPLIT(outcomes, ', ') AS outcomes_array,
    
    -- 2. Handle products_brand_name: preserve digit,comma,digit patterns, replace other ", " with " -- "
    -- First, protect digit-comma-digit patterns by replacing comma with a temporary marker
    -- Then replace remaining ", " with " -- ", then restore the protected patterns
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        products_brand_name,
        r'(\d),(\d)',  -- Match digit,comma,digit (no space)
        r'\1@@@\2'     -- Replace comma with temporary marker @@@
      ),
      ', ',            -- Replace other comma+space combinations
      ' -- '
    ) AS products_brand_name_cleaned,
    
    -- 3. Replace ", " with " -- " in products_industry_code, products_role, and products_industry_name
    REPLACE(products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_code_cleaned,
    REPLACE(products_role, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_role_cleaned,
    REPLACE(products_industry_name, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_name_cleaned
    
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
  WHERE 
    -- Filter for dates between Jan 1-31, 2015
    date_created BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
    AND date_started BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
)

SELECT 
  -- Original columns (using cleaned versions where applicable)
  report_number,
  products_role_cleaned AS products_role,
  date_started,
  products_industry_code_cleaned AS products_industry_code,
  date_created,
  reactions_array,
  consumer_age_unit,
  -- Restore the protected digit-comma-digit patterns in brand name
  REPLACE(products_brand_name_cleaned, '@@@', ',') AS products_brand_name,
  consumer_gender,
  products_industry_name_cleaned AS products_industry_name,
  consumer_age,
  outcomes_array,
  
  -- Calculate array lengths after splitting
  -- For industry_code: split by " -- " since we replaced ", " with " -- "
  ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(products_industry_code_cleaned, ' -- ')) AS industry_code_length,
  
  -- For brand_name: need to handle the temporary markers first, then split
  ARRAY_LENGTH(
    SPLIT(
      REPLACE(products_brand_name_cleaned, '@@@', ','), 
      ' -- '
    )
  ) AS brand_name_length
  
FROM cleaned_food_events
ORDER BY date_created, report_number;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter rows by date range
  filtered_events AS (
    SELECT
      report_number,
      reactions,
      outcomes,
      date_created,
      date_started,
      consumer_gender,
      consumer_age,
      consumer_age_unit,
      products_brand_name,
      products_industry_code,
      products_role,
      products_industry_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
    WHERE date_created BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
      AND date_started BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
  ),

  -- Step 2: Apply all data cleansing transformations
  transformed_events AS (
    SELECT
      report_number,
      -- Split reactions into array by comma-space
      SPLIT(reactions, ', ') AS reactions,
      -- Split outcomes into array by comma-space
      SPLIT(outcomes, ', ') AS outcomes,
      date_created,
      date_started,
      consumer_gender,
      consumer_age,
      consumer_age_unit,
      -- products_brand_name: replace ", " with " -- " except when part of a digit-digit numeric pattern
      REGEXP_REPLACE(products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d), (?!\d)', ' -- ') AS products_brand_name,
      -- products_industry_code: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_code,
      -- products_role: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_role, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_role,
      -- products_industry_name: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_industry_name, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_name,
      -- Calculate industry_code_length = array length after splitting by " -- "
      ARRAY_LENGTH(
        SPLIT(REPLACE(products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- '), ' -- ')
      ) AS industry_code_length,
      -- Calculate brand_name_length = array length after splitting by " -- "
      ARRAY_LENGTH(
        SPLIT(
          REGEXP_REPLACE(products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d), (?!\d)', ' -- '),
          ' -- '
        )
      ) AS brand_name_length
    FROM filtered_events
  )

-- Final output: the cleansed food events data
SELECT *
FROM transformed_events
ORDER BY report_number;
```
</details>

### 119. sf_bq423 (DB: `GOOGLE_ADS`)
**Question**: Between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2024, which image-type advertisement on the topic of Health, published by a verified advertiser located in Cyprus, was shown in Croatia, has times_shown_availability_date as NULL (meaning the times shown data is available), utilized demographic information, geo-location targeting, contextual signals, customer lists, and topics of interest without any of these selection methods being unused, and additionally had its first shown date strictly after January 1, 2023, and last shown date strictly before January 1, 2024? Among such ads, provide the page URL of the one with the highest upper bound of times shown.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT cs."creative_page_url"
FROM "GOOGLE_ADS"."GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER"."CREATIVE_STATS" AS cs,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cs."region_stats") AS r
WHERE cs."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
  AND cs."topic" = 'Health'
  AND cs."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
  AND cs."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
  AND r.value:"region_code"::STRING = 'HR'
  AND r.value:"times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL
  AND r.value:"first_shown"::DATE > '2023-01-01'
  AND r.value:"last_shown"::DATE < '2024-01-01'
  -- All five audience selection methods must not be 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
ORDER BY r.value:"times_shown_upper_bound"::INTEGER DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "flattened" AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."ad_format_type",
        cs."topic",
        cs."advertiser_verification_status",
        cs."advertiser_location",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info",
        r.value AS "region_entry"
    FROM GOOGLE_ADS.GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER.CREATIVE_STATS cs,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cs."region_stats") r
)
SELECT 
    f."creative_page_url"
FROM "flattened" f
WHERE f."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
  AND f."topic" = 'Health'
  AND f."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
  AND f."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
  AND f."region_entry":"region_code"::TEXT = 'HR'
  AND f."region_entry":"times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL
  AND f."region_entry":"first_shown"::DATE > '2023-01-01'
  AND f."region_entry":"last_shown"::DATE < '2024-01-01'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
ORDER BY f."region_entry":"times_shown_upper_bound"::INTEGER DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH sorafenib_drugs AS (
  -- Get drugID for sorafenib from synonyms
  SELECT DISTINCT drugID
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.drug_synonyms_v1`
  WHERE LOWER(synonym) LIKE '%sorafenib%'
),

qualifying_targets AS (
  -- Get sorafenib targets meeting assay conditions (join only on expID)
  SELECT DISTINCT 
    i.target_uniprotID,
    i.targetID
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e
    ON i.expID = e.expID
  WHERE i.drugID IN (SELECT drugID FROM sorafenib_drugs)
    AND i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
    AND (e.exp_assayValueLow <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueLow IS NULL)
    AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueHigh IS NULL)
    AND i.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL
),

all_human_targets AS (
  -- Get all Homo sapiens targets for non-targets calculation
  SELECT DISTINCT target_uniprotID
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1`
  WHERE targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL
),

eligible_pathways AS (
  -- Get lowest-level Homo sapiens pathways with TAS evidence
  SELECT DISTINCT 
    p.stable_id,
    p.name,
    p.url
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` p
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pp
    ON p.stable_id = pp.pathway_stable_id
  WHERE p.lowest_level = TRUE
    AND p.species = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND pp.evidence_code = 'TAS'
),

pathway_mapping AS (
  -- Map Uniprot IDs to pathways via physical entities
  SELECT DISTINCT 
    ep.stable_id AS pathway_stable_id,
    ep.name AS pathway_name,
    ep.url AS pathway_url,
    pe.uniprot_id
  FROM eligible_pathways ep
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pp
    ON ep.stable_id = pp.pathway_stable_id
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
    ON pp.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
  WHERE pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
    AND pp.evidence_code = 'TAS'
),

pathway_counts AS (
  -- Calculate contingency table counts for each pathway
  SELECT 
    pm.pathway_stable_id,
    pm.pathway_name,
    pm.pathway_url,
    -- Targets in pathway (a)
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE 
      WHEN qt.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL 
      THEN qt.target_uniprotID 
    END) AS targets_in_pathway,
    -- Total qualifying targets (for targets outside pathway calculation)
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT target_uniprotID) FROM qualifying_targets) AS total_qualifying_targets,
    -- Non-targets in pathway (c)
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE 
      WHEN aht.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL 
      AND qt.target_uniprotID IS NULL 
      THEN aht.target_uniprotID 
    END) AS non_targets_in_pathway,
    -- Total non-targets (all human targets minus qualifying targets)
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT target_uniprotID) FROM all_human_targets) 
    - (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT target_uniprotID) FROM qualifying_targets) AS total_non_targets
  FROM pathway_mapping pm
  LEFT JOIN qualifying_targets qt
    ON pm.uniprot_id = qt.target_uniprotID
  LEFT JOIN all_human_targets aht
    ON pm.uniprot_id = aht.target_uniprotID
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
),

chi_squared_calc AS (
  -- Calculate chi-squared statistic for each pathway
  SELECT 
    pathway_stable_id,
    pathway_name,
    pathway_url,
    targets_in_pathway AS a,
    total_qualifying_targets - targets_in_pathway AS b,  -- Targets outside pathway
    non_targets_in_pathway AS c,
    total_non_targets - non_targets_in_pathway AS d,     -- Non-targets outside pathway
    -- Chi-squared formula: (ad - bc)� * (a+b+c+d) / ((a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d))
    CASE 
      WHEN (total_qualifying_targets * total_non_targets) = 0 THEN 0
      ELSE 
        POWER(
          (targets_in_pathway * (total_non_targets - non_targets_in_pathway) - 
          (total_qualifying_targets - targets_in_pathway) * non_targets_in_pathway), 2
        ) * (total_qualifying_targets + total_non_targets) /
        NULLIF(
          total_qualifying_targets * total_non_targets * 
          (targets_in_pathway + non_targets_in_pathway) * 
          ((total_qualifying_targets - targets_in_pathway) + (total_non_targets - non_targets_in_pathway)),
          0
        )
    END AS chi_squared_statistic
  FROM pathway_counts
  WHERE total_qualifying_targets > 0
    AND total_non_targets > 0
),

ranked_pathways AS (
  -- Rank pathways by chi-squared statistic
  SELECT 
    pathway_stable_id,
    pathway_name,
    pathway_url,
    a AS targets_in_pathway,
    b AS targets_outside_pathway,
    c AS non_targets_in_pathway,
    d AS non_targets_outside_pathway,
    chi_squared_statistic,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY chi_squared_statistic DESC) AS pathway_rank
  FROM chi_squared_calc
  WHERE chi_squared_statistic IS NOT NULL
)

-- Final output: top 3 pathways with counts
SELECT 
  pathway_stable_id,
  pathway_name,
  pathway_url,
  targets_in_pathway,
  targets_outside_pathway,
  non_targets_in_pathway,
  non_targets_outside_pathway,
  ROUND(chi_squared_statistic, 4) AS chi_squared_statistic,
  pathway_rank
FROM ranked_pathways
WHERE pathway_rank <= 3
ORDER BY pathway_rank;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- 1. Distinct human targets of sorafenib satisfying assay conditions
sorafenib_targets AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT i.target_uniprotID AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e
    ON i.expID = e.expID
  WHERE LOWER(i.drugName) = 'sorafenib'
    AND i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
    AND (e.exp_assayValueLow   <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueLow   IS NULL)
    AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh  <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueHigh  IS NULL)
),

-- 2. All human UniProt IDs that appear in any human Reactome pathway
human_pe_universe AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pe.uniprot_id AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pep
    ON pe.stable_id = pep.pe_stable_id
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
    ON pep.pathway_stable_id = pw.stable_id
  WHERE pw.species = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- 3. For each lowest‑level human pathway with TAS evidence, list its member UniProt IDs
pathway_pe_uniprot AS (
  SELECT pw.stable_id   AS pathway_id,
         pw.name        AS pathway_name,
         pe.uniprot_id  AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pep
    ON pw.stable_id = pep.pathway_stable_id
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
    ON pep.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
  WHERE pw.lowest_level = TRUE
    AND pw.species      = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND pep.evidence_code = 'TAS'
    AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- 4. Per pathway counts: total members and sorafenib target members
pathway_stats AS (
  SELECT p.pathway_id,
         p.pathway_name,
         COUNT(DISTINCT p.uniprot)                                  AS total_in_pathway,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.uniprot IS NOT NULL
                              THEN p.uniprot END)                  AS targets_in_pathway
  FROM pathway_pe_uniprot p
  LEFT JOIN sorafenib_targets s
    ON p.uniprot = s.uniprot
  GROUP BY p.pathway_id, p.pathway_name
),

-- 5. Global counts needed for chi‑squared calculation
overall_counts AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot) FROM sorafenib_targets) AS total_targets,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot) FROM human_pe_universe) AS total_universe
)

-- 6. Compute chi‑squared for each pathway, keep top 3, and output the requested counts
SELECT
  ps.pathway_name,
  ps.targets_in_pathway   AS targets_within_pathway,
  oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway   AS targets_outside_pathway,
  ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway   AS nontargets_within_pathway,
  oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) AS nontargets_outside_pathway
  -- Chi‑squared value is included for transparency (not explicitly requested)
  -- , ROUND(
  --   ( (ps.targets_in_pathway * 
  --        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway))
  --      - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) * (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)
  --     )^2 * oc.total_universe
  --   ) / NULLIF(
  --     ( (ps.targets_in_pathway + (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
  --       (ps.total_in_pathway + (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway)) *
  --       (ps.targets_in_pathway + (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
  --       ((oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) + 
  --        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)))
  --     ), 0
  --   ), 4
  -- ) AS chi_squared
FROM pathway_stats ps
CROSS JOIN overall_counts oc
ORDER BY
  -- Order by chi‑squared descending (computed inline with the same formula)
  ( (ps.targets_in_pathway * 
        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway))
      - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) * (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)
    )^2 * oc.total_universe
  ) / NULLIF(
    ( (ps.targets_in_pathway + (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
      (ps.total_in_pathway + (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway)) *
      (ps.targets_in_pathway + (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
      ((oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) + 
       (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)))
    ), 0
  ) DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH country_regions AS (
  SELECT 
    country_code,
    long_name AS country_name,
    region
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.country_summary`
  WHERE region IS NOT NULL 
    AND region != 'None'
)
SELECT 
  cr.country_name,
  cr.country_code,
  cr.region,
  ROUND(SUM(id.value), 4) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` AS id
INNER JOIN country_regions AS cr 
  ON id.country_code = cr.country_code
WHERE 
  id.indicator_code IN (
    'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD',   -- Long-term external debt stocks (DOD, current US$)
    'DT.DOD.DECT.CD',   -- External debt stocks, long-term (DOD, current US$)
    'DT.AMT.DLXF.CD'    -- Long-term external debt (disbursements, current US$)
  )
  AND id.value IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cr.country_name, cr.country_code, cr.region
ORDER BY total_long_term_external_debt DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the indicator for long-term external debt.
-- We use indicator_code 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD' (External debt stocks, long-term, current US$).
-- Step 2: Join the debt data with the country_summary table to obtain region information.
-- Step 3: Exclude rows where region is 'None' (i.e., regional aggregates).
-- Step 4: Aggregate by country, summing the debt values over all available years.
-- Step 5: Order by total debt descending and return the top 10 countries.

WITH filtered_debt AS (
  SELECT 
    d.country_code,
    d.country_name,
    d.value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` d
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.country_summary` c
    ON d.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE d.indicator_code = 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD'
    -- Filter out rows with missing or non-country regions
    AND c.region IS NOT NULL
    AND c.region != 'None'
    -- Exclude null/NaN debt values
    AND d.value IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT IS_NAN(d.value)
)
SELECT 
  country_name,
  ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM filtered_debt
GROUP BY country_name, country_code
ORDER BY total_long_term_external_debt DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
-- First, find projects that are feature toggle libraries
feature_toggle_projects AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    p.id AS project_id,
    p.name AS project_name,
    p.platform,
    ftl.library_name,
    ftl.languages AS library_languages
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.projects` p
  INNER JOIN feature_toggle_libraries ftl
    ON LOWER(p.name) = LOWER(ftl.artifact_name)
    AND LOWER(p.platform) = LOWER(ftl.platform)
),

-- Find repositories that depend on these projects via repository_dependencies
repositories_with_toggles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    rd.repository_id,
    rd.repository_name_with_owner,
    rd.host_type,
    ftp.project_name AS artifact_name,
    ftp.library_name,
    ftp.library_languages
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.repository_dependencies` rd
  INNER JOIN feature_toggle_projects ftp
    ON rd.dependency_project_id = ftp.project_id
  WHERE rd.repository_name_with_owner IS NOT NULL
),

-- Alternative approach: also check dependencies table for project-to-project dependencies
project_dependencies_with_toggles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    d.project_id AS dependent_project_id,
    d.project_name AS dependent_project_name,
    ftp.project_name AS artifact_name,
    ftp.library_name,
    ftp.library_languages
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.dependencies` d
  INNER JOIN feature_toggle_projects ftp
    ON d.dependency_project_id = ftp.project_id
),

-- Get repositories for projects that depend on feature toggle libraries
repositories_via_projects AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    pwr.repository_id,
    pwr.repository_name_with_owner,
    pwr.repository_host_type AS host_type,
    pdwt.artifact_name,
    pdwt.library_name,
    pdwt.library_languages
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.projects_with_repository_fields` pwr
  INNER JOIN project_dependencies_with_toggles pdwt
    ON pwr.id = pdwt.dependent_project_id
  WHERE pwr.repository_name_with_owner IS NOT NULL
    AND pwr.repository_name_with_owner != ''
),

-- Combine both approaches
all_repositories_with_toggles AS (
  SELECT * FROM repositories_with_toggles
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM repositories_via_projects
)

-- Main query to get all required repository details
SELECT DISTINCT
  arwt.repository_name_with_owner,
  arwt.host_type,
  -- Convert size from KB to bytes (multiply by 1024)
  COALESCE(r.size, 0) * 1024 AS size_bytes,
  COALESCE(pwr.repository_language, 'Unknown') AS primary_programming_language,
  COALESCE(r.fork_source_name_with_owner, 'Not a fork') AS fork_source_name,
  COALESCE(r.updated_timestamp, pwr.repository_updated_timestamp) AS last_update_timestamp,
  arwt.artifact_name,
  arwt.library_name,
  arwt.library_languages
FROM all_repositories_with_toggles arwt
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.repositories` r
  ON arwt.repository_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.libraries_io.projects_with_repository_fields` pwr
  ON arwt.repository_id = pwr.repository_id
WHERE arwt.repository_name_with_owner IS NOT NULL
  AND arwt.repository_name_with_owner != ''
ORDER BY arwt.repository_name_with_owner, arwt.library_name;
```

### 124. bq229 (DB: `open_images`)
**Question**: Using the bigquery-public-data.open_images dataset, can you provide a count of how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'cat' (where the image has label '/m/01yrx' with confidence=1) and how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'other' (meaning they have no cat label '/m/01yrx' at all)?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| category   |   url_count |
|:-----------|------------:|
| cat        |       40231 |
| other      |     9122224 |

**OR**

|   cat_count |   other_count |
|------------:|--------------:|
|       40231 |   9.12222e+06 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   cat_image_count |   other_image_count |
|------------------:|--------------------:|
|             40231 |         9.12222e+06 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Images with confident cat label
confident_cat_images AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels` l
  WHERE l.label_name = '/m/01yrx' 
    AND l.confidence = 1
),
-- All images with any cat label
any_cat_images AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels` l
  WHERE l.label_name = '/m/01yrx'
)
SELECT
  -- Cat images: have confident cat label
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.original_url)
   FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
   WHERE i.image_id IN (SELECT image_id FROM confident_cat_images)) AS cat_image_count,
  
  -- Other images: no cat label at all
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.original_url)
   FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
   WHERE i.image_id NOT IN (SELECT image_id FROM any_cat_images)) AS other_image_count;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Final complete SQL query
WITH 
-- Get all image URLs that are labeled as 'cat' with exactly confidence=1
cat_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.open_images.train_annotations` a 
        ON i.image_id = a.image_id
    WHERE a.label_id = '/m/01yrx' 
      AND a.confidence = 1
),

-- Get all image URLs that have ANY cat label (at any confidence level)
-- This is needed to determine 'other' images that have no cat label at all
cat_any_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.open_images.train_annotations` a 
        ON i.image_id = a.image_id
    WHERE a.label_id = '/m/01yrx'
),

-- Get all distinct image URLs from the entire dataset
all_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
)

-- Final selection: Count cat images and other images separately
SELECT 
    'cat' AS category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT image_url) AS image_count
FROM cat_images
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    'other' AS category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT image_url) AS image_count
FROM (
    SELECT image_url 
    FROM all_images
    EXCEPT DISTINCT
    SELECT image_url 
    FROM cat_any_images
)
```
</details>

```sql
WITH parent_forum AS (
    -- Find the parent forum titled "General"
    SELECT 
        "Id" AS "parent_forum_id",
        "Title" AS "parent_forum_title"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE LOWER("Title") = 'general'
),
sub_forums AS (
    -- Find all sub-forums under the "General" parent forum
    SELECT 
        f."Id" AS "sub_forum_id",
        f."Title" AS "sub_forum_title",
        pf."parent_forum_title"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS" f
    INNER JOIN parent_forum pf ON f."ParentForumId" = pf."parent_forum_id"
),
topics AS (
    -- Get topics from sub-forums with timestamp conversion
    SELECT 
        ft."Id" AS "topic_id",
        ft."Title" AS "topic_title",
        -- Convert Unix timestamp in microseconds to timestamp
        TO_TIMESTAMP(ft."CreationDate" / 1000000) AS "creation_timestamp",
        COALESCE(ft."TotalViews", 0) AS "total_views",
        sf."sub_forum_id",
        sf."parent_forum_title"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMTOPICS" ft
    INNER JOIN sub_forums sf ON ft."ForumId" = sf."sub_forum_id"
),
message_stats AS (
    -- Calculate reply counts and distinct users
    SELECT 
        fm."ForumTopicId",
        COUNT(*) AS "reply_count",
        COUNT(DISTINCT fm."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGES" fm
    INNER JOIN topics t ON fm."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
),
vote_stats AS (
    -- Calculate total upvotes per topic
    SELECT 
        fm."ForumTopicId",
        COUNT(fmv."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGES" fm
    LEFT JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGEVOTES" fmv 
        ON fm."Id" = fmv."ForumMessageId"
    INNER JOIN topics t ON fm."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
),
final_results AS (
    -- Combine all data
    SELECT 
        t."creation_timestamp" AS "CreationDate",
        COALESCE(t."topic_title", 'No Title') AS "title",
        t."parent_forum_title",
        COALESCE(ms."reply_count", 0) AS "reply_count",
        COALESCE(ms."distinct_user_replies", 0) AS "distinct_user_replies",
        COALESCE(vs."total_upvotes", 0) AS "total_upvotes",
        t."total_views"
    FROM topics t
    LEFT JOIN message_stats ms ON t."topic_id" = ms."ForumTopicId"
    LEFT JOIN vote_stats vs ON t."topic_id" = vs."ForumTopicId"
    ORDER BY t."creation_timestamp" ASC
    LIMIT 5
)
SELECT * FROM final_results;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the parent forum "General" and get its id
WITH "general_forum" AS (
    SELECT "id"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE LOWER("Title") LIKE '%general%'
),

-- Step 2: Get all sub-forums (children) of the General forum
"sub_forums" AS (
    SELECT "id" AS "forum_id"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE "ParentForumId" IN (SELECT "id" FROM "general_forum")
),

-- Step 3: Get the earliest 5 topics from any sub-forum under General
"earliest_topics" AS (
    SELECT 
        t."id" AS "topic_id",
        t."CreationDate",
        t."Title",
        f."Title" AS "parent_forum_title",
        t."ForumId",
        t."ViewCount"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMTOPICS" t
    INNER JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS" f
        ON t."ForumId" = f."id"
    WHERE f."id" IN (SELECT "forum_id" FROM "sub_forums")
    ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 4: Aggregate reply and user metrics per topic
"topic_metrics" AS (
    SELECT 
        et."topic_id",
        et."CreationDate",
        et."Title",
        et."parent_forum_title",
        COALESCE(COUNT(m."id"), 0) AS "reply_count",
        COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT m."UserId"), 0) AS "distinct_user_replies_count",
        COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m."VoteType" = 'Upvote' THEN m."id" END), 0) AS "total_upvotes",
        -- Note: ViewCount is already in the topic table
        COALESCE(et."ViewCount", 0) AS "total_views"
    FROM "earliest_topics" et
    LEFT JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGES" m
        ON et."topic_id" = m."TopicId"
    GROUP BY 
        et."topic_id",
        et."CreationDate",
        et."Title",
        et."parent_forum_title",
        et."ViewCount"
)

-- Step 5: Final output with required fields
SELECT 
    "CreationDate",
    "Title",
    "parent_forum_title",
    "reply_count",
    "distinct_user_replies_count",
    "total_upvotes",
    "total_views"
FROM "topic_metrics"
ORDER BY "CreationDate" ASC;
```

|---------------------:|:-----------------------|--------------------:|--------------------:|----------------:|
|                    6 | Gift Store             |                5796 |             5744.48 |           51.52 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify orders that do not appear in the invoice table
non_invoiced_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID"
    FROM 
        "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        WHERE si."OrderID" = so."OrderID"
    )
),

-- Step 2: Calculate order value (including tax) for each non-invoiced order
-- Using the same calculation as in SALES_INVOICELINES: UnitPrice * Quantity + TaxAmount
order_values AS (
    SELECT 
        nio."OrderID",
        nio."CustomerID",
        SUM(
            sol."UnitPrice" * sol."Quantity" + 
            (sol."UnitPrice" * sol."Quantity" * sol."TaxRate" / 100.0)
        ) AS "OrderValue"
    FROM 
        non_invoiced_orders nio
    JOIN 
        "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol 
        ON nio."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    GROUP BY 
        nio."OrderID", 
        nio."CustomerID"
),

-- Step 3: Get customer category for each order
orders_with_category AS (
    SELECT 
        ov."OrderID",
        ov."CustomerID",
        ov."OrderValue",
        sc."CustomerCategoryID"
    FROM 
        order_values ov
    JOIN 
        "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" sc 
        ON ov."CustomerID" = sc."CustomerID"
),

-- Step 4: Calculate maximum lost order value per customer category
max_lost_per_category AS (
    SELECT 
        cc."CustomerCategoryID",
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(owc."OrderValue") AS "MaxLostOrderValue"
    FROM 
        orders_with_category owc
    JOIN 
        "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc 
        ON owc."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY 
        cc."CustomerCategoryID", 
        cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 5: Calculate overall average of maximum lost order values
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG("MaxLostOrderValue") AS "OverallAvgMaxLost"
    FROM 
        max_lost_per_category
),

-- Step 6: Find which category's maximum lost order value is closest to the overall average
closest_category AS (
    SELECT 
        mlpc."CustomerCategoryID",
        mlpc."CustomerCategoryName",
        mlpc."MaxLostOrderValue",
        oa."OverallAvgMaxLost",
        ABS(mlpc."MaxLostOrderValue" - oa."OverallAvgMaxLost") AS "AbsDifference",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ABS(mlpc."MaxLostOrderValue" - oa."OverallAvgMaxLost") ASC) AS rn
    FROM 
        max_lost_per_category mlpc
    CROSS JOIN 
        overall_avg oa
)

-- Final output: The customer category whose maximum lost order value is closest to the overall average
SELECT 
    "CustomerCategoryID",
    "CustomerCategoryName",
    "MaxLostOrderValue",
    "OverallAvgMaxLost",
    "AbsDifference"
FROM 
    closest_category
WHERE 
    rn = 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Identify orders that do NOT appear in the invoice table
lost_orders AS (
    SELECT
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID"
    FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    LEFT JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        ON so."OrderID" = si."OrderID"
    WHERE si."InvoiceID" IS NULL
),

-- Step 2: Calculate the total value (Quantity * UnitPrice) for each lost order
order_values AS (
    SELECT
        lo."OrderID",
        SUM(sol."Quantity" * sol."UnitPrice") AS lost_order_value
    FROM lost_orders lo
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol
        ON lo."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    GROUP BY lo."OrderID"
),

-- Step 3: For each customer category, calculate the maximum lost order value
category_max_values AS (
    SELECT
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(ov.lost_order_value) AS max_lost_value
    FROM order_values ov
    INNER JOIN lost_orders lo
        ON ov."OrderID" = lo."OrderID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" c
        ON lo."CustomerID" = c."CustomerID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc
        ON c."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 4: Compute the overall average of these per-category maximum values
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(max_lost_value) AS avg_max_lost_value
    FROM category_max_values
)

-- Step 5: Determine which customer category's max value is closest to the overall average
SELECT
    cm."CustomerCategoryName" AS customer_category
FROM category_max_values cm
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
ORDER BY ROUND(ABS(cm.max_lost_value - oa.avg_max_lost_value), 4)
LIMIT 1;
```

### 128. bq393 (DB: `hacker_news`)
**Question**: I want to identify users who had activity followed by inactivity. Specifically, find the user ID and their corresponding month number (counting from their first activity month) for the user with the highest month number who became inactive (no activity recorded) after their last recorded activity month. For this analysis, only consider data up until September 10, 2024, and ensure the month number represents the count of months since the user's first activity. The user should have at least one month where they were expected to be active (within their activity span) but actually had no records.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| USER_ID     |   MONTH_NUMBER |
|:------------|---------------:|
| gaborcselle |            216 |

**OR**

| user_id   |   month_number |
|:----------|---------------:|
| adamsmith |            216 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| user_id     |   last_active_month_number |
|:------------|---------------------------:|
| gaborcselle |                        214 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH user_monthly_activity AS (
  -- Step 1: Get distinct user activity by month (up to Sep 10, 2024)
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `by` AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE timestamp <= TIMESTAMP('2024-09-10')
    AND `by` IS NOT NULL
    AND timestamp IS NOT NULL
),
user_first_activity AS (
  -- Step 2: Find each user's first activity month
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month) AS first_activity_month
  FROM user_monthly_activity
  GROUP BY user_id
),
user_activity_sequence AS (
  -- Step 3: Calculate month numbers and create complete sequence
  SELECT 
    uma.user_id,
    uma.activity_month,
    ufa.first_activity_month,
    DATE_DIFF(uma.activity_month, ufa.first_activity_month, MONTH) AS month_number,
    -- Get previous activity month for gap detection
    LAG(uma.activity_month) OVER (PARTITION BY uma.user_id ORDER BY uma.activity_month) AS prev_activity_month
  FROM user_monthly_activity uma
  JOIN user_first_activity ufa ON uma.user_id = ufa.user_id
),
activity_gaps AS (
  -- Step 4: Identify gaps in activity
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    activity_month,
    month_number,
    prev_activity_month,
    -- Check if there's a gap of more than 1 month since last activity
    DATE_DIFF(activity_month, prev_activity_month, MONTH) > 1 AS has_gap_before,
    -- Also check if this is the last activity and there's potential inactivity after
    LEAD(activity_month) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY activity_month) IS NULL AS is_last_activity
  FROM user_activity_sequence
),
user_inactivity_info AS (
  -- Step 5: Find users who became inactive and their last activity month number
  -- Fixed: Use subquery to allow referencing computed column in WHERE clause
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    last_active_month_number,
    last_activity_month,
    expected_next_month
  FROM (
    SELECT 
      user_id,
      month_number AS last_active_month_number,
      activity_month AS last_activity_month,
      DATE_ADD(activity_month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS expected_next_month,
      -- Calculate expected next month is before cutoff
      DATE_ADD(activity_month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) <= DATE_TRUNC(DATE('2024-09-10'), MONTH) AS has_expected_next_month,
      has_gap_before,
      is_last_activity
    FROM activity_gaps
  )
  WHERE is_last_activity = TRUE
    -- User must have at least one gap OR be missing expected activity months
    AND (has_gap_before = TRUE OR has_expected_next_month = TRUE)
),
ranked_users AS (
  -- Step 6: Rank users by highest month number when becoming inactive
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    last_active_month_number,
    last_activity_month,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY last_active_month_number DESC) AS rank_num
  FROM user_inactivity_info
)
-- Step 7: Return the user with highest month number who became inactive
SELECT 
  user_id,
  last_active_month_number
FROM ranked_users
WHERE rank_num = 1
ORDER BY last_active_month_number DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get distinct user activity months up to Sep 10, 2024
user_activity_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `by` AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE `by` IS NOT NULL 
    AND LOWER(TRIM(`by`)) != 'none'
    AND `by` != ''
    AND timestamp <= TIMESTAMP('2024-09-10')
),

-- Step 2: Compute first, last, count of active months, and span months for each user
user_first_last AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month) AS first_month,
    MAX(activity_month) AS last_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT activity_month) AS num_active_months,
    1 + DATE_DIFF(MAX(activity_month), MIN(activity_month), MONTH) AS span_months
  FROM user_activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
),

-- Step 3: Users who became inactive after last activity
-- Exclude users whose last activity is in Sep 2024 (cutoff month, can't verify inactivity)
users_inactive_after AS (
  SELECT
    ufl.user_id,
    ufl.first_month,
    ufl.last_month,
    ufl.num_active_months,
    ufl.span_months
  FROM user_first_last ufl
  WHERE ufl.last_month < DATE_TRUNC(DATE('2024-09-10'), MONTH)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM user_activity_months uam
      WHERE uam.user_id = ufl.user_id
        AND uam.activity_month > ufl.last_month
    )
),

-- Step 4: Users with at least one gap within their activity span
users_with_gaps AS (
  SELECT
    uia.user_id,
    uia.first_month,
    uia.last_month
  FROM users_inactive_after uia
  WHERE uia.num_active_months < uia.span_months
),

-- Step 5: Compute month number (counting from first activity month = 1)
users_final AS (
  SELECT
    uwg.user_id,
    DATE_DIFF(uwg.last_month, uwg.first_month, MONTH) + 1 AS month_number
  FROM users_with_gaps uwg
)

-- Step 6: Get the user with the highest month number
SELECT
  user_id,
  month_number
FROM users_final
ORDER BY month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 129. bq403 (DB: `irs_990`)
**Question**: Which three years in 2012-2017 have the smallest absolute difference between median revenue and median functional expenses for organizations filing IRS 990 forms? Please output three years and respective differences.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   filing_year |   median_difference |
|--------------:|--------------------:|
|          2012 |             20639   |
|          2013 |             20988   |
|          2017 |             26391.5 |

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   year |   absolute_difference |
|-------:|----------------------:|
|   2017 |                  4244 |
|   2014 |                  6852 |
|   2012 |                  9487 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH revenue_data AS (
  -- Extract revenue data from irs_990_ein for 2012-2017
  SELECT 
    ein,
    CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_period AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
    revenue_amt
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_ein`
  WHERE tax_period IS NOT NULL
    AND revenue_amt IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_period AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) BETWEEN 2012 AND 2017
),

expense_data AS (
  -- Combine functional expense data from all yearly tables (2012-2017)
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2012`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2012
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2013`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2013
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2014`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2014
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2015`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2015
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2016`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2016
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT ein, CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2017`
  WHERE totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL AND tax_pd IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(tax_pd AS STRING), 1, 4) AS INT64) = 2017
),

matched_data AS (
  -- Join revenue and expense data by EIN and year
  SELECT 
    r.year,
    r.revenue_amt,
    e.totfuncexpns
  FROM revenue_data r
  INNER JOIN expense_data e
    ON r.ein = e.ein AND r.year = e.year
  WHERE r.revenue_amt IS NOT NULL 
    AND e.totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
),

yearly_medians AS (
  -- Calculate median revenue and median expenses per year
  SELECT 
    year,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(revenue_amt, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_revenue,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totfuncexpns, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_expenses
  FROM matched_data
  GROUP BY year
)

-- Final selection: top 3 years with smallest absolute difference
SELECT 
  year,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_expenses) AS absolute_difference
FROM yearly_medians
ORDER BY absolute_difference ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH yearly_data AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_*`
  WHERE REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}$')
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2017'
    AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
    AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
),
medians AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(totrevenue, 0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY year) AS median_revenue,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(totfuncexpns, 0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY year) AS median_func_expenses
  FROM yearly_data
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  year,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_func_expenses) AS abs_diff
FROM medians
ORDER BY abs_diff
LIMIT 3;
```

### 130. bq402 (DB: `ecommerce`)
**Question**: Calculate the conversion rate from unique visitors to purchasers by using data exclusively from the `web_analytics` table in the `data-to-insights.ecommerce` dataset. A visitor is defined as a unique `fullVisitorId` present in the table, while a purchaser is a visitor who has at least one transaction recorded (`totals.transactions` is not null). The conversion rate is computed by dividing the number of unique purchasers by the total number of unique visitors. Additionally, calculate the average number of transactions per purchaser, considering only those visitors who have made at least one transaction.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|         0.0269845 |                          1.24412 |

**OR**

|   TOTAL_UNIQUE_VISITORS |   UNIQUE_PURCHASERS |   TOTAL_TRANSACTIONS |   CONVERSION_RATE_PERCENTAGE |   AVG_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PURCHASER |
|------------------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|                  741721 |               20015 |                24901 |                          2.7 |                             1.24 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   total_visitors |   total_purchasers |   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|-----------------:|-------------------:|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|           741721 |              20015 |             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH visitor_stats AS (
  -- Aggregate transaction data per visitor
  SELECT 
    fullVisitorId,
    -- Check if visitor had any transaction (purchaser flag)
    MAX(CASE WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_purchaser,
    -- Sum all transactions for this visitor
    SUM(IFNULL(totals.transactions, 0)) AS total_transactions
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  GROUP BY fullVisitorId
)
SELECT 
  COUNT(*) AS total_visitors,
  SUM(is_purchaser) AS total_purchasers,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(is_purchaser), COUNT(*)), 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(CASE WHEN is_purchaser = 1 THEN total_transactions ELSE 0 END),
      SUM(is_purchaser)
    ), 
    4
  ) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM visitor_stats;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Total unique visitors across all sessions
  visitor_stats AS (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  ),

  -- Purchasers: visitors with at least one transaction,
  -- along with their total transaction count across all sessions
  purchaser_stats AS (
    SELECT
      fullVisitorId,
      SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions_per_visitor
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
    WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY fullVisitorId
  ),

  -- Aggregate purchaser-level data
  aggregated AS (
    SELECT
      (SELECT total_visitors FROM visitor_stats) AS unique_visitors,
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId)                AS unique_purchasers,
      AVG(total_transactions_per_visitor)          AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
    FROM purchaser_stats
  )

-- Final output: conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
SELECT
  unique_visitors,
  unique_purchasers,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(unique_purchasers, unique_visitors), 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(avg_transactions_per_purchaser, 4)                  AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM aggregated;
```
</details>

### 131. sf_bq072 (DB: `DEATH`)
**Question**: Please provide, for each age from 12 through 18 (inclusive), the total number of deaths and the number of deaths among individuals identified as Black (based on race descriptions containing the word ‘black’), specifically for deaths associated with ICD-10 codes whose descriptions include the word ‘vehicle’ and for deaths associated with ICD-10 codes whose descriptions include the word ‘firearm.’ Use the EntityAxisConditions table to determine which ICD-10 codes were involved in each death, rather than joining ICD-10 code information directly on the death records.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

*... and 9 more rows.*

**OR**

|------:|-----------------------:|-----------------------:|-----------------------:|-----------------------:|

|    13 |                     71 |                     12 |                     71 |                     15 |
|    14 |                     93 |                     20 |                    105 |                     27 |
|    15 |                    133 |                     23 |                    164 |                     58 |
|    16 |                    262 |                     42 |                    246 |                    109 |

*... and 2 more rows.*

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   Age |   Vehicle_TotalDeaths |   Vehicle_BlackDeaths |   Firearm_TotalDeaths |   Firearm_BlackDeaths |
|------:|----------------------:|----------------------:|----------------------:|----------------------:|
|    12 |                    60 |                    16 |                    39 |                     7 |
|    13 |                    71 |                    12 |                    71 |                    15 |
|    14 |                    93 |                    20 |                   105 |                    27 |
|    15 |                   133 |                    23 |                   164 |                    58 |
|    16 |                   262 |                    42 |                   246 |                   109 |

*... and 2 more rows.*

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get ICD-10 codes for vehicle and firearm related deaths
vehicle_codes AS (
    SELECT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),
firearm_codes AS (
    SELECT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),
-- Step 2: Get death records with vehicle-related ICD-10 codes from EntityAxisConditions
vehicle_deaths AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
    WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM vehicle_codes)
),
-- Step 3: Get death records with firearm-related ICD-10 codes from EntityAxisConditions
firearm_deaths AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
    WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM firearm_codes)
),
-- Step 4: Get death records for ages 12-18 (in years) with race information
death_data AS (
    SELECT 
        d."Id" AS "DeathRecordId",
        d."Age",
        d."Race",
        -- Determine if race description contains 'black' (case-insensitive)
        CASE 
            WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN 1 
            ELSE 0 
        END AS "IsBlack"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" d
    LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE" r ON d."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE d."AgeType" = 1  -- Assuming 1 = years (based on AGETYPE table)
      AND d."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
),
-- Step 5: Generate all ages from 12 to 18 inclusive
ages AS (
    SELECT 12 AS "Age" UNION ALL
    SELECT 13 UNION ALL
    SELECT 14 UNION ALL
    SELECT 15 UNION ALL
    SELECT 16 UNION ALL
    SELECT 17 UNION ALL
    SELECT 18
),
-- Step 6: Aggregate vehicle-related deaths by age
vehicle_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        dd."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dd."DeathRecordId") AS "TotalDeaths",
        SUM(dd."IsBlack") AS "BlackDeaths"
    FROM death_data dd
    INNER JOIN vehicle_deaths vd ON dd."DeathRecordId" = vd."DeathRecordId"
    GROUP BY dd."Age"
),
-- Step 7: Aggregate firearm-related deaths by age
firearm_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        dd."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dd."DeathRecordId") AS "TotalDeaths",
        SUM(dd."IsBlack") AS "BlackDeaths"
    FROM death_data dd
    INNER JOIN firearm_deaths fd ON dd."DeathRecordId" = fd."DeathRecordId"
    GROUP BY dd."Age"
)
-- Step 8: Combine results for all ages 12-18, showing both vehicle and firearm counts
SELECT 
    a."Age",
    COALESCE(vc."TotalDeaths", 0) AS "Vehicle_TotalDeaths",
    COALESCE(vc."BlackDeaths", 0) AS "Vehicle_BlackDeaths",
    COALESCE(fc."TotalDeaths", 0) AS "Firearm_TotalDeaths",
    COALESCE(fc."BlackDeaths", 0) AS "Firearm_BlackDeaths"
FROM ages a
LEFT JOIN vehicle_counts vc ON a."Age" = vc."Age"
LEFT JOIN firearm_counts fc ON a."Age" = fc."Age"
ORDER BY a."Age";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define ICD-10 codes whose descriptions contain 'vehicle' or 'firearm'
WITH vehicle_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),
firearm_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),

-- Step 2: Identify death records (through EntityAxisConditions) that have at least one such code
vehicle_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS eac
    INNER JOIN vehicle_icd_codes vic ON eac."Icd10Code" = vic."Code"
),
firearm_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS eac
    INNER JOIN firearm_icd_codes fic ON eac."Icd10Code" = fic."Code"
),

-- Step 3: For each cause, compute total deaths and Black deaths per age (12-18, age in years)
vehicle_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.DEATHRECORDS dr
    INNER JOIN vehicle_death_ids vdi ON dr."Id" = vdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN DEATH.DEATH.RACE r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1          -- age in years
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
),
firearm_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.DEATHRECORDS dr
    INNER JOIN firearm_death_ids fdi ON dr."Id" = fdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN DEATH.DEATH.RACE r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
)

-- Step 4: Combine and output results with cause label
SELECT
    "Age",
    'vehicle' AS cause,
    "total_deaths",
    "black_deaths"
FROM vehicle_stats
UNION ALL
SELECT
    "Age",
    'firearm' AS cause,
    "total_deaths",
    "black_deaths"
FROM firearm_stats
ORDER BY "Age", cause;
```
</details>

### 132. ga021 (DB: `firebase`)
**Question**: What is the retention rate for users two weeks after their initial quickplay event, calculated separately for each quickplay event type, within the period from July 2, 2018, to July 16, 2018? Please focus on users who started a session (session_start) during this period.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| quickplay_event_type     |   cohort_users |   retained_users |   retention_rate |

| level_fail_quickplay     |             28 |                9 |         0.321429 |

| level_complete_quickplay |            30 |               14 |           46.67 |
| level_retry_quickplay    |             7 |                3 |           42.86 |
