| month_highest_count   |   highest_count | month_lowest_count   |   lowest_count |   avg_balance_highest_month |   avg_balance_lowest_month |   difference_in_averages |
|:----------------------|----------------:|:---------------------|---------------:|----------------------------:|---------------------------:|-------------------------:|
| 2020-01               |             424 | 2020-05              |              0 |                     557.704 |                          0 |                  557.704 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE months AS (
    -- Generate all months of 2020 as 'YYYY-MM' strings
    SELECT '2020-01' AS "month"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        CASE 
            WHEN "month" = '2020-12' THEN NULL
            ELSE 
                printf('%04d-%02d', 
                    CAST(substr("month", 1, 4) AS INTEGER),
                    CAST(substr("month", 6, 2) AS INTEGER) + 1
                )
        END
    FROM months
    WHERE "month" IS NOT NULL AND "month" < '2020-12'
),
all_customers AS (
    -- Get distinct customers from transactions in 2020
    SELECT DISTINCT "customer_id"
    FROM "customer_transactions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "txn_date") = '2020'
),
customer_month_combinations AS (
    -- Create all combinations of customers and months
    SELECT 
        c."customer_id",
        m."month"
    FROM all_customers c
    CROSS JOIN months m
),
monthly_balances AS (
    -- Calculate net balance for each customer per month (only months with transactions)
    SELECT 
        "customer_id",
        strftime('%Y-%m', "txn_date") AS "month",
        SUM(
            CASE 
                WHEN LOWER("txn_type") = 'deposit' THEN "txn_amount"
                WHEN LOWER("txn_type") = 'withdrawal' THEN -"txn_amount"
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS "balance"
    FROM "customer_transactions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "txn_date") = '2020'
        AND LOWER("txn_type") IN ('deposit', 'withdrawal')
    GROUP BY "customer_id", strftime('%Y-%m', "txn_date")
),
complete_balances AS (
    -- Combine to get balance for every customer-month (0 if no transactions)
    SELECT 
        cm."customer_id",
        cm."month",
        COALESCE(mb."balance", 0) AS "month_end_balance"
    FROM customer_month_combinations cm
    LEFT JOIN monthly_balances mb 
        ON cm."customer_id" = mb."customer_id" 
        AND cm."month" = mb."month"
),
positive_counts AS (
    -- Count customers with positive month-end balance per month
    SELECT 
        "month",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "month_end_balance" > 0 THEN 1 END) AS "positive_customer_count"
    FROM complete_balances
    GROUP BY "month"
),
ranked_months AS (
    -- Rank months by positive count (highest and lowest)
    SELECT 
        "month",
        "positive_customer_count",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "positive_customer_count" DESC) AS "rank_desc",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "positive_customer_count" ASC) AS "rank_asc"
    FROM positive_counts
),
max_month AS (
    -- Month with highest positive count (pick first in case of ties)
    SELECT "month", "positive_customer_count"
    FROM ranked_months
    WHERE "rank_desc" = 1
    ORDER BY "month" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
min_month AS (
    -- Month with lowest positive count (pick first in case of ties)
    SELECT "month", "positive_customer_count"
    FROM ranked_months
    WHERE "rank_asc" = 1
    ORDER BY "month" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
avg_balances AS (
    -- Average month-end balance for the two selected months
    SELECT 
        cb."month",
        ROUND(AVG(cb."month_end_balance"), 4) AS "avg_month_end_balance"
    FROM complete_balances cb
    WHERE cb."month" IN (SELECT "month" FROM max_month UNION SELECT "month" FROM min_month)
    GROUP BY cb."month"
)
-- Final result
SELECT 
    mm."month" AS "month_highest_count",
    mm."positive_customer_count" AS "highest_count",
    mn."month" AS "month_lowest_count",
    mn."positive_customer_count" AS "lowest_count",
    MAX(CASE WHEN ab."month" = mm."month" THEN ab."avg_month_end_balance" END) AS "avg_balance_highest_month",
    MAX(CASE WHEN ab."month" = mn."month" THEN ab."avg_month_end_balance" END) AS "avg_balance_lowest_month",
    ROUND(
        MAX(CASE WHEN ab."month" = mm."month" THEN ab."avg_month_end_balance" END) -
        MAX(CASE WHEN ab."month" = mn."month" THEN ab."avg_month_end_balance" END),
        4
    ) AS "difference_in_averages"
FROM max_month mm
CROSS JOIN min_month mn
LEFT JOIN avg_balances ab ON ab."month" IN (mm."month", mn."month");
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Generate all months of 2020 (1 to 12)
WITH RECURSIVE months(month) AS (
    SELECT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT month + 1 FROM months WHERE month < 12
),

-- Step 2: Get all customers from customer_nodes
all_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "customer_id" FROM "customer_nodes"
),

-- Step 3: Create grid of all customer-month pairs for 2020
customer_month_grid AS (
    SELECT c."customer_id", m.month
    FROM all_customers c
    CROSS JOIN months m
),

-- Step 4: Aggregate transactions per customer per month in 2020
txn_summary AS (
    SELECT
        "customer_id",
        CAST(strftime('%m', "txn_date") AS INTEGER) AS month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "txn_type" = 'deposit' THEN "txn_amount" ELSE 0 END) AS deposit_sum,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "txn_type" = 'withdrawal' THEN "txn_amount" ELSE 0 END) AS withdrawal_sum
    FROM "customer_transactions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "txn_date") = '2020'
    GROUP BY "customer_id", month
),

-- Step 5: Compute month-end balance for each customer-month
customer_month_balances AS (
    SELECT
        g."customer_id",
        g.month,
        COALESCE(t.deposit_sum, 0) - COALESCE(t.withdrawal_sum, 0) AS balance
    FROM customer_month_grid g
    LEFT JOIN txn_summary t
        ON g."customer_id" = t."customer_id" AND g.month = t.month
),

-- Step 6: Calculate per month – count of positive balances and average balance
month_stats AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_count,
        ROUND(AVG(balance), 4) AS avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    GROUP BY month
),

-- Step 7: Identify the months with highest and lowest positive counts
highest_month AS (
    SELECT month, avg_balance
    FROM month_stats
    ORDER BY positive_count DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
lowest_month AS (
    SELECT month, avg_balance
    FROM month_stats
    ORDER BY positive_count ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 8: Compute the difference between the two averages
SELECT
    ROUND(h.avg_balance - l.avg_balance, 4) AS avg_balance_difference
FROM highest_month h, lowest_month l;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Generate monthly closing balances with changes and cumulative totals
WITH RECURSIVE 
-- Get the date range from transactions
date_range AS (
    SELECT 
        MIN(DATE("txn_date", 'start of month')) AS start_month,
        MAX(DATE("txn_date", 'start of month')) AS end_month
    FROM "customer_transactions"
),
-- Generate all months in the range
all_months AS (
    SELECT start_month AS month_start
    FROM date_range
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE(month_start, '+1 month')
    FROM all_months
    WHERE month_start < (SELECT end_month FROM date_range)
),
-- Get all distinct customers
distinct_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "customer_id"
    FROM "customer_transactions"
),
-- Create all possible customer-month combinations
customer_month_combos AS (
    SELECT 
        c."customer_id",
        m.month_start
    FROM distinct_customers c
    CROSS JOIN all_months m
),
-- Calculate net monthly transactions per customer
monthly_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_id",
        DATE("txn_date", 'start of month') AS month_start,
        SUM(
            CASE 
                WHEN "txn_type" = 'deposit' THEN "txn_amount"
                ELSE -"txn_amount"  -- purchases and withdrawals reduce balance
            END
        ) AS monthly_change
    FROM "customer_transactions"
    GROUP BY "customer_id", month_start
),
-- Combine with all months and calculate cumulative balances
monthly_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        cmc."customer_id",
        strftime('%Y-%m', cmc.month_start) AS month,
        cmc.month_start,
        COALESCE(mt.monthly_change, 0) AS monthly_change,
        SUM(COALESCE(mt.monthly_change, 0)) OVER (
            PARTITION BY cmc."customer_id" 
            ORDER BY cmc.month_start
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS cumulative_balance
    FROM customer_month_combos cmc
    LEFT JOIN monthly_transactions mt 
        ON cmc."customer_id" = mt."customer_id" 
        AND cmc.month_start = mt.month_start
)
-- Final output with formatted results
SELECT 
    "customer_id",
    month AS "month_year",
    monthly_change,
    cumulative_balance AS "closing_balance"
FROM monthly_balances
ORDER BY "customer_id", month_start;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: All distinct year-month periods present in the transaction data
all_months AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month
    FROM customer_transactions
),

-- Step 2: Convert each transaction to a signed amount
-- deposit: +txn_amount ; purchase/withdrawal: -txn_amount
signed_txns AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        txn_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
            ELSE -txn_amount
        END AS signed_amount
    FROM customer_transactions
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate net change per customer per month
monthly_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
        SUM(signed_amount) AS net_change
    FROM signed_txns
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
),

-- Step 4: Build a complete grid of all customers × all months
-- This ensures months with no customer activity are still included
customer_month_grid AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        m.month
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
    CROSS JOIN all_months m
),

-- Step 5: Left join the actual changes onto the grid, filling NULLs with 0
filled_data AS (
    SELECT 
        cmg.customer_id,
        cmg.month,
        COALESCE(mc.net_change, 0) AS net_change
    FROM customer_month_grid cmg
    LEFT JOIN monthly_changes mc 
        ON cmg.customer_id = mc.customer_id AND cmg.month = mc.month
)

-- Step 6: Compute cumulative running balance using a window function
-- The cumulative balance represents the closing balance at month-end
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    month,
    net_change AS monthly_change,
    SUM(net_change) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id 
        ORDER BY month
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM filled_data
ORDER BY customer_id, month;
```
</details>

        AND m.year GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
),
actor_gaps AS (
    SELECT 
        PID,
        year,
        LEAD(year) OVER (PARTITION BY PID ORDER BY year) AS next_year
    FROM actor_years
),
actors_with_bad_gap AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT PID
    FROM actor_gaps
    WHERE next_year - year > 4
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PID) AS actor_count
FROM actor_years
WHERE PID NOT IN (SELECT PID FROM actors_with_bad_gap);
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH actor_movie_years AS (
    -- Step 1: Get all distinct actor-movie-year combinations
    SELECT DISTINCT 
        p.PID, 
        p.Name, 
        CAST(m.year AS INTEGER) AS movie_year
    FROM Person p
    JOIN M_Cast mc ON p.PID = mc.PID
    JOIN Movie m ON mc.MID = m.MID
    WHERE m.year IS NOT NULL AND m.year != ''
),
actor_years_with_prev AS (
    -- Step 2: For each actor, sort by year and get the previous movie year
    SELECT 
        PID,
        Name,
        movie_year,
        LAG(movie_year) OVER (PARTITION BY PID ORDER BY movie_year) AS prev_year
    FROM actor_movie_years
),
actor_max_gap AS (
    -- Step 3: Compute the maximum gap between consecutive movie years for each actor
    SELECT 
        PID,
        Name,
        MAX(movie_year - prev_year) AS max_gap
    FROM actor_years_with_prev
    WHERE prev_year IS NOT NULL  -- exclude first movie for each actor (no previous year)
    GROUP BY PID, Name
)
-- Step 4: Count actors who never had a gap > 3 consecutive years without a movie
-- Condition: max_gap <= 4 (since diff=4 means exactly 3 years between movies, which is allowed)
-- Also include actors with only a single movie (they have no gaps at all)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS actor_count
FROM (
    SELECT PID FROM actor_max_gap WHERE max_gap <= 4
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT PID FROM actor_movie_years amy
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM actor_max_gap WHERE PID = amy.PID)
) qualified_actors;
```
</details>

### 155. local130 (DB: `school_scheduling`)
**Question**: Could you provide a list of last names for all students who have completed English courses (where completion is defined as having a ClassStatus of 2), along with their quintile ranks based on their individual grades in those courses? The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH english_completions AS (
    -- Get all students who completed English courses with their grades
    SELECT 
        s."StudLastName",
        ss."Grade",
        ss."StudentID"
    FROM "Student_Schedules" ss
    INNER JOIN "Classes" c ON ss."ClassID" = c."ClassID"
    INNER JOIN "Subjects" sub ON c."SubjectID" = sub."SubjectID"
    INNER JOIN "Students" s ON ss."StudentID" = s."StudentID"
    INNER JOIN "Categories" cat ON sub."CategoryID" = cat."CategoryID"
    WHERE ss."ClassStatus" = 2  -- Completed courses only
        AND LOWER(cat."CategoryDescription") LIKE '%english%'  -- English departments/categories
        AND ss."Grade" IS NOT NULL  -- Ensure grade exists
),
ranked_students AS (
    -- Calculate rank_count (number of students with grade >= current student's grade)
    SELECT 
        "StudLastName",
        "Grade",
        "StudentID",
        (
            SELECT COUNT(*) 
            FROM english_completions ec2 
            WHERE ec2."Grade" >= ec1."Grade"
        ) AS rank_count,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM english_completions) AS total_count
    FROM english_completions ec1
),
quintile_calc AS (
    -- Calculate quintile ratio and assign labels
    SELECT 
        "StudLastName",
        "Grade",
        "StudentID",
        ROUND(CAST("rank_count" AS REAL) / CAST("total_count" AS REAL), 4) AS quintile_ratio,
        CASE 
            WHEN CAST("rank_count" AS REAL) / CAST("total_count" AS REAL) <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
            WHEN CAST("rank_count" AS REAL) / CAST("total_count" AS REAL) <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
            WHEN CAST("rank_count" AS REAL) / CAST("total_count" AS REAL) <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
            WHEN CAST("rank_count" AS REAL) / CAST("total_count" AS REAL) <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
            ELSE 'Fifth'
        END AS quintile_label
    FROM ranked_students
)
-- Final selection with proper ordering
SELECT 
    "StudLastName" AS last_name,
    quintile_label
FROM quintile_calc
ORDER BY 
    CASE quintile_label
        WHEN 'First' THEN 1
        WHEN 'Second' THEN 2
        WHEN 'Third' THEN 3
        WHEN 'Fourth' THEN 4
        WHEN 'Fifth' THEN 5
    END,
    "StudLastName";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE to extract completed English course enrollments with student last names and grades
WITH "english_completions" AS (
    SELECT
        s."StudentID",
        s."StudLastName",
        ss."Grade"
    FROM "Student_Schedules" ss
    INNER JOIN "Classes" c ON ss."ClassID" = c."ClassID"
    INNER JOIN "Subjects" sub ON c."SubjectID" = sub."SubjectID"
    INNER JOIN "Students" s ON ss."StudentID" = s."StudentID"
    WHERE ss."ClassStatus" = 2                                      -- completed
      AND (LOWER(sub."SubjectName") LIKE '%english%'                -- contains 'English'
           OR LOWER(sub."SubjectCode") LIKE 'eng%')                 -- or code starts with 'ENG'
),
-- total number of completed English course rows (denominator)
"total" AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS "cnt" FROM "english_completions"
)
SELECT
    ec."StudLastName",
    CASE
        WHEN (ec."rank_ge" * 1.0 / t."cnt") <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
        WHEN (ec."rank_ge" * 1.0 / t."cnt") <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
        WHEN (ec."rank_ge" * 1.0 / t."cnt") <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
        WHEN (ec."rank_ge" * 1.0 / t."cnt") <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
        ELSE 'Fifth'
    END AS "Quintile"
FROM (
    SELECT
        "StudentID",
        "StudLastName",
        "Grade",
        -- number of rows with grade >= current grade (includes ties)
        COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY "Grade" DESC) AS "rank_ge"
    FROM "english_completions"
) ec
CROSS JOIN "total" t
ORDER BY
    (ec."rank_ge" * 1.0 / t."cnt") ASC;   -- ascending proportion: First first, Fifth last
```
</details>

```sql
Let me now design the SQL query based on the schema information provided.

**Step-by-step Reasoning:**

1. **Tables needed:** `Musical_Styles` (for StyleName) and `Musical_Preferences` (for PreferenceSeq counts)
2. **Join condition:** Both tables share `StyleID` - so `Musical_Styles.StyleID = Musical_Preferences.StyleID`
3. **Aggregation:** For each style, count occurrences where `PreferenceSeq = 1`, `PreferenceSeq = 2`, and `PreferenceSeq = 3` — using conditional `SUM(CASE ...)` to pivot into separate columns
4. **Grouping:** By `StyleName` (and `StyleID` to avoid ambiguity), one row per style
5. **Output:** Three count columns representing 1st, 2nd, and 3rd preference counts

Here is the final SQL:

```sql
SELECT
    ms."StyleName",
    SUM(CASE WHEN mp."PreferenceSeq" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "1st_Preference_Count",
    SUM(CASE WHEN mp."PreferenceSeq" = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "2nd_Preference_Count",
    SUM(CASE WHEN mp."PreferenceSeq" = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "3rd_Preference_Count"
FROM "Musical_Styles" AS ms
INNER JOIN "Musical_Preferences" AS mp
    ON ms."StyleID" = mp."StyleID"
GROUP BY ms."StyleID", ms."StyleName"
ORDER BY ms."StyleName";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>

```sql
-- Calculate annual sales per salesperson
WITH annual_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        soh.salespersonid,
        CAST(SUBSTR(soh.orderdate, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
        ROUND(SUM(sod.unitprice * sod.orderqty * (1 - sod.unitpricediscount)), 4) AS total_sales
    FROM 
        "salesorderheader" soh
    INNER JOIN 
        "salesorderdetail" sod ON soh.salesorderid = sod.salesorderid
    WHERE 
        soh.salespersonid IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        soh.salespersonid, year
),

-- Calculate annual quota per salesperson
annual_quota AS (
    SELECT 
        spqh."BusinessEntityID",
        CAST(SUBSTR(spqh."QuotaDate", 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
        ROUND(SUM(spqh."SalesQuota"), 4) AS total_quota
    FROM 
        "SalesPersonQuotaHistory" spqh
    GROUP BY 
        spqh."BusinessEntityID", year
),

-- Get all unique salesperson-year combinations from both sources
all_years AS (
    SELECT salespersonid AS businessentityid, year FROM annual_sales
    UNION
    SELECT "BusinessEntityID", year FROM annual_quota
)

-- Final comparison with difference calculation
SELECT 
    ay.businessentityid AS salesperson_id,
    ay.year,
    COALESCE(asales.total_sales, 0) AS annual_total_sales,
    COALESCE(aquota.total_quota, 0) AS annual_sales_quota,
    ROUND(COALESCE(asales.total_sales, 0) - COALESCE(aquota.total_quota, 0), 4) AS sales_vs_quota_difference
FROM 
    all_years ay
LEFT JOIN 
    annual_sales asales ON ay.businessentityid = asales.salespersonid AND ay.year = asales.year
LEFT JOIN 
    annual_quota aquota ON ay.businessentityid = aquota."BusinessEntityID" AND ay.year = aquota.year
ORDER BY 
    ay.businessentityid, ay.year;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Calculate annual total sales per salesperson from order headers
annual_sales AS (
    SELECT
        CAST("salespersonid" AS INTEGER) AS "businessentityid",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "orderdate") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        ROUND(SUM("subtotal"), 4) AS "total_sales"
    FROM "salesorderheader"
    WHERE "salespersonid" IS NOT NULL AND "salespersonid" != ''
    GROUP BY CAST("salespersonid" AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%Y', "orderdate") AS INTEGER)
),

-- Step 2: Calculate annual total sales quota per salesperson from quota history
annual_quota AS (
    SELECT
        "BusinessEntityID" AS "businessentityid",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "QuotaDate") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        ROUND(SUM("SalesQuota"), 4) AS "total_quota"
    FROM "SalesPersonQuotaHistory"
    GROUP BY "BusinessEntityID", CAST(strftime('%Y', "QuotaDate") AS INTEGER)
),

-- Step 3: Build all distinct (salesperson, year) pairs to simulate FULL OUTER JOIN
all_pairs AS (
    SELECT "businessentityid", "year" FROM annual_sales
    UNION
    SELECT "businessentityid", "year" FROM annual_quota
)

-- Step 4: Join everything together and compute the difference
SELECT
    ap."businessentityid" AS "salesperson_id",
    ap."year",
    ROUND(COALESCE(s."total_sales", 0), 4) AS "total_sales",
    ROUND(COALESCE(q."total_quota", 0), 4) AS "total_quota",
    ROUND(COALESCE(s."total_sales", 0) - COALESCE(q."total_quota", 0), 4) AS "sales_vs_quota_difference"
FROM "all_pairs" ap
LEFT JOIN "annual_sales" s ON ap."businessentityid" = s."businessentityid" AND ap."year" = s."year"
LEFT JOIN "annual_quota" q ON ap."businessentityid" = q."businessentityid" AND ap."year" = q."year"
ORDER BY ap."businessentityid", ap."year";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH director_movie_details AS (
    -- Get all movies with director info, dates, and ratings
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id AS director_id,
        m.id AS movie_id,
        m.date_published,
        m.duration,
        r.avg_rating,
        r.total_votes
    FROM director_mapping dm
    INNER JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    INNER JOIN ratings r ON dm.movie_id = r.movie_id
    WHERE m.date_published IS NOT NULL
),
director_movie_sequence AS (
    -- Calculate inter-movie gaps using window functions
    SELECT 
        director_id,
        movie_id,
        date_published,
        duration,
        avg_rating,
        total_votes,
        -- Calculate days since previous movie by same director
        CASE 
            WHEN LAG(date_published) OVER (
                PARTITION BY director_id 
                ORDER BY date_published
            ) IS NOT NULL 
            THEN JULIANDAY(date_published) - JULIANDAY(
                LAG(date_published) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY director_id 
                    ORDER BY date_published
                )
            )
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS days_since_previous_movie
    FROM director_movie_details
),
director_stats AS (
    -- Aggregate statistics per director
    SELECT 
        director_id,
        COUNT(movie_id) AS movie_count,
        ROUND(AVG(days_since_previous_movie)) AS avg_inter_movie_days,
        AVG(avg_rating) AS raw_avg_rating,
        SUM(total_votes) AS total_votes,
        MIN(avg_rating) AS min_rating,
        MAX(avg_rating) AS max_rating,
        SUM(duration) AS total_duration
    FROM director_movie_sequence
    GROUP BY director_id
    HAVING COUNT(movie_id) > 0  -- Ensure at least one movie
)
-- Final query with names and proper formatting
SELECT 
    ds.director_id,
    n.name AS director_name,
    ds.movie_count,
    ds.avg_inter_movie_days,
    ROUND(ds.raw_avg_rating, 2) AS avg_rating,
    ds.total_votes,
    ds.min_rating,
    ds.max_rating,
    ds.total_duration
FROM director_stats ds
INNER JOIN names n ON ds.director_id = n.id
ORDER BY ds.movie_count DESC NULLS LAST, ds.total_duration DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 9;
```

```sql
WITH director_movies AS (
    SELECT 
        d.name_id AS director_id,
        n.name AS director_name,
        d.movie_id,
        m.date_published,
        m.duration,
        r.avg_rating,
        r.total_votes
    FROM director_mapping d
    JOIN movies m ON d.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN names n ON d.name_id = n.id
    LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),

-- For each director, order their movies chronologically and find the previous movie's date
movie_gaps AS (
    SELECT 
        director_id,
        director_name,
        movie_id,
        date_published,
        duration,
        avg_rating,
        total_votes,
        LAG(date_published) OVER (
            PARTITION BY director_id 
            ORDER BY date_published
        ) AS prev_date
    FROM director_movies
),

-- Calculate the inter-movie gap in days (difference between consecutive movies)
gaps_calculated AS (
    SELECT 
        director_id,
        director_name,
        movie_id,
        duration,
        avg_rating,
        total_votes,
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_date IS NOT NULL 
            THEN JULIANDAY(date_published) - JULIANDAY(prev_date)
        END AS days_gap
    FROM movie_gaps
),

-- Aggregate all stats per director
director_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        director_id,
        director_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT movie_id) AS movie_count,
        ROUND(AVG(days_gap)) AS avg_inter_movie_duration,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
        COALESCE(SUM(total_votes), 0) AS total_votes,
        MIN(avg_rating) AS min_rating,
        MAX(avg_rating) AS max_rating,
        SUM(duration) AS total_duration
    FROM gaps_calculated
    GROUP BY director_id, director_name
)

-- Final output: top 9 directors
SELECT 
    director_id,
    director_name,
    movie_count,
    avg_inter_movie_duration,
    avg_rating,
    total_votes,
    min_rating,
    max_rating,
    total_duration
FROM director_stats
ORDER BY movie_count DESC NULLS LAST, total_duration DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 9;
```

WITH delivery_dates AS (
    -- Join deliveries with orders to get creation dates

    FROM delivery_dates

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH track_durations AS (
    -- Calculate duration in minutes for each track
    SELECT 
        "TrackId",
        "Milliseconds" / (1000.0 * 60.0) AS duration_minutes
    FROM "Track"
),
global_stats AS (
    -- Compute global min, avg, max durations
    SELECT 
        MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_duration,
        AVG(duration_minutes) AS avg_duration,
        MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_duration
    FROM track_durations
),
classification_bounds AS (
    -- Calculate classification boundaries
    SELECT 
        min_duration,
        avg_duration,
        max_duration,
        (min_duration + avg_duration) / 2.0 AS short_medium_boundary,
        (avg_duration + max_duration) / 2.0 AS medium_long_boundary
    FROM global_stats
),
classified_tracks AS (
    -- Classify tracks and calculate revenue
    SELECT 
        t."TrackId",
        td.duration_minutes,
        CASE 
            WHEN td.duration_minutes < cb.short_medium_boundary THEN 'short'
            WHEN td.duration_minutes >= cb.short_medium_boundary 
                 AND td.duration_minutes < cb.medium_long_boundary THEN 'medium'
            ELSE 'long'
        END AS category,
        COALESCE(SUM(il."Quantity" * il."UnitPrice"), 0) AS track_revenue
    FROM track_durations td
    INNER JOIN "Track" t ON td."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    CROSS JOIN classification_bounds cb
    LEFT JOIN "InvoiceLine" il ON t."TrackId" = il."TrackId"
    GROUP BY t."TrackId", td.duration_minutes, cb.short_medium_boundary, cb.medium_long_boundary
)
-- Final aggregation by category
SELECT 
    category,
    ROUND(MIN(duration_minutes), 4) AS min_duration_minutes,
    ROUND(MAX(duration_minutes), 4) AS max_duration_minutes,
    ROUND(SUM(track_revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM classified_tracks
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY 
    CASE category
        WHEN 'short' THEN 1
        WHEN 'medium' THEN 2
        WHEN 'long' THEN 3
    END;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE 1: Calculate duration in minutes for every track
WITH track_durations AS (
    SELECT 
        "TrackId",
        "Milliseconds" / 60000.0 AS duration_minutes
    FROM "Track"
),

-- CTE 2: Compute global min, avg, max durations
stats AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_dur,
        AVG(duration_minutes) AS avg_dur,
        MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_dur
    FROM track_durations
),

-- CTE 3: Classify each track into Short / Medium / Long
classified_tracks AS (
    SELECT
        t."TrackId",
        t.duration_minutes,
        CASE
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= s.min_dur 
                 AND t.duration_minutes < (s.min_dur + s.avg_dur) / 2.0 
            THEN 'Short'
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= (s.min_dur + s.avg_dur) / 2.0 
                 AND t.duration_minutes < (s.avg_dur + s.max_dur) / 2.0 
            THEN 'Medium'
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= (s.avg_dur + s.max_dur) / 2.0 
                 AND t.duration_minutes <= s.max_dur 
            THEN 'Long'
        END AS category
    FROM track_durations t
    CROSS JOIN stats s
)

-- Final: Aggregate by category
SELECT
    ct.category,
    ROUND(MIN(ct.duration_minutes), 4) AS min_time_minutes,
    ROUND(MAX(ct.duration_minutes), 4) AS max_time_minutes,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(il."UnitPrice", 0) * COALESCE(il."Quantity", 0)), 4) AS total_revenue
FROM classified_tracks ct
LEFT JOIN "InvoiceLine" il ON ct."TrackId" = il."TrackId"
WHERE ct.category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ct.category
ORDER BY ct.category;
```
</details>

### 163. local272 (DB: `oracle_sql`)
**Question**: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   product_id | aisle   |   position |   QUANTITY_TO_PICK |
|-------------:|:--------|-----------:|-------------------:|
|         6520 | A       |         16 |                 22 |
|         4280 | B       |          3 |                 30 |
|         4280 | C       |         20 |                 30 |
|         6520 | D       |          9 |                 18 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   product_id | aisle   |   position |   total_qty_to_pick |
|-------------:|:--------|-----------:|--------------------:|
|         4280 | C       |          1 |                  36 |
|         4280 | D       |         18 |                  24 |
|         6520 | A       |         16 |                   6 |
|         6520 | A       |         29 |                  14 |
|         6520 | C       |         13 |                  20 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get all order lines for order 423 with their cumulative quantities
order_line_data AS (
    SELECT 
        ol.product_id,
        ol.qty AS ordered_qty,
        ol.id AS orderline_id,
        -- Calculate cumulative quantity for each product across order lines
        SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ol.product_id 
            ORDER BY ol.id
        ) AS cumulative_ordered_qty,
        -- Calculate previous cumulative for boundary calculation
        COALESCE(
            SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
                PARTITION BY ol.product_id 
                ORDER BY ol.id 
                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
            ), 0
        ) AS prev_cumulative_ordered
    FROM orderlines ol
    WHERE ol.order_id = 423
),

-- Step 2: Get available inventory in warehouse 1 with purchase dates
warehouse_inventory AS (
    SELECT 
        i.product_id,
        i.qty AS available_qty,
        i.location_id,
        i.id AS inventory_id,
        p.purchased,
        l.aisle,
        l.position,
        -- Prioritize by earlier purchased date and smaller quantities
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id 
            ORDER BY p.purchased ASC, i.qty ASC
        ) AS inventory_priority
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),

-- Step 3: Calculate cumulative available inventory for each product
cumulative_inventory AS (
    SELECT 
        wi.*,
        SUM(wi.available_qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY wi.product_id 
            ORDER BY wi.inventory_priority
        ) AS cumulative_available_qty,
        COALESCE(
            SUM(wi.available_qty) OVER (
                PARTITION BY wi.product_id 
                ORDER BY wi.inventory_priority 
                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
            ), 0
        ) AS prev_cumulative_available
    FROM warehouse_inventory wi
),

-- Step 4: Match order requirements with available inventory
inventory_allocation AS (
    SELECT 
        old.product_id,
        old.orderline_id,
        old.ordered_qty,
        old.cumulative_ordered_qty,
        old.prev_cumulative_ordered,
        ci.location_id,
        ci.aisle,
        ci.position,
        ci.available_qty,
        ci.cumulative_available_qty,
        ci.prev_cumulative_available,
        ci.purchased,
        -- Calculate how much to pick from this location for this order line
        -- Using CASE instead of LEAST (SQLite doesn't have LEAST function)
        CASE 
            -- When this inventory location can partially fulfill the cumulative order
            WHEN ci.cumulative_available_qty > old.prev_cumulative_ordered 
                 AND ci.prev_cumulative_available < old.cumulative_ordered_qty
            THEN 
                ROUND(
                    CASE 
                        WHEN ci.available_qty <= (old.cumulative_ordered_qty - 
                            CASE 
                                WHEN old.prev_cumulative_ordered >= ci.prev_cumulative_available 
                                THEN old.prev_cumulative_ordered 
                                ELSE ci.prev_cumulative_available 
                            END)
                        THEN ci.available_qty
                        ELSE (old.cumulative_ordered_qty - 
                            CASE 
                                WHEN old.prev_cumulative_ordered >= ci.prev_cumulative_available 
                                THEN old.prev_cumulative_ordered 
                                ELSE ci.prev_cumulative_available 
                            END)
                    END, 
                    4
                )
            ELSE 0
        END AS qty_to_pick
    FROM order_line_data old
    JOIN cumulative_inventory ci ON old.product_id = ci.product_id
    WHERE ci.cumulative_available_qty > old.prev_cumulative_ordered
),

-- Step 5: Filter and format final results
final_allocation AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        aisle,
        position,
        ROUND(SUM(qty_to_pick), 4) AS total_qty_to_pick
    FROM inventory_allocation
    WHERE qty_to_pick > 0
    GROUP BY product_id, location_id, aisle, position
    HAVING ROUND(SUM(qty_to_pick), 4) > 0
)

-- Final selection with ordering
SELECT 
    product_id,
    aisle,
    position,
    total_qty_to_pick
FROM final_allocation
ORDER BY product_id, aisle, position;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH seller_metrics AS (
    -- Calculate basic seller metrics: total quantity, total sales, average price
    SELECT 
        oi."seller_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_quantity",
        ROUND(SUM(oi."price"), 4) AS "total_sales",
        ROUND(AVG(oi."price"), 4) AS "avg_item_price"
    FROM "order_items" oi
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 100
),

seller_reviews AS (
    -- Calculate average review score per seller
    SELECT 
        oi."seller_id",
        ROUND(AVG(orr."review_score"), 4) AS "avg_review_score"
    FROM "order_items" oi
    JOIN "order_reviews" orr ON oi."order_id" = orr."order_id"
    WHERE orr."review_score" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
),

seller_packing AS (
    -- Calculate average packing time per seller (in days)
    SELECT 
        oi."seller_id",
        ROUND(AVG(
            julianday(o."order_delivered_carrier_date") - 
            julianday(o."order_approved_at")
        ), 4) AS "avg_packing_days"
    FROM "order_items" oi
    JOIN "orders" o ON oi."order_id" = o."order_id"
    WHERE o."order_approved_at" IS NOT NULL 
        AND o."order_delivered_carrier_date" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
),

seller_category_sales AS (
    -- Calculate sales volume per seller per category
    SELECT 
        oi."seller_id",
        pct."product_category_name_english",
        COUNT(*) AS "category_quantity"
    FROM "order_items" oi
    JOIN "products" p ON oi."product_id" = p."product_id"
    JOIN "product_category_name_translation" pct 
        ON p."product_category_name" = pct."product_category_name"
    WHERE pct."product_category_name_english" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id", pct."product_category_name_english"
),

ranked_categories AS (
    -- Rank categories by sales volume for each seller
    SELECT 
        "seller_id",
        "product_category_name_english",
        "category_quantity",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "seller_id" 
            ORDER BY "category_quantity" DESC
        ) AS "category_rank"
    FROM "seller_category_sales"
)

-- Final comprehensive report
SELECT 
    sm."seller_id",
    sm."total_quantity",
    sm."total_sales",
    sm."avg_item_price",
    COALESCE(sr."avg_review_score", 0) AS "avg_review_score",
    COALESCE(sp."avg_packing_days", 0) AS "avg_packing_days",
    rc."product_category_name_english" AS "top_category",
    rc."category_quantity" AS "top_category_quantity"
FROM "seller_metrics" sm
LEFT JOIN "seller_reviews" sr ON sm."seller_id" = sr."seller_id"
LEFT JOIN "seller_packing" sp ON sm."seller_id" = sp."seller_id"
LEFT JOIN "ranked_categories" rc ON sm."seller_id" = rc."seller_id" 
    AND rc."category_rank" = 1
ORDER BY sm."total_sales" DESC NULLS LAST;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE 1: Sellers with >100 items sold and their core sales metrics
WITH "seller_sales" AS (
    SELECT
        "oi"."seller_id",
        SUM("oi"."price") AS "total_sales",
        AVG("oi"."price") AS "avg_item_price",
        COUNT("oi"."order_item_id") AS "total_quantity"
    FROM "order_items" "oi"
    GROUP BY "oi"."seller_id"
    HAVING COUNT("oi"."order_item_id") > 100
),

-- CTE 2: Average review scores per seller (via order_items → orders → order_reviews)
"seller_reviews" AS (
    SELECT
        "oi"."seller_id",
        AVG(CAST("r"."review_score" AS REAL)) AS "avg_review_score"
    FROM "order_items" "oi"
    JOIN "orders" "o" ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."order_id"
    JOIN "order_reviews" "r" ON "o"."order_id" = "r"."order_id"
    WHERE "oi"."seller_id" IN (SELECT "seller_id" FROM "seller_sales")
    GROUP BY "oi"."seller_id"
),

-- CTE 3: Average packing time in days (from purchase to carrier delivery)
"seller_packing" AS (
    SELECT
        "oi"."seller_id",
        AVG(
            JULIANDAY("o"."order_delivered_carrier_date") -
            JULIANDAY("o"."order_purchase_timestamp")
        ) AS "avg_packing_days"
    FROM "order_items" "oi"
    JOIN "orders" "o" ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."order_id"
    WHERE "oi"."seller_id" IN (SELECT "seller_id" FROM "seller_sales")
      AND "o"."order_delivered_carrier_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND "o"."order_purchase_timestamp" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "oi"."seller_id"
),

-- CTE 4: For each seller, find the English product category with highest revenue
"seller_top_category" AS (
    SELECT
        "oi"."seller_id",
        "pct"."product_category_name_english",
        SUM("oi"."price") AS "category_revenue",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "oi"."seller_id"
            ORDER BY SUM("oi"."price") DESC
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM "order_items" "oi"
    JOIN "products" "p" ON "oi"."product_id" = "p"."product_id"
    JOIN "product_category_name_translation" "pct"
        ON "p"."product_category_name" = "pct"."product_category_name"
    WHERE "oi"."seller_id" IN (SELECT "seller_id" FROM "seller_sales")
    GROUP BY "oi"."seller_id", "pct"."product_category_name_english"
)

-- Final comprehensive performance report
SELECT
    "sm"."seller_id",
    ROUND("sm"."total_sales", 4) AS "total_sales",
    ROUND("sm"."avg_item_price", 4) AS "avg_item_price",
    ROUND("sr"."avg_review_score", 4) AS "avg_review_score",
    ROUND("sp"."avg_packing_days", 4) AS "avg_packing_days",
    "stc"."product_category_name_english" AS "top_category"
FROM "seller_sales" "sm"
LEFT JOIN "seller_reviews" "sr"
    ON "sm"."seller_id" = "sr"."seller_id"
LEFT JOIN "seller_packing" "sp"
    ON "sm"."seller_id" = "sp"."seller_id"
LEFT JOIN "seller_top_category" "stc"
    ON "sm"."seller_id" = "stc"."seller_id" AND "stc"."rn" = 1
ORDER BY "sm"."total_sales" DESC NULLS LAST;
```

```sql
WITH user_ages AS (
  SELECT 
    "user_id",
    -- Calculate age by year difference, adjusting for month/day
    CAST(
      (strftime('%Y', CURRENT_DATE) - strftime('%Y', "birth_date")) - 
      CASE 
        WHEN strftime('%m-%d', CURRENT_DATE) < strftime('%m-%d', "birth_date") 
        THEN 1 
        ELSE 0 
      END AS INTEGER
    ) AS age
  FROM "mst_users"
  WHERE "birth_date" IS NOT NULL 
    AND "birth_date" != 'None'
    AND date("birth_date") IS NOT NULL
    AND date("birth_date") <= CURRENT_DATE
)
SELECT 
  CASE
    WHEN age BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN '20s'
    WHEN age BETWEEN 30 AND 39 THEN '30s'
    WHEN age BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN '40s'
    WHEN age BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN '50s'
    ELSE 'others'
  END AS age_category,
  COUNT(*) AS user_count
FROM user_ages
GROUP BY age_category
ORDER BY 
  CASE age_category
    WHEN '20s' THEN 1
    WHEN '30s' THEN 2
    WHEN '40s' THEN 3
    WHEN '50s' THEN 4
    ELSE 5
  END;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

-- Step 1: Compute each user's age from birth_date relative to current date
WITH user_age AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        -- Precise age: subtract years, then subtract 1 if birthday hasn't occurred yet this year
        CAST(strftime('%Y', DATE('now')) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', "birth_date") AS INTEGER) -
        CASE
            WHEN strftime('%m-%d', DATE('now')) < strftime('%m-%d', "birth_date") THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS age
    FROM "mst_users"
)
-- Step 2: Categorize ages and count users
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN age BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN '20s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 30 AND 39 THEN '30s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN '40s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN '50s'
        ELSE 'others'
    END AS "age_category",
    COUNT(*) AS "user_count"
FROM user_age
GROUP BY "age_category"
ORDER BY "age_category";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH lap_data AS (
    SELECT 
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap,
        position
    FROM lap_positions
    WHERE lap_type = 'Race'
),
pit_stops_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap
    FROM pit_stops
),
retirements_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap AS retirement_lap
    FROM retirements
),
lap_transitions AS (
    SELECT 
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap,
        position AS current_position,
        LAG(position) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY lap) AS previous_position,
        LAG(lap) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY lap) AS previous_lap
    FROM lap_data
),
valid_transitions AS (
    SELECT 
        lt.race_id,
        lt.driver_id,
        lt.lap,
        lt.current_position,
        lt.previous_position
    FROM lap_transitions lt
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops_agg ps1 ON lt.race_id = ps1.race_id AND lt.driver_id = ps1.driver_id AND ps1.lap = lt.lap
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops_agg ps2 ON lt.race_id = ps2.race_id AND lt.driver_id = ps2.driver_id AND ps2.lap = lt.previous_lap
    LEFT JOIN retirements_agg r ON lt.race_id = r.race_id AND lt.driver_id = r.driver_id
    WHERE lt.lap > 1 
        AND lt.previous_position IS NOT NULL
        AND ps1.lap IS NULL
        AND ps2.lap IS NULL
        AND (r.retirement_lap IS NULL OR r.retirement_lap > lt.lap)
),
position_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap,
        current_position - previous_position AS delta
    FROM valid_transitions
),
overtake_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        driver_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN delta < 0 THEN -delta ELSE 0 END) AS overtook_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN delta > 0 THEN delta ELSE 0 END) AS overtaken_count
    FROM position_changes
    GROUP BY driver_id
)
SELECT 
    d.full_name
FROM overtake_counts oc
JOIN drivers_ext d ON oc.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE oc.overtaken_count > oc.overtook_count
ORDER BY d.full_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH lap_transitions AS (
    SELECT 
        lp.race_id,
        lp.driver_id,
        lp.lap AS current_lap,
        lp.position AS current_position,
        LAG(lp.lap) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id 
            ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) AS prev_lap,
        LAG(lp.position) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id 
            ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) AS prev_position
    FROM lap_positions lp
    WHERE lp.lap_type = 'Race'
),
transitions_with_exclusions AS (
    SELECT 
        lt.race_id,
        lt.driver_id,
        lt.current_lap,
        lt.prev_lap,
        lt.current_position,
        lt.prev_position,
        (lt.current_position - lt.prev_position) AS pos_change,
        CASE WHEN lt.prev_lap = 1 OR lt.current_lap = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_first_lap,
        CASE WHEN ps_entry.driver_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_pit_entry,
        CASE WHEN ps_exit.driver_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_pit_exit,
        CASE WHEN rt.driver_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_retirement
    FROM lap_transitions lt
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps_entry 
        ON ps_entry.race_id = lt.race_id 
        AND ps_entry.driver_id = lt.driver_id 
        AND ps_entry.lap = lt.current_lap
    LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps_exit 
        ON ps_exit.race_id = lt.race_id 
        AND ps_exit.driver_id = lt.driver_id 
        AND ps_exit.lap = lt.prev_lap
    LEFT JOIN retirements rt 
        ON rt.race_id = lt.race_id 
        AND rt.driver_id = lt.driver_id 
        AND rt.lap = lt.current_lap
    WHERE lt.prev_lap IS NOT NULL
),
valid_transitions AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM transitions_with_exclusions
    WHERE is_first_lap = 0
      AND is_pit_entry = 0
      AND is_pit_exit = 0
      AND is_retirement = 0
),
driver_overtake_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        vt.driver_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN vt.pos_change > 0 THEN vt.pos_change ELSE 0 END) AS overtaken_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN vt.pos_change < 0 THEN ABS(vt.pos_change) ELSE 0 END) AS overtook_count
    FROM valid_transitions vt
    GROUP BY vt.driver_id
)
SELECT 
    de.full_name
FROM driver_overtake_stats dos
JOIN drivers_ext de ON de.driver_id = dos.driver_id
WHERE dos.overtaken_count > dos.overtook_count
ORDER BY de.full_name;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH population_data AS (
    -- Get population estimates from DATACOMMONS_TIMESERIES for zip codes
    SELECT
        ts."GEO_ID" AS "ZIP_GEO_ID",
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts."DATE"::DATE) AS "YEAR",
        ts."VALUE" AS "POPULATION"
    FROM
        "GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT"."CYBERSYN"."DATACOMMONS_TIMESERIES" ts
    INNER JOIN
        "GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT"."CYBERSYN"."DATACOMMONS_ATTRIBUTES" attr
        ON ts."VARIABLE" = attr."VARIABLE"
    WHERE
        LOWER(attr."VARIABLE_NAME") LIKE '%population%'
        AND ts."GEO_ID" LIKE 'zip/%'
        AND ts."DATE"::DATE BETWEEN '2014-01-01'::DATE AND '2020-12-31'::DATE
        AND ts."VALUE" IS NOT NULL
),

growth_rates AS (
    -- Compute growth rates for 2015-2020, filter current population >= 25000
    SELECT
        "ZIP_GEO_ID",
        "YEAR",
        "POPULATION",
        LAG("POPULATION", 1) OVER (PARTITION BY "ZIP_GEO_ID" ORDER BY "YEAR") AS "PREV_POPULATION",
        CASE 
            WHEN LAG("POPULATION", 1) OVER (PARTITION BY "ZIP_GEO_ID" ORDER BY "YEAR") > 0 
            THEN (("POPULATION" - LAG("POPULATION", 1) OVER (PARTITION BY "ZIP_GEO_ID" ORDER BY "YEAR")) / 
                  LAG("POPULATION", 1) OVER (PARTITION BY "ZIP_GEO_ID" ORDER BY "YEAR")) * 100 
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS "GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT"
    FROM
        population_data
    WHERE
        "POPULATION" >= 25000
),

ranked_growth AS (
    -- Rank zip codes by growth rate within each year
    SELECT
        "ZIP_GEO_ID",
        "YEAR",
        "GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT",
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "YEAR" ORDER BY "GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT" DESC) AS "RANK"
    FROM
        growth_rates
    WHERE
        "GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT" IS NOT NULL
        AND "YEAR" BETWEEN 2015 AND 2020
),

zip_state_info AS (
    -- Get state information for zip codes using GEOGRAPHY_RELATIONSHIPS
    SELECT DISTINCT
        gr."GEO_ID" AS "ZIP_GEO_ID",
        gi."GEO_NAME" AS "STATE_NAME"
    FROM
        "GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT"."CYBERSYN"."GEOGRAPHY_RELATIONSHIPS" gr
    INNER JOIN
        "GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT"."CYBERSYN"."GEOGRAPHY_INDEX" gi
        ON gr."RELATED_GEO_ID" = gi."GEO_ID"
    WHERE
        gr."GEO_ID" LIKE 'zip/%'
        AND gi."LEVEL" = 'State'
),

state_abbr_mapping AS (
    -- Static mapping of state names to two-letter abbreviations
    SELECT 'Alabama' AS "STATE_NAME", 'AL' AS "STATE_ABBR" UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Alaska', 'AK' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Arizona', 'AZ' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Arkansas', 'AR' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'California', 'CA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Colorado', 'CO' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Connecticut', 'CT' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Delaware', 'DE' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'District of Columbia', 'DC' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Florida', 'FL' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Georgia', 'GA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Hawaii', 'HI' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Idaho', 'ID' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Illinois', 'IL' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Indiana', 'IN' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Iowa', 'IA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kansas', 'KS' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Kentucky', 'KY' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Louisiana', 'LA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Maine', 'ME' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Maryland', 'MD' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Massachusetts', 'MA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Michigan', 'MI' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Minnesota', 'MN' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Mississippi', 'MS' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Missouri', 'MO' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Montana', 'MT' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Nebraska', 'NE' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Nevada', 'NV' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'New Hampshire', 'NH' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'New Jersey', 'NJ' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'New Mexico', 'NM' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'New York', 'NY' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'North Carolina', 'NC' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'North Dakota', 'ND' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Ohio', 'OH' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Oklahoma', 'OK' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Oregon', 'OR' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Pennsylvania', 'PA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Rhode Island', 'RI' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'South Carolina', 'SC' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'South Dakota', 'SD' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Tennessee', 'TN' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Texas', 'TX' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Utah', 'UT' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Vermont', 'VT' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Virginia', 'VA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Washington', 'WA' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'West Virginia', 'WV' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Wisconsin', 'WI' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Wyoming', 'WY' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Puerto Rico', 'PR'
)

-- Final query: join all components, extract zip code and state abbreviation
SELECT
    rg."YEAR",
    SPLIT_PART(rg."ZIP_GEO_ID", '/', 2) AS "ZIP_CODE",
    COALESCE(sam."STATE_ABBR", 
             CASE 
                 WHEN zsi."STATE_NAME" LIKE '%, %' 
                 THEN SPLIT_PART(zsi."STATE_NAME", ', ', -1)
                 ELSE zsi."STATE_NAME"
             END) AS "STATE_ABBR",
    ROUND(rg."GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT", 4) AS "ANNUAL_GROWTH_RATE_PERCENT"
FROM
    ranked_growth rg
LEFT JOIN
    zip_state_info zsi
    ON rg."ZIP_GEO_ID" = zsi."ZIP_GEO_ID"
LEFT JOIN
    state_abbr_mapping sam
    ON zsi."STATE_NAME" = sam."STATE_NAME"
WHERE
    rg."RANK" = 2
ORDER BY
    rg."YEAR";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- I'll write the complete query now

WITH 
-- Identify the population estimate variable for 5-Year ACS
population_variable AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "VARIABLE"
    FROM GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT.CYBERSYN.AMERICAN_COMMUNITY_SURVEY_ATTRIBUTES
    WHERE "MEASURE" = 'Population'
      AND "MEASUREMENT_PERIOD" = '5YR'
      AND "MEASUREMENT_TYPE" = 'estimate'
      AND "FREQUENCY" = 'Annual'
),

-- Get population values for ZCTAs
pop_values AS (
    SELECT 
        t."GEO_ID",
        t."DATE",
        TRY_CAST(t."VALUE" AS NUMBER) AS "POPULATION"
    FROM GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT.CYBERSYN.AMERICAN_COMMUNITY_SURVEY_TIMESERIES t
    JOIN population_variable pv ON t."VARIABLE" = pv."VARIABLE"
    WHERE t."GEO_ID" LIKE 'zip/%'
      AND TRY_CAST(t."VALUE" AS NUMBER) IS NOT NULL
      AND YEAR(t."DATE") BETWEEN 2015 AND 2020
),

-- Get state info for each ZCTA
zcta_states AS (
    SELECT 
        gr."GEO_ID" AS "ZCTA_GEO_ID",
        gr."RELATED_GEO_ID" AS "STATE_GEO_ID"
    FROM GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT.CYBERSYN.GEOGRAPHY_RELATIONSHIPS gr
    WHERE gr."LEVEL" = 'CensusZipCodeTabulationArea'
      AND gr."RELATED_LEVEL" = 'State'
      AND gr."RELATIONSHIP_TYPE" = 'Contains'
),

state_abbrev AS (
    SELECT 
        gi."GEO_ID",
        SPLIT_PART(gi."GEO_NAME", '|', 1) AS "STATE_ABBREVIATION"
    FROM GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT.CYBERSYN.GEOGRAPHY_INDEX gi
    WHERE gi."LEVEL" = 'State'
),

-- Combine with zip code names
zcta_info AS (
    SELECT 
        gi."GEO_ID" AS "ZCTA_GEO_ID",
        REPLACE(gi."GEO_ID", 'zip/', '') AS "ZIP_CODE",
        sa."STATE_ABBREVIATION"
    FROM GLOBAL_GOVERNMENT.CYBERSYN.GEOGRAPHY_INDEX gi
    JOIN zcta_states zs ON gi."GEO_ID" = zs."ZCTA_GEO_ID"
    JOIN state_abbrev sa ON zs."STATE_GEO_ID" = sa."GEO_ID"
    WHERE gi."LEVEL" = 'CensusZipCodeTabulationArea'
),

-- Annual population with growth rate calculation
annual_pop AS (
    SELECT 
        pv."GEO_ID",
        YEAR(pv."DATE") AS "YEAR",
        pv."POPULATION",
        LAG(pv."POPULATION") OVER (PARTITION BY pv."GEO_ID" ORDER BY pv."DATE") AS "PREV_POP"
    FROM pop_values pv
),

growth_rates AS (
    SELECT 
        ap."GEO_ID",
        ap."YEAR",
        ap."POPULATION",
        CASE 
            WHEN ap."PREV_POP" IS NOT NULL AND ap."PREV_POP" > 0 
            THEN ROUND((ap."POPULATION" - ap."PREV_POP") / ap."PREV_POP" * 100, 4)
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS "GROWTH_RATE_PCT"
    FROM annual_pop ap
    WHERE ap."POPULATION" >= 25000
      AND ap."YEAR" BETWEEN 2015 AND 2020
),

ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        gr."YEAR",
        zi."ZIP_CODE",
        zi."STATE_ABBREVIATION",
        gr."GROWTH_RATE_PCT",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gr."YEAR" ORDER BY gr."GROWTH_RATE_PCT" DESC) AS "RANK"
    FROM growth_rates gr
    JOIN zcta_info zi ON gr."GEO_ID" = zi."ZCTA_GEO_ID"
    WHERE gr."GROWTH_RATE_PCT" IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT 
    "YEAR",
    "ZIP_CODE",
    "STATE_ABBREVIATION",
    "GROWTH_RATE_PCT"
FROM ranked
WHERE "RANK" = 2
ORDER BY "YEAR";
```
</details>

),
jan_values AS (
    SELECT 
        jp."TICKER",
        jp."jan_date",
        s."VALUE" AS "jan_price"
    FROM jan_prices jp
    INNER JOIN "FINANCE__ECONOMICS"."CYBERSYN"."STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES" s
        ON jp."TICKER" = s."TICKER" 
        AND jp."jan_date" = s."DATE"
        AND s."VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
),
jun_values AS (
    SELECT 
        jp."TICKER",
        jp."jun_date",
        s."VALUE" AS "jun_price"
    FROM jun_prices jp
    INNER JOIN "FINANCE__ECONOMICS"."CYBERSYN"."STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES" s
        ON jp."TICKER" = s."TICKER" 
        AND jp."jun_date" = s."DATE"
        AND s."VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
)
SELECT 
    jv."TICKER",
    jv."jan_date",
    jv."jan_price",
    jv2."jun_date",
    jv2."jun_price",
    ROUND(
        CASE 
            WHEN jv."jan_price" = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE (jv2."jun_price" - jv."jan_price") / jv."jan_price" * 100
        END, 
        4
    ) AS "pct_change"
FROM jan_values jv
INNER JOIN jun_values jv2 ON jv."TICKER" = jv2."TICKER"
ORDER BY "pct_change" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify Magnificent 7 companies and their primary tickers
WITH magnificent_7 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "PRIMARY_TICKER" AS ticker, "COMPANY_NAME"
    FROM FINANCE__ECONOMICS.CYBERSYN.COMPANY_INDEX
    WHERE LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%apple%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%microsoft%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%amazon%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%alphabet%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%nvidia%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%tesla%'
       OR LOWER("COMPANY_NAME") LIKE '%meta platforms%'
),

-- Step 2: Get post-market close prices for the relevant tickers and date range
price_data AS (
    SELECT s."TICKER", s."VALUE", s."DATE"
    FROM FINANCE__ECONOMICS.CYBERSYN.STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES s
    JOIN magnificent_7 m ON s."TICKER" = m.ticker
    WHERE s."VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
      AND s."DATE" BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-06-30'
),

-- Step 3: Find the first and last trading day in the range for each ticker
first_last AS (
    SELECT "TICKER",
           MIN("DATE") AS start_date,
           MAX("DATE") AS end_date
    FROM price_data
    GROUP BY "TICKER"
),

-- Step 4: Extract the price at the start date
start_price AS (
    SELECT p."TICKER", p."VALUE" AS start_value
    FROM price_data p
    JOIN first_last f ON p."TICKER" = f."TICKER" AND p."DATE" = f.start_date
),

-- Step 5: Extract the price at the end date
end_price AS (
    SELECT p."TICKER", p."VALUE" AS end_value
    FROM price_data p
    JOIN first_last f ON p."TICKER" = f."TICKER" AND p."DATE" = f.end_date
)

-- Step 6: Calculate percentage change and join with company names
SELECT
    m."COMPANY_NAME",
    ROUND((e.end_value - s.start_value) / s.start_value * 100, 4) AS percentage_change
FROM magnificent_7 m
JOIN start_price s ON m.ticker = s."TICKER"
JOIN end_price e ON m.ticker = e."TICKER"
ORDER BY m."COMPANY_NAME";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH home_depot_stores AS (
    -- Get all Home Depot stores with their coordinates
    SELECT 
        poi."POI_ID" AS "home_depot_id",
        poi."POI_NAME" AS "home_depot_name",
        addr."LONGITUDE" AS "home_depot_lon",
        addr."LATITUDE" AS "home_depot_lat"
    FROM "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."POINT_OF_INTEREST_INDEX" poi
    INNER JOIN "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."POINT_OF_INTEREST_ADDRESSES_RELATIONSHIPS" rel
        ON poi."POI_ID" = rel."POI_ID"
    INNER JOIN "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."US_ADDRESSES" addr
        ON rel."ADDRESS_ID" = addr."ADDRESS_ID"
    WHERE poi."POI_NAME" = 'The Home Depot'
        AND addr."LONGITUDE" IS NOT NULL
        AND addr."LATITUDE" IS NOT NULL
),
lowes_stores AS (
    -- Get all Lowe's stores with their coordinates
    SELECT 
        poi."POI_ID" AS "lowes_id",
        poi."POI_NAME" AS "lowes_name",
        addr."LONGITUDE" AS "lowes_lon",
        addr."LATITUDE" AS "lowes_lat"
    FROM "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."POINT_OF_INTEREST_INDEX" poi
    INNER JOIN "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."POINT_OF_INTEREST_ADDRESSES_RELATIONSHIPS" rel
        ON poi."POI_ID" = rel."POI_ID"
    INNER JOIN "US_REAL_ESTATE"."CYBERSYN"."US_ADDRESSES" addr
        ON rel."ADDRESS_ID" = addr."ADDRESS_ID"
    WHERE poi."POI_NAME" = 'Lowe''s Home Improvement'
        AND addr."LONGITUDE" IS NOT NULL
        AND addr."LATITUDE" IS NOT NULL
),
all_distances AS (
    -- Calculate distances between all Home Depot and Lowe's pairs
    SELECT 
        hd."home_depot_id",
        hd."home_depot_name",
        hd."home_depot_lon",
        hd."home_depot_lat",
        lw."lowes_id",
        lw."lowes_name",
        lw."lowes_lon",
        lw."lowes_lat",
        -- Calculate distance in meters and convert to miles
        ST_DISTANCE(
            ST_MAKEPOINT(hd."home_depot_lon", hd."home_depot_lat"),
            ST_MAKEPOINT(lw."lowes_lon", lw."lowes_lat")
        ) / 1609 AS "distance_miles"
    FROM home_depot_stores hd
    CROSS JOIN lowes_stores lw
)
-- For each Home Depot, keep only the nearest Lowe's
SELECT 
    "home_depot_id",
    "home_depot_name",
    "home_depot_lon",
    "home_depot_lat",
    "lowes_id",
    "lowes_name",
    "lowes_lon",
    "lowes_lat",
    ROUND("distance_miles", 4) AS "nearest_distance_miles"
FROM all_distances
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY "home_depot_id" 
    ORDER BY "distance_miles"
) = 1
ORDER BY "home_depot_id";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH home_depot AS (
    -- Get all The Home Depot stores with their geographic coordinates
    SELECT 
        poi."POI_ID",
        addr."LONGITUDE",
        addr."LATITUDE"
    FROM US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.POINT_OF_INTEREST_INDEX poi
    INNER JOIN US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.POINT_OF_INTEREST_ADDRESSES_RELATIONSHIPS rel
        ON poi."POI_ID" = rel."POI_ID"
    INNER JOIN US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.US_ADDRESSES addr
        ON rel."ADDRESS_ID" = addr."ADDRESS_ID"
    WHERE LOWER(poi."POI_NAME") LIKE LOWER('%Home%Depot%')
),
lowes AS (
    -- Get all Lowe's Home Improvement stores with their geographic coordinates
    SELECT 
        poi."POI_ID",
        addr."LONGITUDE",
        addr."LATITUDE"
    FROM US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.POINT_OF_INTEREST_INDEX poi
    INNER JOIN US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.POINT_OF_INTEREST_ADDRESSES_RELATIONSHIPS rel
        ON poi."POI_ID" = rel."POI_ID"
    INNER JOIN US_REAL_ESTATE.CYBERSYN.US_ADDRESSES addr
        ON rel."ADDRESS_ID" = addr."ADDRESS_ID"
    WHERE LOWER(poi."POI_NAME") LIKE LOWER('%Lowe%')
),
distance_calc AS (
    -- Cross join each Home Depot with every Lowe's and compute straight-line distance in miles
    SELECT 
        hd."POI_ID" AS home_depot_poi_id,
        lw."POI_ID" AS lowes_poi_id,
        ROUND(
            ST_DISTANCE(
                ST_MAKEPOINT(hd."LONGITUDE", hd."LATITUDE"),
                ST_MAKEPOINT(lw."LONGITUDE", lw."LATITUDE")
            ) / 1609,
            4
        ) AS distance_miles
    FROM home_depot hd
    CROSS JOIN lowes lw
)
-- For each Home Depot store, keep only the nearest Lowe's location
SELECT 
    home_depot_poi_id,
    lowes_poi_id,
    distance_miles
FROM distance_calc
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY home_depot_poi_id 
    ORDER BY distance_miles ASC
) = 1
ORDER BY home_depot_poi_id;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH years AS (
    -- Generate years 2010 through 2019
    SELECT 2010 + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY NULL) - 1 AS "year"
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))
),
aggregated_claims AS (
    -- Aggregate building and contents damage amounts by year for City Of New York
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "DATE_OF_LOSS") AS "year_of_loss",
        SUM(COALESCE("BUILDING_DAMAGE_AMOUNT", 0)) AS "total_building_damage_amount",
        SUM(COALESCE("CONTENTS_DAMAGE_AMOUNT", 0)) AS "total_contents_damage_amount"
    FROM "WEATHER__ENVIRONMENT"."CYBERSYN"."FEMA_NATIONAL_FLOOD_INSURANCE_PROGRAM_CLAIM_INDEX"
    WHERE
        UPPER(TRIM("NFIP_COMMUNITY_NAME")) = 'CITY OF NEW YORK'
        AND "DATE_OF_LOSS" IS NOT NULL
        AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "DATE_OF_LOSS") BETWEEN 2010 AND 2019
    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "DATE_OF_LOSS")
)
SELECT
    y."year",
    COALESCE(ac."total_building_damage_amount", 0) AS "total_building_damage_amount",
    COALESCE(ac."total_contents_damage_amount", 0) AS "total_contents_damage_amount"
FROM years y
LEFT JOIN aggregated_claims ac ON y."year" = ac."year_of_loss"
ORDER BY y."year";
```

    YEAR("DATE_OF_LOSS") AS "year_of_loss",
    ROUND(SUM("BUILDING_DAMAGE_AMOUNT"), 4) AS "total_building_damage_amount",
    ROUND(SUM("CONTENTS_DAMAGE_AMOUNT"), 4) AS "total_contents_damage_amount"
FROM WEATHER__ENVIRONMENT.CYBERSYN.FEMA_NATIONAL_FLOOD_INSURANCE_PROGRAM_CLAIM_INDEX
WHERE "NFIP_COMMUNITY_NAME" = 'City Of New York'
  AND YEAR("DATE_OF_LOSS") BETWEEN 2010 AND 2019
GROUP BY YEAR("DATE_OF_LOSS")
ORDER BY "year_of_loss";
```

WITH send_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID" AS "app_group_id",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID" AS "campaign_id",
        "USER_ID" AS "user_id",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" AS "message_variation_id",
        "PLATFORM" AS "platform",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" AS "ad_tracking_enabled",
        NULL AS "carrier",
        NULL AS "browser",
        NULL AS "device_model",
        COUNT(*) AS "push_notification_sends",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "unique_push_notification_sends"
    FROM "BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET"."PUBLIC"."USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_SEND_VIEW"
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('hour', TO_TIMESTAMP("TIME")) = TIMESTAMP '2023-06-01 08:00:00'
    GROUP BY 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
),
bounce_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID" AS "app_group_id",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID" AS "campaign_id",
        "USER_ID" AS "user_id",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" AS "message_variation_id",
        "PLATFORM" AS "platform",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" AS "ad_tracking_enabled",
        NULL AS "carrier",
        NULL AS "browser",
        NULL AS "device_model",
        COUNT(*) AS "push_notification_bounced",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "unique_push_notification_bounced"
    FROM "BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET"."PUBLIC"."USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_BOUNCE_VIEW"
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('hour', TO_TIMESTAMP("TIME")) = TIMESTAMP '2023-06-01 08:00:00'
    GROUP BY 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
),
open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID" AS "app_group_id",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID" AS "campaign_id",
        "USER_ID" AS "user_id",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" AS "message_variation_id",
        "PLATFORM" AS "platform",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" AS "ad_tracking_enabled",
        "CARRIER" AS "carrier",
        "BROWSER" AS "browser",
        NULL AS "device_model",
        COUNT(*) AS "push_notification_open",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "unique_push_notification_opened"
    FROM "BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET"."PUBLIC"."USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_OPEN_VIEW"
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('hour', TO_TIMESTAMP("TIME")) = TIMESTAMP '2023-06-01 08:00:00'
    GROUP BY 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER"
),
influenced_open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID" AS "app_group_id",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID" AS "campaign_id",
        "USER_ID" AS "user_id",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" AS "message_variation_id",
        "PLATFORM" AS "platform",
        NULL AS "ad_tracking_enabled",                -- column not in this table
        "CARRIER" AS "carrier",
        "BROWSER" AS "browser",
        NULL AS "device_model",
        COUNT(*) AS "push_notification_influenced_open",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "unique_push_notification_influenced_open"
    FROM "BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET"."PUBLIC"."USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_INFLUENCEDOPEN_VIEW"
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('hour', TO_TIMESTAMP("TIME")) = TIMESTAMP '2023-06-01 08:00:00'
    GROUP BY 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER"
),
combined_events AS (
    SELECT 
        COALESCE(s."app_group_id", b."app_group_id", o."app_group_id", i."app_group_id") AS "app_group_id",
        COALESCE(s."campaign_id", b."campaign_id", o."campaign_id", i."campaign_id") AS "campaign_id",
        COALESCE(s."user_id", b."user_id", o."user_id", i."user_id") AS "user_id",
        COALESCE(s."message_variation_id", b."message_variation_id", o."message_variation_id", i."message_variation_id") AS "message_variation_id",
        COALESCE(s."platform", b."platform", o."platform", i."platform") AS "platform",
        COALESCE(s."ad_tracking_enabled", b."ad_tracking_enabled", o."ad_tracking_enabled", i."ad_tracking_enabled") AS "ad_tracking_enabled",
        COALESCE(o."carrier", i."carrier") AS "carrier",
        COALESCE(o."browser", i."browser") AS "browser",
        COALESCE(o."device_model", i."device_model") AS "device_model",
        COALESCE(s."push_notification_sends", 0) AS "push_notification_sends",
        COALESCE(s."unique_push_notification_sends", 0) AS "unique_push_notification_sends",
        COALESCE(b."push_notification_bounced", 0) AS "push_notification_bounced",
        COALESCE(b."unique_push_notification_bounced", 0) AS "unique_push_notification_bounced",
        COALESCE(o."push_notification_open", 0) AS "push_notification_open",
        COALESCE(o."unique_push_notification_opened", 0) AS "unique_push_notification_opened",
        COALESCE(i."push_notification_influenced_open", 0) AS "push_notification_influenced_open",
        COALESCE(i."unique_push_notification_influenced_open", 0) AS "unique_push_notification_influenced_open"
    FROM send_events s
    FULL OUTER JOIN bounce_events b 
        ON s."app_group_id" = b."app_group_id"
        AND s."campaign_id" = b."campaign_id"
        AND s."user_id" = b."user_id"
        AND s."message_variation_id" = b."message_variation_id"
        AND s."platform" = b."platform"
        AND s."ad_tracking_enabled" = b."ad_tracking_enabled"
    FULL OUTER JOIN open_events o 
        ON COALESCE(s."app_group_id", b."app_group_id") = o."app_group_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."campaign_id", b."campaign_id") = o."campaign_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."user_id", b."user_id") = o."user_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."message_variation_id", b."message_variation_id") = o."message_variation_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."platform", b."platform") = o."platform"
        AND COALESCE(s."ad_tracking_enabled", b."ad_tracking_enabled") = o."ad_tracking_enabled"
    FULL OUTER JOIN influenced_open_events i 
        ON COALESCE(s."app_group_id", b."app_group_id", o."app_group_id") = i."app_group_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."campaign_id", b."campaign_id", o."campaign_id") = i."campaign_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."user_id", b."user_id", o."user_id") = i."user_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."message_variation_id", b."message_variation_id", o."message_variation_id") = i."message_variation_id"
        AND COALESCE(s."platform", b."platform", o."platform") = i."platform"
        AND COALESCE(s."ad_tracking_enabled", b."ad_tracking_enabled", o."ad_tracking_enabled") = i."ad_tracking_enabled"
)
SELECT 
    "app_group_id",
    "campaign_id",
    "user_id",
    "message_variation_id",
    "platform",
    "ad_tracking_enabled",
    "carrier",
    "browser",
    "device_model",
    SUM("push_notification_sends") AS "push_notification_sends",
    SUM("unique_push_notification_sends") AS "unique_push_notification_sends",
    SUM("push_notification_bounced") AS "push_notification_bounced",
    SUM("unique_push_notification_bounced") AS "unique_push_notification_bounced",
    SUM("push_notification_open") AS "push_notification_open",
    SUM("unique_push_notification_opened") AS "unique_push_notification_opened",
    SUM("push_notification_influenced_open") AS "push_notification_influenced_open",
    SUM("unique_push_notification_influenced_open") AS "unique_push_notification_influenced_open"
FROM combined_events
GROUP BY 
    "app_group_id",
    "campaign_id",
    "user_id",
    "message_variation_id",
    "platform",
    "ad_tracking_enabled",
    "carrier",
    "browser",
    "device_model"
ORDER BY 
    "app_group_id",
    "campaign_id",
    "user_id",
    "message_variation_id";
```

    COALESCE(i."push_notification_influenced_open", 0) AS "push_notification_influenced_open",
    COALESCE(i."unique_push_notification_influenced_open", 0) AS "unique_push_notification_influenced_open"
FROM all_keys k
LEFT JOIN send_agg s
    ON k."APP_GROUP_ID" = s."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = s."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = s."USER_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = s."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = s."PLATFORM"
    AND k."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" = s."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NULL AND s."CARRIER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NULL AND s."BROWSER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL AND s."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN bounce_agg b
    ON k."APP_GROUP_ID" = b."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = b."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = b."USER_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = b."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = b."PLATFORM"
    AND k."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" = b."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NULL AND b."CARRIER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NULL AND b."BROWSER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL AND b."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN open_agg o
    ON k."APP_GROUP_ID" = o."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = o."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = o."USER_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = o."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = o."PLATFORM"
    AND k."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" = o."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
    AND k."CARRIER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."CARRIER"
    AND k."BROWSER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."BROWSER"
    AND k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."DEVICE_MODEL"
LEFT JOIN influenced_open_agg i
    ON k."APP_GROUP_ID" = i."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = i."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = i."USER_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = i."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = i."PLATFORM"
    AND k."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED" = i."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED"
    AND k."CARRIER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM i."CARRIER"
    AND k."BROWSER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM i."BROWSER"
    AND k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM i."DEVICE_MODEL"
ORDER BY k."APP_GROUP_ID", k."CAMPAIGN_ID", k."USER_ID", k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
         k."PLATFORM", k."AD_TRACKING_ENABLED", k."CARRIER", k."BROWSER", k."DEVICE_MODEL";
```
</details>

### 173. sf029 (DB: `AMAZON_VENDOR_ANALYTICS__SAMPLE_DATASET`)
**Question**: Generate a daily detailed sales report for each product under the 'Manufacturing' distributor view, covering the 30 days leading up to February 6, 2022, by joining the sales, traffic, inventory, and net PPM data on date, ASIN, program, period, and distributor_view.
